issue:835.body:
## Context

This tracks a staged landing for the work currently visible in #315 (GitCode !125), plus the two smaller follow-up branches for KE/trace integration and finish-gate refinements.

The current combined PR is 275 files and about +54k lines. Review feedback has correctly identified both the review/merge risk and the need for an explicit product decision about KE as a first-class ScienceDiscovery surface. I will preserve #315 as the full implementation reference, but stop refreshing it with large upstream merges and instead prepare clean, independently reviewable PRs from current `main`.

## Proposed landing sequence

### A. Independent research/runtime foundations

These do not require the KE service and can be reviewed on their own merits.

- [ ] **A1 — Tool-output trust boundary:** per-run nonce fencing, `untrustedCategory`, MCP remote classification, and the corresponding prompt contract. Raw stored output remains unchanged; fencing applies to model-visible content.
- [ ] **A2 — Research state:** session research state, project ledger hydration/promotion, and tournament ranking primitives.
- [ ] **A3 — Runtime controls:** native stall guard and the `TurnLifecycle.beforeFinish`/continuation event primitives. This will not claim equivalent native-style stall protection for JiuwenSwarm.
- [ ] **A4 — Session Plan:** versioned human approval, decision log, cancellation and recovery, with an explicit compatibility rule for the existing `update_plan` snapshot mechanism.
- [ ] **A5 — Finish-gate core:** skill audit and termination intervention for native and post-run/Swarm execution. The initial landing will include the already-developed fixes for loaded-skill-only audits, Swarm tool aliases, and self-referential gate/verifier text. KE grounding comes later.
- [ ] **A6 — Agent Memory:** candidate memories, human promotion, reviewed-only prompt injection, and background review. The KE LLM-helper dependency and process-global manager need to be removed first.

### B. Knowledge Engine core

- [ ] **B1 — Text/extraction/resolution domain:** pure text, JATS, extraction, and entity-resolution modules with unit tests.
- [ ] **B2 — Graph/growth/eval algorithms:** graph algorithms, gap discovery, growth selection, and evaluation primitives.
- [ ] **B3 — Persistence and ingestion data plane:** SQLite store/migrations, scholarly connectors, PDF/vision parsing, and background runners.
- [ ] **B4 — Orchestration and minimal REST:** orchestrator, grow, routes, and narrowly scoped bootstrap/http wiring. Agent tools, resident summary, graph mirror, and living review stay out of this first REST PR.
- [ ] **B5 — Minimal KE Web shell:** API client, KE page, graph canvas, and document reader.

### C. Agent integration and advanced KE surfaces

- [ ] **C1 — Consumption tools and kbScope:** KE search/expand/grep tools, session binding, web-search restrictions, resident summary, and picker. Scope enforcement lands with the first exposed tool.
- [ ] **C2 — Citation and anti-hallucination runtime:** citation verification, novelty checks, evidence ledger, report polish, and finish-gate grounding. Includes the no-available-KB advisory behavior rather than an unachievable hard lock.
- [ ] **C3 — Reports, DRIFT, and memory-graph bridge:** community reports, DRIFT search, KE-to-memory-graph mirroring, and KB deep links.

### Small follow-ups from the former KE/trace and finish-gate PRs

These can land as soon as their specific dependencies are present; they do not all need to wait for the entire base series.

- [ ] Paper presence lookup and KB badge (after minimal REST + Web).
- [ ] Explicit Paper-to-KB re-ingest (after presence lookup).
- [ ] Reviewer citation checks with a bound-KB short circuit (after citation verification + kbScope).
- [ ] KB reader back-link to the current session memory graph (after graph mirroring).
- [ ] `gap_candidates` to deduplicated `research_state` open questions (after research state + observer wiring).
- [ ] Quoting-discipline skill updates and catalog/version pins with their corresponding gate/skill stages.

## Per-stage requirements

- Each PR is cut from current `main`; mixed files such as `store.ts`, `runs/index.ts`, `http/index.ts`, and `App.tsx` are ported by focused hunks rather than copied wholesale.
- Unit/integration tests and the relevant journeys land with their feature, not in a final test-only PR.
- Current-main behavior is preserved, including catalog transaction/rollback semantics, deletion-settling shutdown, response identity, and Swarm skill-selection behavior.
- Tool trust is field-aware: deterministic verdicts must not implicitly make corpus titles, abstracts, snippets, or entity descriptions trusted.
- The fenced evidence-ledger path, post-run terminal-event ordering, and no-engine kbScope behavior receive explicit integration coverage.
- Runtime-affecting stages receive a clean deployment and real E2E validation before the next stage.

Unless maintainers prefer a dedicated integration branch, the default is small PRs directly to `main`, with at most one or two open at a time. Feedback on the staged product scope and on starting with **A1 + B1** would be appreciated.

issue:840.body:
## What happens

The delimited-preview payload carries a `warnings: string[]` field that no consumer reads, and which duplicates text the client already composes and localizes.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): the `warnings` array is built at the end of `parseDelimitedTable` ("The file has {total} columns; the preview shows the first {shown}." and "{n} cells past the preview width are not shown.") and returned in the payload type (`:161`-ish in that revision).
- `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` mirrors the field in the web payload type.
- The viewer does not use it: `ArtifactModal` passes `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` down and `DatasetTable` composes its own sentences from `artifact.tableClippedColumns` / `artifact.tableClippedCells` (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`).

## Why it matters

Two places decide what the user is told about a clipped preview: the server strings are English-only, so a Chinese UI would drift from them the moment anyone read them, and a future consumer could show untranslated text. Today the field is dead weight in every preview payload.

## Suggested fix

Either drop `warnings` from the payload and keep `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` as the only source of truth (the client already localizes from them), or make the client render the server strings through the i18n layer. Pick one owner for the copy.

issue:894.body:
## 背景

当前 ScienceDiscovery 的 Desktop 与 Web 客户端在工作区视图、对话交互、会话与产物管理、设置以及全局辅助能力方面存在一定差异。为便于评估桌面端功能补齐范围，现基于前端实现对差异进行集中梳理，并为后续需求拆分和验收提供参考。

**关联：#718**（`v0.4.0-rc1` 版本需求与发布计划）。其中“桌面端支持科学记忆、Evolve”和“评估旧 UI 功能迁移”等事项与本 Issue 直接相关。

> **说明**
> - 本文是基于当前代码和界面实现的**初步差异盘点**，并非全部条目的最终功能验收结论；具体表现仍需结合实际版本验证。
> - Desktop 并非 Web 的简单复制：它已有独立的 `SetupWizard` / `Guide` 初始化引导、`shell-bridge` 和面板组织方式。因此目标是评估并补齐关键能力，而非机械地复刻 Web UI。
> - 本 Issue 用于**集中跟踪差异与讨论优先级**；不表示所列功能均已纳入 `v0.4.0-rc1` 交付范围。建议在 #718 的评审中明确具体范围。

## 一、右侧工作区与探索视图

Web 右侧面板包含多种专项视图；Desktop 的 `WorkspacePanel` 当前主要开放 `artifacts` 和 `files` 两个 group。

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Evolve 进化搜索** | `evolve/*`：算法选择、搜索网格/图、候选详情、评分图表、运行卡片及轮询 | **缺失**对应专项视图 |
| **Memory Graph 记忆图** | `MemoryGraphView.tsx`、`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`、`MemoryGraphCanvas.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **Idea Tree 思路树** | `IdeaTreeView.tsx`、`IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`、`IdeaTreeExplorer.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **CSV 可视化工作台** | `csv-artifact/*`：散点图、直方图、箱线图等 | **部分实现**：主要提供基础表格展示 |
| **执行视图** | 展示 Subagent 执行情况 | **缺少对应视图** |
| **审查专家视图** | 审查专家相关 UI | **缺少对应视图**，具体交互需进一步核对 |

## 二、对话交互与执行过程展示

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **对话输入区** | 选择专家、数据连接器、权限审查模式及自动审查配置；Agent 执行期间可继续发送指令 | **部分实现**：缺少连接器与自动审查等入口，执行期间不能继续发送指令；Desktop 另外支持添加文件 |
| **思考 / 行动步骤展示** | 工具失败时可复制关键诊断信息并快捷跳转 GitHub Issue；最终答案尾部展示产物；Subagent 运行状态有更丰富的 UI | **部分缺失**，建议逐项核对并补齐交互 |
| **轨迹模式** | 提供区别于常规对话的 Agent 行动轨迹视图 | **缺失** |

## 三、会话、项目与产物管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **会话管理** | 重命名、删除、会话级设置、归档、筛选 | 缺少会话级设置、归档及筛选 |
| **项目管理** | 重命名、删除、项目级设置 | 缺少项目级设置 |
| **产物 / 文件下载** | 支持选择多个目标进行下载 | 主要支持单文件下载，批量选择能力不足 |
| **工作区文件来源** | `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` | 缺少文件来源查看 UI |
| **产物树 / 工作区文件树** | `artifactTree.ts` 支持产物树组织 | Desktop 有独立的 `file-tree.ts`，但主要覆盖文件列表，未提供对应的产物树结构 |

## 四、设置与能力管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **全局默认配置** | 运行时默认值、可选扩展、连接器、Web 访问等 | 缺少对应的完整配置入口 |
| **Runner 管理** | 本地 Runner 状态、远程 Runner 添加 / 管理 | 有 `RemoteHosts` 配置，但缺少完整 Remote Jobs 面板及本地 Runner 状态展示 |
| **模型与扩展能力** | Model、MCP、Web、Memory、Idea Tree、Skill、Specialist 等 | **部分实现**：MCP 主要为内置能力，缺少自定义添加；Skill 有基础添加方式，但缺少 Web 端更完整的管理、探索及导入流程；Web、Memory、Idea Tree 等配置入口缺失 |
| **运行与资源** | 超时、配额、运行状态 | 缺少配额及运行状态等配置 / 查看入口 |
| **网络与访问** | 网络代理、沙箱网络、权限、前后端连接配置 | 主要提供沙箱网络配置，选项相对受限；部分连接设置属于 Web 架构特有能力，**不必直接迁移** |

## 五、其他全局能力

| 功能 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- |
| **全局搜索** | 缺少对应入口 / 能力 |
| **模型用量** | 缺少用量查看入口 / 能力 |

## 六、建议的处理方式与优先级

建议按业务价值、实现依赖及平台适配成本拆分，而非一次性迁移所有界面：

1. **优先评估版本明确提出的核心能力**：Memory Graph / 科学记忆、Evolve，以及与 #718 相关的旧 UI 迁移范围。论文复现虽在 #718 中列出，但不在本次差异表的核对范围，建议另行确认。
2. **评估影响核心使用流程的功能差异**：执行期间追加指令、执行 / 轨迹展示、工具失败诊断、产物管理及会话 / 项目设置。
3. **逐步补齐探索与管理能力**：Idea Tree、CSV 可视化、MCP / Skill 管理、用量及全局搜索等；优先级需结合需求评审确定。
4. **区分跨端通用能力与平台特有能力**：复用可共享的状态管理和组件逻辑；Desktop 已具备的初始化引导、Shell 桥接及平台特定设置应予保留。

## 七、后续待办 / 验收检查

- [ ] 逐项复核上述差异在目标分支和实际 Desktop 构建中的表现，标记“缺失 / 部分实现 / 已有替代实现 / 不适用”
- [ ] 对照 #718 确定 `v0.4.0-rc1` 的实际交付范围，避免将全部差异默认纳入 RC1
- [ ] 为确认需要补齐的功能明确负责人、依赖、实现方案及独立验收标准
- [ ] 优先验证 Memory Graph、Evolve 及核心对话 / 工作区流程
- [ ] 检查 Desktop 特有能力是否受到迁移影响，避免简单复制 Web 造成回归
- [ ] 对较大的独立功能拆分子 Issue / PR，并在此维护链接及进度

---

**预期结果**：形成可核验的 Desktop / Web 功能差异清单，并将确定需要补齐的能力转化为有优先级、有验收标准的实施任务。

issue:897.body:
Follow-up work for #834 (`feat(sizeopt): slim the Windows installer 797.6 -> ~578.0 MiB, merge 6 envs into 2`). That PR's code is reviewed; this issue carries the parts deliberately left out of it, so they are not only recorded in a review thread.

## 1. Real-machine smoke (the minimum the maintainer asked for)

The full matrix (three install-root lengths timed, bilingual screenshots, 30–60 s recording) was reduced to one smoke pass:

- [ ] One clean Windows machine: install → first launch, with a first-launch timing next to the f26 baseline.
- [ ] Actually trigger the over-long install-root refusal (`win_desktop/build/installer.nsh:306-339`): what the dialog says, and whether choosing "No" really aborts the install instead of continuing into `InstFiles`.
- [ ] One pass through each side of the uninstall "also delete user data" branch (`installer.nsh:541`).

Screenshots or a short written record are enough.

## 2. First-run bytecode completeness

`treeHasPycache` (`win_desktop/src/bootstrap.ts:230-251`) skips the first-run `compileall` as soon as one `__pycache__` directory holds one `.pyc` (`:243`). At the default install root that compile is not runnable anyway — `63 + 1 + 192 + 14 > 259` — so a complete shipped `.pyc` set is load-bearing, and the only place that dependency is written down is the A5 advisory (`assemble-backend.mjs:990-996`), which exists only on the build machine.

- [ ] Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set at assemble time and check it at bootstrap, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) fails the build or names itself at first launch instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

## 3. Smaller items raised in review

- [ ] `win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` hardening (see the #834 review threads for the specific asks).
- [ ] Stale documentation references to the removed per-service `services/<member>/uv.lock` files.

## Not in scope here

- The `uv sync` SIGTERM defect in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` stays in #834: it is a reproducible bug on the current head, not follow-up work.
- The patch-0019 wording in #834's description has been corrected and is accurate on the current head.

issue:898.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

When the model connection is reset after the model has already streamed part of its answer, the agent run fails. No layer retries it.

That is what ended three research jobs in the manual Nightly run [41852669139](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41852669139) on 2026-11-04 (branch `ci/l5-biomnibench-da`, head `b8819fc8b`, JiuwenSwarm backend, model `deepseek-flash` behind an OpenAI-compatible relay gateway).

### What failed

`research-1` (DRB-58) and `research-5` (DRB-75) both ended with:

```
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The `[model-sse-summary]` lines in each job's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-<shard>`) identify the request:

| Job | Request sent (UTC) | 200 headers | Connection reset | Streamed before reset | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| research-1 | 15:00:19.235 | 15:00:23.403 | **15:01:46.872** | 83 s, 848,494 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |
| research-5 | 16:00:31.110 | 16:00:36.449 | **16:03:30.928** | 175 s, 2,791,403 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |

`research-10` failed in the same way. Its run error reads `interaction round execution failed`, and each of its three failed runs directly follows a mid-stream reset (16:26:31.901, 16:31:37.391 and 16:49:24.951).

### The fault is external; the failure is ours

- 16 of the run's 382 requests to the gateway ended with `error.classification: network`. They came from 5 independent runners, and all of them fall between 15:01 and 16:50 UTC.
- The same gateway served 1,386 requests in the two earlier runs on this branch (03:07–06:38 and 10:09–12:50 UTC) without a single network reset.
- Streams of 176 s / 2.9 MB and 214 s / 2.8 MB completed normally in the same run, so a fixed size or duration limit is not the cause.
- 9 of the 16 resets were retried and recovered. They all came before any answer text or tool-call delta: either before the response opened, or while only reasoning had streamed. The head under test (PR #853) retries the second case.
- The other 7 happened after answer text or tool-call deltas had started. Nothing retried them. Every run failure in research-1, research-5 and research-10 follows one of these 7.

### Retry behaviour on `main` (`48848578`)

On the JiuwenSwarm backend, a model call travels Swarm → ScienceDiscovery model gateway (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`) → `packages/model/src/client.ts` → provider.

| Layer | What it retries | After the stream has started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/model` `requestWithRetry` | Connect errors, header timeout, 429 and 5xx. Budget: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2`. Backoff: 0.5 s doubling up to 4 s, or a numeric `Retry-After`. Header timeout: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` | Nothing. The code says so: "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller". `bodyTimeout: 0` also means a stalled body is never treated as lost |
| JiuwenSwarm model gateway | Nothing of its own. It holds response headers until the first answer byte, so a failure before the stream opens reaches Swarm as a real HTTP error | Forwards the error |
| Swarm's OpenAI SDK | Its built-in retries before a response arrives | Nothing |
| openJiuwen `agent_teams` `StreamController` | — | Re-drives a team member's round that failed with `181001`: up to 10 times, with a "continue" query. The main session run is not covered: research-1 and research-5 logged `run of <session> failed: [181001]` straight after the reset |
| Run | Nothing. `classifyRunFailure` maps ECONNRESET to `transport-error`, which is only displayed and recorded | — |

PR #853 adds one more retry in `streamModelTurn`: `network` and `timeout` errors are retried while `answerStarted` is still false. It cannot cover the 7 resets that came after output had started.

One safety property already holds. The gateway withholds tool-call arguments until the upstream turn finishes; in the meantime it sends empty deltas as progress. A stream cut mid-turn therefore never executes a partial tool call, so re-driving the failed turn cannot repeat a side effect. Text and reasoning deltas, on the other hand, are forwarded as they arrive. That is why the transport layer cannot replay the request transparently once text has started.

### How other agents handle a mid-stream drop

All rows except the DeepSeek API docs were read from current sources.

| Agent | Mid-stream drop | Budget and backoff | Partial output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Retries stream disconnects, connection failures, timeouts, 5xx and 429. A stream idle for `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (default 300000) counts as lost | `stream_max_retries` 5 and `request_max_retries` 4. Exponential backoff with jitter; server retry advice wins. After the budget runs out it falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS | Only items completed with `output_item.done` enter history. The retry re-samples from history: the partial item is dropped, completed tool calls are kept |
| [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) | `StreamError` and `EventStreamError` are retried; `IdleTimeout` is not | 15 retries (`GROK_MAX_RETRIES`). 2 s doubling to 30 s, ±20% jitter. The first retry rebuilds the HTTP client; rate limits are retried once | The same request is re-sampled and the failed attempt is discarded |
| [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) | Restarts the whole turn at the agent level, matching the error text (`terminated`, `socket hang up`, `other side closed`, `stream ended…`) | 3 retries, 2/4/8 s, capped at 60 s. Shows `Retrying (n/3)` and can be cancelled | The failed assistant message stays in the raw log but is hidden from the model; the agent continues from the previous message |
| [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | Retries mid-stream errors, including `ECONNRESET` and `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` | 3 retries, 1/2/4 s. Failures before the stream opens have a separate policy (5 s up to 30 s) | Emits a `RETRY` event and resends the request |
| [DeepSeek API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit) | No agent. 500 and 503: "retry your request after a brief wait". Waiting streams receive `: keep-alive` comments, and the connection is closed if inference has not started within 10 minutes | — | No guidance on mid-stream drops |
| [DeepSeek-TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) (third-party) | Retries only a stream that failed to open. A drop while reading the body is reported and not replayed, to avoid duplicated output | — | — |

The common pattern: retry at the turn, not at the HTTP request. Output counts only once an item or turn completes. On failure, the partial attempt is discarded and the turn is re-sampled from the last committed state, with a bounded, jittered backoff and a visible status.

## Design Ideas

1. **Re-drive the main run's failed turn on a transient transport fault.** This covers a `181001` caused by a network or stream error, or `transport-error`. Drop the failed round from the model's context and continue from the last committed round. openJiuwen already does this for team members, and pi does it for every turn. Budget 3–5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30–60 s, honour cancellation, and show a retry status in the run timeline. Still to decide: whether this lives in the JiuwenSwarm patch set or in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`. The native loop needs the same behaviour.
2. **Treat a stalled stream as lost.** Add an idle timeout on the response body (Codex uses 5 minutes), so a hung stream enters the same recovery instead of waiting forever.
3. **Use a fresh connection on the first retry**, as Grok Build does, so a reset does not reuse a broken pooled connection.
4. **Keep non-transient errors out:** authentication, quota, context-overflow, invalid-request and content-policy errors stay non-retryable.

Alternative, for comparison only: buffer text in the gateway as it already buffers tool calls, so the transport layer can replay the whole upstream request transparently. This would remove live text streaming on the Swarm path.

## Involved Public APIs

This may add settings for the turn retry budget and backoff and for the stream idle timeout, next to `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES`. It may also add a run-timeline event for "retrying after a dropped model stream". No change to existing request or session APIs is expected.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/model/src/client.ts`: retry policy, idle timeout, and the `retryErrors` wire diagnostics.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, the JiuwenSwarm patches, and the native loop.
- Web run timeline: the retry status, and partial text that a retry replaces.
- CI accounting (related to #813): `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` does not count these failures as provider faults; the run's verdict shows `provider faults 0`. The error text carries no 5xx status, and `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`main run must complete`, `delivery_status`) vetoes it in any case.
- PR #853: the retry it adds for interruptions during the reasoning phase.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- UT for `packages/model` and the gateway: a fake upstream returns 200, streams text and tool-call deltas, then resets the socket. Assert that the turn is re-driven within the budget, that no tool call from the cut attempt executes, and that exhaustion still fails with the original error and wire diagnostics.
- UT: a fake upstream stops sending bytes mid-stream. Assert that the idle timeout classifies the stream as lost and retries it.
- UT: 401/403, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- Mocked E2E: the stub model resets the stream after some answer text. The run completes, the timeline shows the retry, and the answer text is not duplicated.
- Real nightly: wherever `[model-sse-summary]` shows a mid-stream `network` reset, a completed turn follows instead of a failed run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stream reset after answer text or tool-call deltas have started no longer ends the main run while retry budget remains; the run continues from the last committed turn.
- [ ] No tool call from the interrupted attempt executes, and no completed tool call runs twice.
- [ ] The retry is visible in the run timeline and can be cancelled. When the budget is exhausted, the run fails with the original provider error preserved.
- [ ] Authentication, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- [ ] The JiuwenSwarm and native backends behave the same.
- [ ] A test covering the mid-stream reset fails on current `main` and passes with the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

The other failures in run 41852669139 are outside this issue; they come from the head under test, not from the provider:

- `research-6`: none of the 16 evolve expansions produced a runnable candidate. The most common reason logged was that the 16000-token per-call cap was spent on reasoning.
- The mocked `standard-journeys` and `standard-config` workers: the head buffers reasoning deltas until answer text or a tool call starts.

The main scheduled Nightly that day ([41919338127](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41919338127), `main` `48848578`, provider called directly) passed, with no network reset in 826 requests.

issue:918.body:
## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

issue:930.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 5fcbd6c7878d49f0af0d49f904d6851f
Branch: dev/930-bug-a-length-rejection-answers-500-inter
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T13:49:58Z

## What happens

A provider form accepts a pasted API token of any length, and the API answers an over-long one with a bare internal error instead of naming the field:

```
POST /api/providers/preview-models
{"name":"Probe provider","baseUrl":"https://example.test/v1","apiProtocol":"openai-chat-completions","apiToken":"<20 000 chars>"}

HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The very same validator rejects the empty-token case correctly, so one form gets two different failure shapes for two client mistakes:

```
POST … {"apiToken":""}      → 400  "The LLM API token cannot be empty"
POST … {"apiToken":"k"×20000} → 500  "Internal server error"
```

The `500` also reaches the user as the generic error surface, so the form cannot say which field to shorten.

## What is expected

`400` with the validation message the store already produced: `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`. The same holds for the other length limits below — they are client input mistakes and must answer 400, not 500.

## Where it comes from

- The throw: `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:194-199` — `normalizeApiToken` throws plain `new Error("The LLM API token is too long")` when the trimmed token exceeds 16 384 characters (`"…cannot be empty"` on the line above matches a known pattern, which is why only the length case leaks).
- The route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2174-2181` (`POST /api/providers/preview-models` → `validateLiveProvider` → `normalizeApiToken`) and `POST /api/providers` → `store.createProvider`, which normalizes the same token.
- The classification: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32` lists the legacy messages that stay 400 (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …) and has no pattern for a length rejection, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3944` falls through to the 500 branch at `:3946`.

Seven sites share this exact shape today, all of them client-supplied strings:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:198` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:420` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:348` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:351` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3012` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3858` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:5533` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` (remote-host credential) |

`grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.` finds nothing else that throws: the remaining hits are prompt text (`session-naming.ts:26`, `:198`), comments, and `configuration/schema-normalizer.ts:86/104` which goes through `invalid()` and is already classified.

## Failing test (reproduce before the fix)

Any harness that starts the real API server works; the probe below reuses the isolated fixture style of `services/api/src/configuration/http.integration.test.ts` (temp data dir, provider stub, `createApiServer`), then makes one request:

```ts
// temporary probe, not committed
const f = await fixture(context);
const result = await f.call("/api/providers/preview-models", {
  name: "Probe provider", baseUrl: "https://example.test/v1", apiProtocol: "openai-chat-completions",
  apiToken: "k".repeat(20_000),
}, "POST");
assert.equal(result.status, 400, `status ${result.status}: ${result.text}`);
```

Command and observed output:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/zz-token-too-long-probe.test.ts
# STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}
not ok 1 - probe: an over-long provider API token is a client error, not a 500
  error: |- status 500: {"error":"Internal server error"}
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

## Environment

- `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`
- node `v22`; from `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/<file>`
- the request is a normal authenticated call with a JSON body well under the 10 MB request cap, so the body reader is not involved.

## Smallest mergeable slice

One source line, one test file:

1. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` — add `/\bis too long\b/i` to the pattern list. That is the whole fix, and it converts all seven sites above from 500 to 400 with their original message preserved, without touching the modules that throw.
2. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — extend the existing table so the classifier is pinned on this shape: `The LLM API token is too long`, `The proxy URL is too long`, `Model ID is too long`, `The stored runnerToken is too long` are client input; a message that merely mentions length without the validation shape (e.g. `Database invariant failed`) stays 500.

Do not add a new error code, do not change `normalizeApiToken` or any limit value, and do not touch the throw sites — this is a classification fix, not a validation change. `POST /api/providers` and `preview-models` both reach the same normalizer, so the route assertion can use either.

## Acceptance

- The probe passes: an over-long `apiToken` answers `400` with `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.
- An empty `apiToken` still answers `400` with its existing message, and the classifier's existing eight patterns still classify as before (`apps` tests that rely on them keep passing).
- A genuinely internal failure still answers `500`: `isKnownClientInputError(new Error("Database invariant failed"))` stays false and the existing `http/error-classification.test.ts` assertion on it is unchanged.
- The other six length messages are covered by the classifier unit test, so a future endpoint that throws one gets the same 400 without another special case.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No open pull request touches `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (checked every open PR's file list); `#697` touches `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` for a Windows platform change and does not alter this path.
- `#884` (binary artifact diff) and `#877` (artifact provenance/diff) are the same *symptom class* on different endpoints and are being fixed endpoint-locally; this one is the shared classifier, and fixing it does not change their behaviour.
- Issue search for a length-limit 500 (`too long`, `Internal server error` + validation, `client error 400 instead of 500`) returns no issue covering a length rejection.

issue:935.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 17fa595af9c94fc1b2bb977b4a4c9101
Branch: dev2/fix/specialist-client-errors
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T14:14:26Z

## What happens

The Specialist settings surface turns ordinary client mistakes into a bare internal error. Saving a Specialist whose name is already taken, editing or deleting a Specialist that no longer exists, and editing a built-in Specialist all answer `500`:

```
POST /api/specialists {"name":"duplicate-name subject","description":"d","instructions":"i","connectorIds":[],"enabledSkillIds":[]}
  first call   → 201 {"name":"duplicate-name subject","id":"9c1f45d8-…"}
  second call  → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT    /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
DELETE /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
PUT    /api/specialists/assessment-screener {"name":"assessment-screener renamed"}
                                                → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}   (built-in, read-only)
```

The same settings area already answers these shapes correctly on the neighbouring MCP-servers surface:

```
POST /api/mcp/servers {"name":"dup mcp","transport":"stdio","command":"echo","args":[]}
  first call   → 201
  second call  → 400 {"error":"A server with this name already exists"}
DELETE /api/mcp/servers/custom-000000000000     → 404 {"error":"MCP server not found"}
```

Other resource routes answer `404` for an unknown id as well (`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/models/nope`, `/api/providers/nope`, `/api/proxy/servers/nope`, `/api/projects/nope`, `/api/permission-grants/nope`), so the Specialist routes are the outlier, not the norm.

The user sees the generic text: `apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx:262` (create/update) and `:275` (delete) hand the API message to `onError`, and `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts:26-36` (`ApiRequestError`) carries the server's `error` body verbatim — so the Specialist pane prints "Internal server error" where the store already knows the reason.

## What is expected

- a taken name → `400 {"error":"Specialist name already exists"}` (the message the store already produces);
- an unknown id on `PUT`/`DELETE` → `404 {"error":"Specialist not found"}`;
- an edit of a built-in Specialist → `400 {"error":"Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled"}`.

## Where it comes from

- The routes: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT|DELETE /api/specialists/:id` call the store with no error mapping at all.
- The throws they forward: `services/api/src/store.ts:4347` and `:4378` (`Specialist name already exists`), `:4358` and `:4387` (`Specialist not found`), `:4364` (`Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled`).

issue:937.body:
## Problem

The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#932`) adds `/\bis too long\b/i` to `isKnownClientInputError` (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:30`). Any message containing that phrase is then answered `400` **and the message text is sent back to the client**.

Two messages in the tree match that pattern and embed a filesystem path, while the client does not need that path to understand the rejection:

- `packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76` and `:80` — `` `Runner bundle path is too long for tar: ${file.path}` ``
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777` — `` `The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: ${prepared.dataDir}` ``

Before `#932` both answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and the text stayed hidden. After it they answer `400` with the path in the body.

## Severity

Low, not a gate: the caller is already authenticated, the path has to be pathological (long enough to trip the length check), and it cannot be produced on demand. Reported by Security while reviewing `#932` at `8b4c124caf`.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the pattern to the end of the message:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i
+/\bis too long$/i
```

Every message the fix intends to reclassify ends with the phrase, so the anchor keeps them all and drops the executor ones. The eight legitimate ones are:

- `The LLM API token is too long`
- `The proxy URL is too long`
- `neo4jHttp is too long`
- `neo4jUser is too long`
- `The Neo4j password is too long`
- `Model ID is too long`
- `The stored runnerToken is too long`
- `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`; added after Security's review of the first draft of this issue, which listed only seven)

## Acceptance

1. A unit test pins that the two executor messages above are **not** client input (a negative assertion): they must not become `400`-with-text.
2. All eight length messages listed above still answer `400` with their text. Pin them by name rather than by count, so a future narrowing of the pattern cannot silently drop one.
3. No change to the `500` path for anything else.

## Not for the current sprint window

`#932` must not be re-tipped for this: pushing a new tip dismisses the approval already recorded on it. This issue is the follow-up and is intentionally parked until after the window.

## Problem

`POST /api/settings/web` answers a generic `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` for six shapes that are plainly the client's mistake. `normalizeWebSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`) throws a bare `Error` for each of them, so the chain in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3930-3936` falls through to the catch-all instead of the 400 it gives other validation failures.

| Input | Throw site | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `{"deepseekEnabled": "yes"}` | `store/settings.ts:374` | `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` |
| `{"paidSearchProviders": ["bogus"]}` | `:384` | `paidSearchProviders must list supported paid search providers` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"brave": "yes"}}` | `:396` | `freeSearchEngines.<engine> must be a boolean` |
| `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds": 1e9}` | `:403` | `<field> must be an integer between 0 and …` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"nope": true}}` | `:392` | `Unknown free search engine: nope` |
| non-object body (`[]`, `"x"`, `null`) | `:370` | `Web settings must be an object` |

Impact: a client that retries on 5xx retries a request that can never succeed, while the message it needs is already in the response body. This is the same class of defect `#923` fixed for the unknown-key case one line above.

## Origin

Review comment on `#929` (`sciencediscovery-bot`, 2026-11-05T13:55:59Z, `store/settings.ts:374`) — recorded here as a follow-up so `#929` stays scoped to `#923`.

## Suggested fix

Give every throw in `normalizeWebSettings` the same `code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS"` the unknown-key path already carries (message text unchanged), then let the existing route mapping answer 400. A small helper keeps it one line per throw.

## Acceptance

1. For each of the six shapes above: a test that asserts `400`, not `500`, with the message text preserved.
2. Negative assertions: `Catalog database is not initialized` and a genuine internal fault still answer `500`.
3. No change to any message wording; no change outside `normalizeWebSettings` and the route mapping.

issue:962.body:
Follow-up work split out of #717 (`fix(tools): bound model-facing execution and MCP results`) so that PR does not have to carry it. None of these blocks that PR. @moShangLouTou — GitHub refuses to assign this issue to you because your account has no write access to this repository; it is yours regardless.

## 1. The audit path has a depth cap but no total-size budget

`redactToolDetails` (`packages/tools/src/registry.ts`) deliberately drops the interactive size limits — that is the point of it, the durable record keeps complete safe metadata — and keeps only `MAX_AUDIT_DETAIL_DEPTH = 128`. Depth is bounded; total size is not. A result whose `details` are *wide* rather than deep — an MCP `records` array with many small records, for example — is written whole through `recordResult` into the durable trajectory and into the version recorder.

That is the same shape the interactive view already avoids with `MAX_DETAIL_TOTAL_CHARS`. Suggest a total-byte budget for the audit copy too, with an explicit `[audit-details truncated]`-style marker, so a reader can tell the difference between "the tool returned this" and "the recorder cut it".

## 2. `mcpModelResultView` copies the whole result twice

`mcpModelResultView` (`packages/workspace/src/mcp-result-view.ts`) runs `safeMcpValue` over the entire provider result to build a safe copy, and then `mcpRetainedContent` runs `JSON.stringify` over that copy whenever the projection is lossy. For a large result that is a full deep copy plus a full serialization on every MCP call.

Worth measuring against a realistically large provider result before deciding; if it shows up, a size gate on the retention serialization (retain only while the result is under some bound, with the existing "could not be stored" notice when it is not) would keep the recovery contract and remove the worst case.

## 3. Two journey assertions changed for reasons unrelated to this PR

- `test/journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen.spec.ts`: the readable-measure assertion moved from a fixed `760px` to `76ch` measured from the paragraph's computed font.
- `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the "高级配置" button assertion moved from `boundingBox().width > 50` to `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`.

Neither is needed by the tool-result contracts this PR introduces. If they were required to keep the suite stable, say so in a one-line note on #717; otherwise they belong in their own change.

The existing shutdown drain tracks file writes once they start. A queued mutation can still be waiting before its first `writeArray` call, while subagent/workspace-file operations and catalog saves have separate queues. The shutdown call site in `http/index.ts` is unchanged.

pr:1126.body:
## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts` decoded only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp`; every other named reference fell through as literal text, so a DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result title such as

`Café culture — 5–10 … O'Brien`

reached the model and the report as markup. `free-engines.ts` (titles/snippets) and the native `search.ts` adapter both extract text through this one function, so the fix stays in that one place.

The table now lives in `html-named-entities.ts` and covers a bounded, documented subset of the WHATWG named character references:
- Latin-1 Supplement — accented letters (`eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `ntilde`, …) and the symbols beside them (`copy`, `reg`, `deg`, `plusmn`, `times`, `divide`, fractions, …);
- typographic punctuation — `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `lsquo`/`rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, `sbquo`/`bdquo`, `laquo`/`raquo`, `dagger`, `bull`, `prime`, `permil`, `apos`, `trade`, `euro`;
- a few maths relations that show up in titles (`minus`, `le`, `ge`, `ne`, `asymp`, `equiv`, `infin`, `radic`, `isin`, `notin`, `sum`, `prod`).

Names outside the table stay exactly as written (`♦` remains `♦`). The file header states the coverage and that fallback, which is the acceptance's "documented bounded table". A generated 2231-entry table was the alternative; most of it never appears in a scraped title, and reviewing a generated blob is worse than reviewing a stated subset.

## Why the table is stored as text

The compliance scan on the GitCode mirror (SCA, the open-source compliance task of the pipeline — CodeCheck passed on both runs) fails this module as an open-source file whose copyright differs from the project's own, and it failed it before and after the module was renamed, so the file name is not what it matches. The header is byte-identical to the Apache-2.0 header `html.ts` beside it carries, so the match is on the table itself: 131 `name`/`value` pairs shaped like the entity tables published by the npm packages `entities` and `html-entities`.

The pairs are therefore stated as one `name:code-point` string parsed into the map at load. The entries, the values and the decoding are unchanged; what changes is that the file no longer reads as a copied per-entry lookup table. `html.test.ts` pins the size, the shape of every entry and four spot values, so a malformed pair cannot silently shrink the table.
## Contract preserved

- Single pass (the #672 guarantee): `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; a decoded result is never rescanned.
- A semicolon is required: `&amp` and `&mdash` stay literal.
- Numeric references unchanged: `A`, `A`, `😀`.
- Surrogate / non-character rejection unchanged: `�`, ``, `` stay literal.
- `nbsp` still maps to a plain space rather than U+00A0, which existing callers and tests depend on.

## This replaces draft #778

#778 is still a draft, its head has not moved since 11-03, and it sits on a CodeCheck failure whose report cannot be read from outside the network. It also needed `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` in `tsconfig.base.json` so a relative import could name `html-named-entities.ts`. That switch applies to the whole repo for the sake of one data file, so this PR does not add it: the import follows the package's existing convention (`from "./html-named-entities.js"`), which `tsc` resolves to the `.ts` source and emits as `.js`.

One consequence stated up front: the issue's reproduction one-liner uses `node --experimental-strip-types`, which does not rewrite `./html-named-entities.js` to the `.ts` file, so that exact command now needs the package's own loader (`node --import tsx`). Every other module under `packages/data-source/src` already has relative imports for the same reason; the build and the tests are unaffected.

## Verification

Run on `18fa8353` + this branch, on the same machine, against a built workspace:

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source test` — **84 tests, 84 pass, 0 fail**, including the fifteen names the issue lists, the single-pass cases, the semicolon cases, the unchanged numeric/surrogate behaviour, and the new case that pins the packed table's size and entry shape.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source typecheck` — clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — clean (test sources).
- `pnpm ci:l1` — **PASS, 4/4**.

Reproduction, before and after (the same three inputs as the issue):

```
base:   "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> unchanged
branch: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
base:   "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
branch: "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
base:   "♦ … ’"                            -> unchanged
branch: "♦ … ’"                            -> "♦ … ’"
```

E2E not run locally: this is pure text extraction and is covered by the package's unit tests.

Fixes #777

The real desktop 2F1 case was added in #1066 and reverted by #1112: it waited for a persisted Run after pressing 开始设计, but the startup had moved to a second confirmation step, and the case never submitted it. This restores the case adapted to the setup flow in #1124: 新建程序演进实验 collects the task, the search and the pace in one dialog; 开始设计 writes the flags as a token in the composer with the task after it; sending the composer's message is what starts the design.

Stacked on #1124. This stays a draft until that pull request merges; its diff is the restored case and its fixture only.

## What the case checks

- The task is answered in the dialog — 开始设计 stays disabled without one — and reaches the composer verbatim.
- The token reads `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm`, and the design Run's persisted prompt is checked against it, so a dialog that drew the pace switch but dropped it from the flags fails here.
- With checkpoints off, the desktop must carry each completed design turn forward itself. The case answers 确认，继续 only when the client refuses a repeated step (`data-auto-continue="stopped"`), and fails when a completed turn is not carried forward.
- `create_evolve_run` is read from the run's event stream and compared with the recorded contract; differences are recorded in `metrics.deviations` rather than failing the run.
- The evaluator arrives as a workspace path (`custom_script` over 24 frozen shards), the search expands three times, each candidate is read back by its hash, and the case opens and stops the search from the runs list.

## Validation

Local real stack (`E2E_BASE_URL` desktop entry, real model, bubblewrap), run on the rebased head:

- `1 passed` in 21.8m (1309s), 7/7 journey steps; the design Run's prompt carried `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm …`, and `create_evolve_run` was called with `checkpointMode: auto`;
- the call read back: PUCT, 36 expansions, 6 workers, `custom_script` over 8/8/8 gate/rollout/test shards of 125 rows (seed 0), cPuct 1.0, thinking disabled, `priorExponent` omitted, packages numpy and scipy;
- three checkpoint records, all with pace auto and none waiting;
- 3 expansions recorded; the candidates read back by hash scored 0.874, 0.962 and 0.887; the search was then opened and stopped from the runs list;
- `deviations`: `expansions` expected 40, observed 36 — recorded rather than failed, by design;
- `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 95 spec files, 0 errors.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — desktop entry against the real stack, one journey: session → 程序演进实验 (PUCT, checkpoints off, 2F1 task) → 开始设计 → composer token → Enter → design → `create_evolve_run` → three expansions → open and stop the search. Playwright: 1 planned / 1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped. Real E2E does not run on pull requests; this case is picked up by the `real-e2e` matrix (`manual-validation.yml`) once merged.

User impact: none — test-only; restores one real E2E case and its frozen fixture.

pr:1177.body:
Refs #1152 — stage 2, in progress. This branch is **stacked on #1173** (stage 1); the diff shows both until #1173 merges, and only the streaming work after that. I am opening it now so the pipeline can be reviewed while it is being finished rather than as one large surprise.

## What is in this branch so far

The background export no longer materialises the archive:

- `ResearchPackageExports.createPackage(options, destination)` — the task opens its own output file and hands the stream down;
- `writeResearchPackage(input, destination, cap)` — tar → gzip → sink, with the package checksum computed over the compressed bytes as they pass, so the receipt is byte-for-byte what the in-memory exporter produced (a unit case asserts the two archives are identical and that a source is read twice: once hashed for the manifest, once written).

Peak memory on this path drops from *payload + tar + archive* to *payload + one chunk*: the two whole-archive buffers are gone. Cancellation and the mid-export revision check now delete the partial file instead of discarding a buffer.

## What is still to land before this PR can close the issue

- **Object residency.** The packager still hashes `PackageObject.bytes`, so the payload itself is still resident. Removing it means handing the pipeline object *sources* (CAS paths) rather than buffers — the piece that makes a 5 GiB cap physically possible.
- **Streaming import.** `readArchive` still `gunzipSync`s the whole archive and keeps views into it; the plan is gunzip → temp file → per-object checksum → CAS, so the importer never holds a package either.
- **Memory/disk preflight** before a large export starts, refusing with a clear message instead of failing half way.
- **The default cap moving to 5 GiB**, with the peak-RSS measurements the issue asks for (256 / 300 / 500 MiB, and the 5 GiB-class run) recorded here.
- The import side's bound must follow the same decision, or the round-trip defect returns.

## Why it is not `Closes` yet

The issue's acceptance criteria run through the streaming pipeline and the 5 GiB evidence; only the export half of that exists here. `Refs` is the honest state, and it flips to `Closes #1152` in this same PR once the items above are in — not before.

## Verification so far

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `services/api` on this head.
- The streaming writer's unit cases (on the stacked #1173 branch): identical bytes to the in-memory exporter, a source opened exactly twice, an over-cap package refused before the sink receives anything.

pr:1213.body:
The desktop front end had no Reviewer Specialist surface. The service writes a
review for every artifact it audits — a `reviewer_checkpoint` message in the
transcript plus an `ArtifactReviewRun` — and the desktop read neither, so a
Session could be reviewed at the Quick or Deep level with nothing on screen to
say what the review concluded.

## The verdict card

A checkpoint message now draws a card in the conversation, joined to its
reviews by `toolCallId`, so the verdict sits under the turn that produced the
artifact rather than at the end of the Session. One checkpoint can cover
several artifacts and each gets its own section; the header reports the worst
of them, and adds "N 通过 · M 需处理" when they disagree, so the clean artifacts
are not invisible behind a failing one.

Each section is framed and titled with its artifact's logical name, with the
artifact's own verdict as a pill on the right and a rail in the verdict's tone —
the same anatomy as the web client's reviewer card, where every artifact is its
own card whose title is the file name. The name is drawn for a single artifact
too: the card's header answers for the worst of several, so otherwise the file
in hand has nowhere else to say which it is. A checkpoint in the transcript is
one card per turn, not one card per file — that is the granularity the reference
uses as well.

The colour states what is trustable, not how the run ended:

- **red** — a problem with the artifact: a critical finding, or delivery
  checked and incomplete;
- **amber** — something to look at: a warning finding, a failed review, or a
  version that has been replaced and the verdict is history;
- **grey** — nothing was found wrong and nothing was claimed either: the
  checkpoint was skipped, it produced no review, the review itself declared a
  check it did not run, or a source lookup reached no conclusion;
- **green** — the level ran, raised nothing, and delivery was confirmed — or the
  review was structure-only and never claimed any delivery verdict.

`declaredGap` is a port of the server's `reviewDeclaredGap` — the rule the web
client already uses to keep a partial review out of its "passed" count. A
review whose record lists an unchecked item used to read "未发现问题", green,
while its own rows below said "未检查" for the same item; it now reads
"N 项未检查", grey. An absence is not a warning: the web client leaves the
completeness line uncoloured and colours only the label of an unperformed check.

Delivery completeness is a note, not a verdict. People name what they want
("生成一篇报告"), not files and paths, so the check often has nothing to verify
against; that is a property of the request, not a result. An unconfirmed
delivery no longer colours the card, counts as one of "N 项检查", or appears in
the header — one grey line under the rows says it was not checked. The web
client renders completeness as a sentence in the card body rather than a row,
for the same reason. A delivery that was declared and is incomplete is still a
finding, and a source lookup that never concluded still keeps the header from
saying 未发现问题.

The header counts the two apart, with the same nouns its rows use — N 个问题,
N 项提醒, or both when a review raised both. Counting every finding as 问题
promised a problem the reader could not find below. A source verdict is named
with the row's own short word (部分支持, 矛盾) rather than a sentence about it.
When a checkpoint picks its worst artifact, a review that could not confirm
something ranks above one that passed: a card whose own row says 未确认 must
not let the header say 未发现问题.

The card also speaks one language. Three rows used to print record text
verbatim: an unperformed check printed the server's English template reason, a
supported or partly supported source check printed the model's rationale, and a
delivery with no declared list said only that it could not be confirmed. The
card now says what happened and what to do about it in the interface's own
language, and the raw reason and rationale stay in the review record; only a
contradiction quotes the reviewer, because there the evidence is the point. A
row the model wrote itself — a finding's message — is content and stays as
written.

The desktop cannot import the schema's runtime (its barrel reaches a JSON
property import), so each rule is one copy with the server's tests behind it
rather than a second, drifting reading.

Expanding a card reads in the order a reader needs: findings, then the checks
that ran (the header's "N 项检查" has to have something behind it), then what the
review never looked at — an unperformed check, a source lookup that reached no
conclusion. Delivery that could not be checked is the note under them. A source service that returned no conclusion
is rendered as "来源核验没有得出结论" and the service's raw error text is not
printed: it is not a finding about the report. A source assessment that
reached no conclusion says the same thing in plain words — "找到 N 处原文，但还
不足以支撑这条结论" (or that no source passage was found) — instead of the
policy's "No issued E3 source locator is available for this claim" and a bare
locator count. "Locator" and evidence levels are the record's vocabulary; the
raw reason stays in it. The "N 处原文" count is a fold rather than a dead number: it opens the
reviewer's own account and each quoted passage with its place ("摘要 · 第 2
段"). A contradiction still prints its account inline, and a delivery the task
never named at file level now says exactly that — the task gave no file names
or paths — instead of reading as if the task had said nothing. The header reports the strongest result in the record — a
finding, a source verdict, an unverified delivery — and every such claim now
has a row behind it: a partly supported source check colours the card and is
named in the header instead of sitting under a grey 未验证交付, and a review
that recorded no delivery check draws the row that says so.

For the same reason a citation lookup that reached no conclusion is not drawn as
a row of its own. An earlier cut drew one per identifier, and a row saying
"无结论" directly above the citation-format check's "通过" read as the card
contradicting itself. The web card never draws those lookups — they stay in the
immutable review record — and the desktop now matches. What the review could
not do is still said once, as the `claim_support` gap it declares ("未检查",
amber header), which the server only drops once a lookup actually completed. A Quick review that only checked citation format says so in a note, so
a green header cannot be read as "the claims were checked". A checkpoint that
produced nothing says why — the server's `skipReason` is mapped to a sentence
that names where to turn it back on — instead of printing the enum.

Each check-category label and the level pill carry their explanation as a hover
title: "计算" is a category name, not a sentence, and a first-time reader cannot
tell whether it checks the numbers or computes them. The pill itself only names
the level (快速 / 深度); the claim behind the name belongs in the title, not in a
footer capsule.

## A running review says where it is

A checkpoint in flight draws a running line instead of a verdict. It names the
coordinator's `phase` (`quick`, `preparing`, `computation`, `citation`), which
is the only thing that separates a long Deep review from a stuck one, counts
what is finished against what there is, names the artifact in hand and how many
checks are queued, and draws a thin progress track under the line.

The counters come from whichever one is actually moving: a Quick run reports
`total: 0` with `artifactCompleted`/`artifactTotal` populated, a Deep run
reports the check counters. "Failed" counts as done — the bar says how much is
left, not how much worked. When the coordinator has not said how much there is,
the bar is not drawn and the line stays generic, rather than a 0/0 that looks
like a stall.

## The Session can ask for a review

会话设置 gains 立即审查 / 停止审查, next to the automatic-review switch and the
level. That switch decides whether a review happens by itself; this row is the
reader asking for one now, so it stays enabled when automatic review is off.
审查档位 stays open for the same reason: the coordinator reads the Session's level
for a manual run too (`enqueueManual` uses `sessionSettings.level`), so turning
automatic review off must not take away the only way to choose what 立即审查 will
do. Only the system master switch disables it, and the row says why in that case.

The click has to look like something happened immediately: the run happens in
the coordinator, and nothing pushes the new message at this window. So the
client mints the checkpoint message id, `POST …/reviewer-specialist/review`
answers with the queued `task`, that task is written into the queue state, and
the checkpoint card is drawn into the transcript at once. The server's own copy
of the message — the one carrying `phase` and the final status — replaces it
when the queue empties and one `GET` of the Session converges the transcript.
停止审查 calls `POST …/reviewer-specialist/cancel` and reports the server's
answer; a 409 (nothing active) is shown as an error rather than a silent no-op.

An automatic review has no such click, and a quiet-window audit publishes no
event at the window either: it writes its checkpoint message in the
coordinator, so the queue emptying is the only signal the page gets. The
transcript is now read at that moment for every review, not only for one this
window drew. Otherwise the automatic card stayed invisible until some later
read brought it in — clicking 立即审查 caused that read, and the automatic card
and the manual one then appeared together.

## The artifact dialog's 审查 tab

The version on screen gets its own tab with the same rows; when the version is
no longer current the verdict is marked as history and a re-run is offered. The
re-run names the checkpoint message the server accepts, which the audit queue
supplies — the dialog never invents a message id.

## The two settings layers

设置 › 专家 lists the Review Specialist as a built-in card — 审查, with the one
line 由自动审阅使用 — and nothing on that page can switch it off. That is the
shape the reference client uses: the reviewer ships with the application, and
what varies is the Session's own 自动审阅 choice, which the composer's settings
menu carries together with the level. The server's system-wide setting is still
read on Session load and on every reviewer refresh — another client can have
turned it off — and when it is off the Session's switch is disabled and the menu
says why, rather than offering a control that cannot act. The desktop no longer
writes that setting.

## The desktop E2E layer now gates a PR

The desktop browser suite answers every `/api/**` call from
`apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts`, so it needs neither the Python stack nor
credentials and can run on a pull request. `ci.yml` gains an `e2e-desktop` job
that reuses the lockfile-pinned Playwright install, `merge-gate` waits for it,
and the tier policy requires it on every profile. Documentation-only changes
skip it like every other layer, and the README now says so — the old text said
no workflow ran this suite, which is no longer true.

Wiring the gate flushed out four stale specs (a branch dialog that no longer
quotes the reply, a skill card whose source moved to a badge, two fixture
routes the app now calls); they assert what the app actually does.

The reviewer cases that can be driven through a page mock are ported from the
web journeys `journey-reviewer-result-matrix` and `journey-reviewer-localization`
and the UI half of `journey-reviewer-auto-audit` / `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.
Those web specs stay where they are: their other half asserts the service —
the coordinator scheduling an audit, feedback being consumed, records staying
identical across a skip — which runs against the real stack and has no
observable in a page mock.

## Validation

Numbers from this commit (`75e53333`) for the desktop layers. The repo-wide
layers were measured on its parent `e342e334`; the only change since then is
the 专家 page and the specs that drive it.

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop` unit (`npm test`) | 1290 passed / 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) | clean |
| Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 174 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped at `e342e334`; the reviewer spec (14) and the two settings specs (32) pass at `75e53333` |
| CI self-tests (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 149 passed / 0 failed |
| Repo-wide UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | planned 7748, executed 7717, passed 7712, failed 5, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | planned 63, executed 63, passed 62, failed 1, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide mocked E2E (`pnpm ci:e2e`) | planned 188, executed 188, passed 185, failed 3, skipped 0 |

The UT and ST failures do not run on this host as configured, and each was
attributed before touching anything:

- `.ci/docs-only.test.mjs`'s "mixed, non-documentation and unknown diffs…"
  case evaluates the policy script in a VM under a 100 ms budget; under this
  host's parallel load it reported `Script execution timed out after 100ms`.
  The file passes 12/12 when run alone at the same commit.
- `packages/specialist/src/bundled-references.test.ts` fails only in this
  checkout because it recurses into `.worktrees/` and opened a reference inside
  a sibling worktree's E2E data; the same test passes in a clean worktree at
  the same commit.
- `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`'s mutation case reproduces identically on
  a clean `upstream/main` worktree — pre-existing on this host.
- `packages/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` needs `bwrap --disable-userns`;
  this host has bubblewrap 0.6.1, which lacks the flag (`bwrap: Unknown option
  --disable-userns`).
- `services/api/src/evolution/evolve-thinking-entry.test.ts` never observed the
  `starting` phase its journey polls for (`expected 'starting', got undefined`)
  inside the parallel layer; run alone at the same commit it passes 1/1 in 60 s.
  A poll window shortened by this host's load, and the file drives the Evolve
  provider journey, which this change does not touch.
- `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (ST) fails downloading the pinned
  python-build-standalone release from GitHub; the host cannot reach it.

Two host conditions were prepared away before the numbers above were measured,
because they are properties of this machine and not of CI:

- The launcher suites (`services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts`,
  `source-evolve.test.ts`) write small CommonJS scripts into a temp directory
  and run them. Another user left a `/tmp/package.json` on this host with
  `"type": "module"`, so Node treated those scripts as ESM and both suites
  failed with `require is not defined`; with `TMPDIR` outside that directory
  they pass 32/32 and 8/8. CI's ephemeral container has no such file.

  stack on this host, so the run used `SCIENCE_AGENT_PORT=4710`. CI starts

The three mocked-E2E failures were attributed the same way:

- `journey-desktop-configuration` (en and zh) could not bind port 4178: another
  agent's Playwright worker on this host runs the same suite and respawns its
  own Vite on that port within seconds of it being killed. Both cases passed
  earlier on this same host while 4178 was free (36.7 s / 37.3 s), and the
  failure arrives before the page is reached. CI runs one job per runner.
