  a previous run; after resetting the layer's `data` (keeping `envs`) they pass.
  The run reported above is from that clean data.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Two surfaces, both exercised on this commit.

The desktop browser entry (mocked per-page API; no backend), 174 cases: a
confirmed delivery is green; a checkpoint over two artifacts names both in
separate framed sections, each carrying its own verdict while the header reports
the worse one; a review that never verified delivery is amber; a
review that declared an unchecked item is amber and named; structure-only is
green because it never claimed delivery; an incomplete delivery is red; a stale
verdict says it is history and offers a re-run; the eight-checkpoint Quick/Deep
outcome matrix including the two skip reasons and a reload; a running review
reporting its phase and progress; an automatic review's card arriving on its
own when the coordinator finishes; 立即审查 with automatic review off, at a level
chosen while that switch is off, queueing a deep manual review whose card
appears in the transcript and settles; 停止审查 stopping one already under way;
the built-in Review expert listed on 专家 with no switch; a reviewer switched
off on the server disabling the Session switch with its explanation; the
Session's own settings surviving a reload; the artifact dialog's 审查 tab
queueing a re-run with the right message id.

The shared `test/journey-reviewer-*.spec.ts` journeys, against the real control
plane (the mocked E2E layer's own stack), all pass in the same layer:
`journey-reviewer-auto-audit`, `journey-reviewer-localization`,
`journey-reviewer-result-matrix`, `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.

Closes #1203 — the desktop Reviewer Specialist feature request this implements.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account has no write access to apply it)
User impact: the desktop app shows Reviewer Specialist verdicts, can run or stop
a review from the Session settings, and configures both Reviewer settings
layers. The desktop E2E suite becomes a required PR check.
Compatibility and migration: none. No API or configuration change.

pr:1215.body: Closes #1199. ## What changes The desktop 设置 › 技能 page gains the surfaces the web app has and the desktop did not: importing a Skill, editing one in place, reading one on its own page, and taking a package back out. Import, edit, and detail are pages inside the settings pane rather than dialogs, so the list stays one step away. - **添加技能** is a menu in the list header with three entries: **上传技能** (a `SKILL.md`, a ZIP package, or a `.skill` archive, dropped or picked), **从 GitHub 导入** (inspect the repository, then pick the packages to install), and **从零开始写** (the existing authored form). - **搜索** narrows the list on a Skill's name or description as the user types. The global switches stay above the filtered rows and still act on the whole list; a term that matches nothing says so instead of leaving the page blank. - A repository is inspected first (`POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect`) and each chosen package is imported at the commit that inspection saw, so what the user reviewed is what gets installed. Replacing an installed Skill requires `overwrite` plus the revision the user saw (`expectedRevision`); a different revision is a 409 rather than a silent replacement of an edit made in another window. Re-importing identical bytes is a no-op instead of an empty revision, and a built-in Skill stays read-only. - An inspection of a real, large repository says what it is doing and offers **取消**, which stops waiting without reporting a failure. The metadata clone has a 60 s ceiling and the checkout that fetches files 180 s; a timeout is reported as one. The scan no longer downloads the repository: it clones commit metadata only (`--filter=blob:none`) and checks out just the `SKILL.md` files (non-cone sparse), which is what discovery and the candidate list read. A package's resources are fetched only when an installed Skill has to be compared (unchanged vs update) or when the package is imported. A server without partial-clone support falls back to a plain shallow clone — and only an explicit refusal of the filter falls back: previously any transport error did, which turned a one-second hiccup into a 471 MB download (`github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills`) and made a normally 4 s inspection time out at 180 s. A transfer that broke (early EOF, `RPC failed`, reset connection, TLS) is now retried as the same clone once, and a transfer that stops moving is abandoned after 30 s below 1 KiB/s. - The checkout an inspection made is kept for 15 minutes, so the packages that follow are imported from it instead of cloning the repository once per package. Measured against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` (~471 MB, 177 `SKILL.md` files): inspection went from 29 s to **3.6 s** through the API (0.07 s to import a package whose content is its `SKILL.md` alone, 1.1 s for one with 15 resource files). Before the checkout was reused, an import spent ~41 s cloning on its own. A request for another commit, ref or repository still clones. - A selection is imported by one **background job** (`POST /api/skills/import-git/jobs`). The page returns to the list as soon as the job is accepted; the list reports `正在后台导入 n / total`, and the job keeps going when the reader leaves 设置. The job expands the retained checkout once for the whole selection instead of once per package, reports per-package failures without stopping the rest, and switches on the packages it created when JiuwenSwarm is the backend. A job the server no longer knows (a restart or its 30-minute cleanup) is treated as terminal instead of being polled forever. Same-name uploads are renamed only when the desktop asks; the route's default remains 409. - Discovery used to stop at 100 packages, which silently hid 77 of that repository's 177; discovery now lists every package the checkout holds, so no repository can be silently truncated. One inspection response carries at most **500** candidates, reports the repository's `total`, and returns a `nextCursor` while more remain. **加载更多** reads the next page at the same commit, from the checkout the first page made (no second clone); the rows already read stay on screen with their ticks, and new importable rows join the selection only when the user had kept everything selected. Candidate cards use `content-visibility: auto`, so a response holding hundreds of them costs what is on screen. Against the same repository one page is enough: 177 candidates, `total` 177, no cursor. - **Clicking a Skill opens the Skill's own page**, as OpenScience does, instead of expanding its instructions inside the card. A breadcrumb names the list, and the page carries the Skill's mark, name and source badge above its description, **文件** with `SKILL.md` rendered in a measured column, and **详情** printing the frontmatter keys the package declares (`许可证`, `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, …) as label-over-value facts, omitted entirely when there are none. At the product owner's request the page does not repeat the list's switch, a version line, or a 可用范围 block: availability is a list decision, and repeating it here only pushed the document down the page. Sections are separated by a hairline rather than boxed in cards; the instruction column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so a wide table scrolls inside the prose instead of stretching the page. - A row ends in a chevron. Hovering it opens the actions that package allows, drawn in the row's own popover and flipped upwards when the row sits near the bottom of the pane: **导出** on every package (a built-in is read-only, not uncopyable), and **编辑** / **删除** on a managed package: - **导出** downloads the installed package as the ZIP the importer accepts back (`GET /api/skills/:id/package`, built by `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` from the same files the importer reads, under the single root directory an uploaded package has), so an export can be imported again here or on another machine without rearranging it. Built-in packages export too: read-only says who may change them, not who may copy them. - **编辑** opens the editor below. - **删除** reads the deletion impact first (`GET /api/skills/:id/deletion-impact`); if a Project or Session selection still names the package it says how many and stops, rather than turning the route's refusal into a failed request. Otherwise the deletion goes through the settings shell's one confirmation dialog, which names the Skill and what removing it means. - **编辑** is a page of its own: name (read-only), description, one content editor with 撰写 / 上传, and a collapsed 高级设置 holding license, compatibility and the package's files. Reference files can be added under a chosen subdirectory (`references`, `assets`, `scripts`, …); choosing one opens an editor under its row with its own 保存文件, while the main editor stays `SKILL.md`. A non-UTF-8 pick is refused before any write. Saving sends back `metadata` and `allowed-tools` as declared (string or YAML sequence), so optional frontmatter is not dropped; a stale revision from another window surfaces as a conflict message. A partial multi-file upload still surfaces the revision it already stored. - **Uploading a package whose name is taken** is the desktop's choice, not a change to the route's contract: the desktop sends `onDuplicate=rename`, and the server installs it as `name-2`, `name-3`, … with `SKILL.md`'s name rewritten. `POST /api/skills/import` keeps its historical 409 for web and CLI callers, which omit the flag. Every page below the list replaces it and is left through the header's back control; the editor also offers 取消 in its footer, which is the same exit. The header names the page that is actually open, and the list keeps the installed count. The pages share one content measure so moving between them does not move the fields under the pointer, and they reuse the pane's existing tokens and controls rather than introducing a second visual language. A newly installed Skill is enabled when the switches are available; the background job owns that step, so closing 设置 before it finishes does not skip it. Updating an already-installed Skill leaves its switch alone, because a user may have switched it off on purpose. Closing 设置 after visiting 技能 re-reads the catalog, so the composer's `/` palette reflects the change without a reload. Backend support: `ImportSkillFromGitRequest` gains optional `commit`, `overwrite` and `expectedRevision`; `InspectGitSkillRepositoryRequest` gains optional `commit` and `cursor`, and `GitSkillRepositoryInspection` gains `total` and `nextCursor`; background imports add `StartGitSkillImportJobRequest` and `GitSkillImportJob` with `POST/GET /api/skills/import-git/jobs`; `CreateSkillRequest.allowedTools` accepts `string | string[]`; `SkillCatalog` accepts an injectable checkout so the Git import branches can be tested without a network; `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` builds an installed package as a ZIP and `GET /api/skills/:id/package` serves it as `application/zip` with a `content-disposition` name; and `SKILL_VALIDATION` now maps to HTTP 400 instead of falling through to an unclassified 500 when its message wording does not match the client-input patterns. ## Screenshots Captured at `308c08e1`, 1440×900, in zh-CN and en; the list images (`01`, `02`) and the search images were refreshed at `867b4ebb`, where the search field sits above the list. The save dialog is a native OS window, so a page screenshot cannot capture it; the export image shows the row after the write, and the E2E stubs the picker to assert the ZIP name and bytes. The detail page intentionally has no 可用范围 block, version line or switch: those were removed at the product owner's request, and availability stays in the list. | State | 中文 | English | |---|---|---| | 技能 list + 添加技能 menu | | | | Row chevron menu (导出 / 编辑 / 删除) | | | | 上传技能 | | | | Skill detail | | | | 编辑 | | | | Edit-save conflict | | | | 删除 confirmation | | | | Delete refused while a selection names it | | | | 导出 result (native dialog not page-capturable) | | | | 从 GitHub 导入 — inspection running | | | | Git candidates with ticks | | | | Git candidates after 加载更多 | | | | 技能 search filtering the list | | | | A term that matches nothing | | | | Search at 1100 px (no horizontal overflow) | | | ## What was run ### Search and rebase (`867b4ebb`) - Rebased onto `main` (`0c3d4d52`); the merge queue had rejected the previous head as conflicting after #1258. No merge commit: the 25 branch commits were replayed on the new base. - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1277 pass, 0 fail (adds the search field: typing a term narrows both lists, and a term with no match renders the no-match line instead of the empty state) - Desktop Vite against the live stack at 1440×900 and 1100 px, zh-CN and en: the field renders above the list, filtering matches name and description, the no-match line appears, and the pane has no horizontal overflow. ### After the review round (`308c08e1`) - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` skill suites — 70 pass; background-job store tests — 2 pass - `services/api` skills + import-job tests — 27 pass - full desktop Skill E2E journey — 1 passed (13.0 s) - `pnpm --recursive typecheck` — pass (all workspace packages) - `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1193 pass, 0 fail (includes a two-page repository: the header shows the repository total, 加载更多 reads at the same commit from the returned cursor, the rows already read stay, and loading more does not re-tick a selection the user cleared; the card opens the detail page and lists what the page must show; the chevron menu offers 导出 / 编辑 / 删除 only on a managed row, closes on Escape and on a press outside, exports the returned bytes, deletes through the confirmation dialog, and reports a package still named by a selection instead of deleting it) - `packages/specialist` unit tests — 10 pass, 0 fail. Four drive the real checkout against a `git` on `PATH` that answers like the transport: a broken transfer retries the same clone and never asks for a full repository, a clone that never answers is attempted again before giving up, a checkout that loses its connection is fetched again, a refused filter is the only path to a full clone, and a repository that does not exist is cloned exactly once. - `services/api` Skill suites (`skills.test.ts`, `skills-git-import.test.ts`) — 30 pass, 0 fail (includes the checkout-reuse case, a partial-checkout case that builds a real sparse clone from a local repository and asserts that the resources are fetched on import and that the second scan reports `unchanged`, a 120-package listing, a 520-package repository read as 500 + 20 from one checkout with no gap or overlap, a cursor without its commit rejected, `exportPackage` opening its own archive with the importer's unzip — the files under the Skill's root directory, the same bytes importing back through the upload path, a read-only built-in exporting, and an unknown id refused — and the lifecycle test downloading `/api/skills/:id/package` and checking `application/zip`, the `content-disposition` name, the archive's entries, and a 404 for a Skill that does not exist) - `services/api` targeted suites (`server.test.ts`, `skills.test.ts`) — 138 run, 135 pass. Five repeated runs passed on `d0e3e48f`, `0287aa41` passed again, and the final head `308c08e1` passed after the page layout, 详情, editor and background-import changes (1 passed, 13.0 s). 1. Open 设置 › 技能 on the desktop; the Skill about to be imported is not listed. 2. 添加技能 › 上传技能 hands the page one file; it reports the installed package by name, and the list is back through the header's back control. 3. Open the card: the Skill's own page names it, its breadcrumb names the list, it carries the description, renders `SKILL.md` under 文件, shows 详情 with the `license` the card never displayed, and the pane does not scroll horizontally. 4. From the row's chevron menu, open 编辑; the editor page is named after the Skill. 5. Rewrite 指令 and 保存; the editor reports the save. 6. 导出 from the same menu hands the save picker `.zip`; the bytes it writes are a ZIP (the E2E stubs the picker and checks the name and magic). 7. Read the package back through the API: the new instructions are installed and the `license` key the form does not display survived the save. 8. 删除 from the menu, confirmed in the dialog that names the Skill, removes the card and the package from the catalog. The menu steps press an entry with Playwright's `force`, after asserting it is visible, and the reason is recorded in the spec: Playwright's own scroll-into-view measures the entry while the popover is still opening and then moves the settings pane by that distance, which carries the row out from under the pointer; the pointer's absence closes the popover before the press lands. A person scrolls to the row, points at it, and presses; the step does the same. Every entry's effect is asserted after the press, so the skipped stability check does not weaken the journey. pr:1221.body:
Desktop users need Web to manage execution resources and inspect model usage. This brings those capabilities into Desktop's existing settings layout, makes environments clearly belong to a Runner, and adds compact token statistics both in settings and below conversation replies.

Closes #1220.

The release-version CI correction is tracked separately in #1269; this PR's diff contains no release-gate changes.

## Changes

- Combine remote machines and scientific environments into Runtime environments. The overview contains registered Runners and global Conda/Pip sources; Runner details contain connection, resources and environment management. Package sources save quietly, and environment creation uses creation-specific feedback.
- Add execution quotas, JiuwenSwarm paid-search credentials and webpage-fetch selection, and network proxy configuration. DeepSeek search/fetch share a key. Proxy selection, connection testing and bypass editing use compact grouped controls; custom proxy URLs can be viewed and edited.
- Add deployment-wide model usage with date filters, total/input/output tokens and a flat model table. Below each finished conversation turn, add a token badge with an expandable model/token breakdown. Omit unreported fields and avoid counting cache or reasoning tokens twice.
- Record JiuwenSwarm task usage at the model gateway before SDK defaults can turn missing reasoning into zero. Keep platform main/child accounting separate and ignore duplicate SDK reports. Existing usage records are not rewritten.
- Remove project Runner selection from system settings. Unspecified selection follows the registered Runner catalog dynamically; explicit selections and admission restrictions remain enforced. No session Runner picker is introduced.

Analytics reporting fields are additive; exchange rates remain enabled by default for existing clients. Existing Web settings remain available. Dormant DeepSeek credentials require an explicit re-save to enable search rather than being silently activated.

## Validation

Focused checks performed during implementation:

- Runtime-settings browser journeys: **14 mocked-backend Playwright cases passed**, including registration, detail navigation, connection/resources, credentials, deletion, NPU selection, and no project-availability writes. Both real-backend Runner cases were updated and successfully collected (not executed); targeted TypeScript checking of both specifications and their imported helpers passed.

- Resource/settings regressions: **156 passed, 0 failed** (Desktop 116, schema/API 38, focused store 2).
- Conversation and per-turn usage regressions: **150 passed, 0 failed**, including existing transcript/configuration behavior; follow-up usage-label checks: **6 passed**.
- JiuwenSwarm gateway, agent, orchestration and usage-accounting regressions: **240 passed, 0 failed**.
- Latest bypass-layout change: **1 focused save regression passed**. Affected-package type checks, targeted test type checks, and Desktop/API builds passed during implementation; `git diff --check` passed.
- CI regression checks: **8 app-model-setup render scenarios, 6 turn-usage tests, and 16 analytics tests passed**; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passed. App fixtures include the session usage endpoint, and analytics fixtures supply the required context maps.
- Runner-selection review regressions: **35 Web, 14 schema/API, and 28 Desktop tests passed**. Catalog loading cannot seed a partial override; unspecified availability does not imply an existing remote workspace. Web/API/Desktop and shared test type checks passed.
- Verified in a disposable worktree that all 16 feature commits can be rebased onto upstream main `f10ac0fe` without conflicts. The published branch history is preserved.

The browser capture below verifies rendering and navigation in both interface languages against an existing JiuwenSwarm backend. It does not exercise settings writes or paid model calls. Full local UT/ST/E2E gates and native Electron platform checks were not run; the current Actions run reports CI results.

## Screenshots

The conversation images isolate an existing short test exchange and retain its original reply text and recorded token figures in both interface languages.

pr:1225.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

pr:1226.body:
Desktop Settings can manage existing Specialists, but users need the legacy Web UI to create a custom one. This change adds **Add specialist** to the Desktop Specialists page, including when the list is empty.

The add action opens the shared form with a blank draft, Native runtime, and Full access. Name, description, and instructions are required, and the description and instructions limits match the existing API. A successful save refreshes the settings list. A failed save leaves the draft open for retry. Reopening the session picker refreshes the catalog and keeps the current selection.

Closes #1180.

## Validation

Tested commit `c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489` after rebasing onto `eb5f66e80`.

- Desktop typecheck passed.
- 76 focused desktop unit tests passed across `settings-pages.test.tsx` and `composer.test.tsx`.
- Local `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st`, and `ci:e2e` were attempted in WSL. The runs ended before final summaries under the local time limits. UT, ST, and mocked E2E were still preparing the workspace build.

## Desktop browser journeys

PASS in Windows Chrome with a mocked API. Ran `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts` with `--grep "专家"`. **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.**

- Created the first Specialist with the default runtime and capabilities. Canceling a draft made no write, and reopening restored the defaults.
- Corrected a duplicate name after the create request failed. The draft, runtime, and selected abilities survived the error. The new Specialist appeared in the session picker while the current selection stayed in place.
- Existing edit, delete, built-in toggle, and rejected-edit flows passed.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

Users can create and select custom Specialists directly from Desktop. The change uses the existing Specialist API and requires no migration.

## Custom Specialist edit and delete UI

Captured from this PR's Desktop UI at `c04971d66`, using sample Specialist records and a mocked API.

### Actions on a custom Specialist card

The custom Specialist card offers **Edit** and **Delete**.

![Desktop Specialist cards with Edit and Delete actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/34b94f4b4be717e2f6465fa7ce0d11c3ce47e8cd/issue-assets/desktop-add-specialist/pr1226-specialist-actions.png)

### Edit dialog

The dialog opens with the selected Specialist's name, description, instructions, runtime, and capabilities.

![Edit Specialist dialog with an existing configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/34b94f4b4be717e2f6465fa7ce0d11c3ce47e8cd/issue-assets/desktop-add-specialist/pr1226-edit-specialist-dialog.png)

### Delete confirmation

The confirmation names the selected Specialist and offers **Cancel** and **Delete**.

![Delete Specialist confirmation dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/34b94f4b4be717e2f6465fa7ce0d11c3ce47e8cd/issue-assets/desktop-add-specialist/pr1226-delete-specialist-dialog.png)

## Desktop UI E2E coverage

Reran the six Specialist journeys on 2026-11-20 against `c04971d66`. **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, in 47.3 seconds using Windows Chrome.

The suite drives the new Desktop UI through Settings, forms, capability selection, and the session Specialist picker. It covers first creation, cancel/reopen, required fields and default values, duplicate-name recovery, external runtime and capability selection, editing, deletion, built-in toggles, and a rejected edit. During screenshot capture, the delete confirmation also accepted pointer input and canceling sent no delete request.

The API is mocked in these browser journeys. A full Desktop-to-real-backend journey remains a validation gap.

The tests live in [`apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts`](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L132). Run from the repository root with:

```sh
apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts \
  settings-interactions.spec.ts --grep "专家"
```

### Individual test cases and assertions

Each row links to the committed Playwright case on the tested PR revision.

| Desktop UI case | Behavior protected by assertions | Latest result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [First creation and draft cancellation](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L139) | An empty list exposes Add specialist. Cancel sends no POST. Reopening resets the fields, runtime, and capabilities. Required fields block saving. A successful save creates one row and sends the default payload. | PASS |
| [Failed creation, retry, and session picker](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L190) | The form keeps the draft while a duplicate-name error is displayed. | [Editing runtime and capabilities](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L254) | The selected runtime, model, skills, and connectors reach the PUT request for the selected Specialist. The form closes after success. | PASS |
| [Editing and deleting the selected card](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L294) | Renaming updates the visible row and the selected record. Confirming deletion with Enter removes that row and sends DELETE for its ID. | PASS |
| [Built-in Specialist controls](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L328) | Built-in cards expose an enable/disable switch. Switching off updates the visible status and sends only the enabled field. | PASS |
| [Rejected edit](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/c04971d66066fbdfbab2c52cb7bbbf5ef22e4489/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts#L345) | A failed PUT keeps the edit dialog open, preserves the entered name, and displays the server error. | PASS |

Representative assertions from the existing cases show the expected visible outcome and API write.

The first-create case verifies the saved card and exactly one create request.

```ts
await expect(form).toBeHidden();
await expect(browser.locator(".settings-card").filter({ hasText: "Data quality reviewer" })).toBeVisible();
expect(mock.calls.filter((call) => call.method === "POST" && call.path === "/api/specialists")).toHaveLength(1);
```

The edit-and-delete case confirms deletion with the keyboard and verifies that the selected row is removed.

```ts
await confirm.getByRole("button", { name: "删除" }).press("Enter");

await expect(dialog.locator(".settings-card").filter({ hasText: "晶体专家（改）" })).toHaveCount(0);
expect(mock.calls.some((call) => call.method === "DELETE" && call.path === "/api/specialists/specialist-1")).toBe(
  true,
);
```

The rejected-edit case verifies both the error message and preservation of the user's input.

```ts
await expect(form.locator(".row-note.is-error")).toHaveText("name already exists");
await expect(form.getByLabel("名称")).toHaveValue("重复的专家");
```

The latest run on 2026-11-20 completed with **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 flaky**, in **47.3 seconds**. These are browser journeys for `apps/desktop` using a stateful mocked API. The committed delete case uses Enter to confirm. Pointer accessibility and cancel-without-delete were checked separately during screenshot capture. Full real-backend persistence remains outside this browser suite's coverage.

pr:1227.body:
The desktop MCP settings page can manage saved servers. This change adds **Add MCP server** to the page header so users can create a custom server from the desktop app, even when the list is empty.

The dialog uses the existing create endpoint and supports Streamable HTTP, SSE, and STDIO. A new server defaults to Streamable HTTP, stays disabled, and has a 60-second tool timeout. STDIO arguments are entered one per line, preserving spaces inside an argument. A failed save keeps the draft so the user can correct it or retry.

Fixes #1178.

## Validation

The committed real-stack journey passed on `e5434a3f23231cf3910a526321526e81fac3b50c` (1 executed, 1 passed, 0 failed or skipped, seven user steps). It returned `MCP DESKTOP AFB40C13`, recorded a successful Echo invocation, verified edits after reload, and verified deletion and reference cleanup.

The desktop Mock API MCP suite also passed (9 executed, 9 passed, 0 failed or skipped). The final change after that run only disambiguated the cancel button in the separate stack journey.

- WSL workspace build passed before that locator-only correction. The Runner build was refreshed on the final commit.
- `pnpm ci:l1` passed on the final commit (4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed).
- Desktop unit tests (1,172) and custom MCP backend unit tests (7) passed on the original feature commit `0793d5467`.
- The broader local checks remain incomplete. `pnpm ci:ut` stopped at the non-root preflight (7,697 planned, 0 executed). `pnpm ci:st` stopped during Node collection. A completed passing result for the full shared Web E2E suite is unavailable from that attempt.
- Separate full-workspace checks encountered a Launcher permissions assertion under root and a Runner SEA packaging failure for `@sciencediscovery/network`.

## Desktop E2E coverage

The committed tests exercise the new desktop UI.

### Browser scenarios with a Mock API

File: [apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/codex/desktop-add-mcp-server/apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts)

| Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Create from an empty list | Defaults are disabled/HTTP/60 seconds, cancellation resets the draft, a rejected save keeps input, retry creates one server, and testing the connection preserves session defaults. |
| Edit a custom server | The saved description, transport, command and environment variables are sent together. |
| Test and enable/disable a server | The connection test works from its card, and the service switch is independent of default-source selection. |
| Reopen source selection | Saved defaults survive reopening and preserve plugin configuration and service state. |
| Bulk source selection | Select-all and clear preserve unlisted sources and unrelated settings. |
| Retry a rejected selection | The saved value remains visible until a successful retry. |
| Connection failure | The provider's error is shown. |
| Invalid secret key | A blank key is rejected before a save request. |
| Confirm deletion | Confirmation removes the card and sends the delete request. |

```bash
.e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts \
  settings-interactions.spec.ts --grep 'MCP 服务器'
```

### Desktop journey against a real local product stack

File: [apps/desktop/e2e-stack/custom-mcp.spec.ts](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/codex/desktop-add-mcp-server/apps/desktop/e2e-stack/custom-mcp.spec.ts)

The journey runs against a real API, Runner and SDK STDIO MCP server, with a deterministic local model. It verifies seven user steps.

1. Open the add form and check the default transport, disabled state and 60-second timeout.
2. Create the STDIO server through the form and read back its saved configuration.
3. Test the connection and discover the two local fixture tools.
4. Enable the server and independently select it as a default source.
5. Edit its description, reload the page and verify persistence through the UI and API.
6. Send a chat prompt, verify a successful Echo invocation and the actual model-visible tool result, then reload the persisted answer.
7. Cancel deletion once, then confirm deletion, verify the server and default-source reference are removed, and reload the list.

The journey removes its temporary model, project, session and MCP server and verifies cleanup. [Stack setup and run instructions](https://github.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/blob/codex/desktop-add-mcp-server/apps/desktop/e2e-stack/README.md).

```bash

  .e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e-stack/playwright.config.ts
```

The desktop suites have explicit local entry points and have not been registered in the repository CI catalog.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

User impact: Desktop users can add a custom MCP server from Settings.

Compatibility and migration: Existing server records and the create API are reused.

pr:1230.body:
Nightly research-1 failed on DRB-58 after the model returned HTTP 200 and reset every streaming attempt. This PR makes the gateway recovery path actionable and extends the bounded stream retry budget so transient interruptions do not fail the turn after only two retries.

## Changes

- Convert invalid or stale sandbox network authorization failures into retryable tool guidance that asks for a fresh authorization and a new execution.
- Increase interrupted streaming retries from 2 to 4, for at most 5 total upstream requests, and update the regression coverage for the new bound.
- Align the workspace prompt regression and sandbox tool tests with the new authorization guidance and the `unknown` details contract.

## Validation

- Targeted JiuwenSwarm model gateway test: 67 passed, 0 failed.
- Targeted workspace prompt and sandbox network tests: 25 passed, 0 failed.
- Recursive package typecheck and `tsconfig.tests.json` typecheck: passed.
- GitHub Actions L1 slice on the PR head: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed.
- Full UT/ST/mocked-E2E slices were not run locally during PR preparation at the request of the operator. The nightly UT failure that motivated the follow-up was reproduced from its uploaded evidence and fixed here.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for local PR preparation. The affected user journey is the real DRB-58 research run documented in issue #1222; it requires the configured live model service and was not invoked locally. Expected outcome: the research turn completes and declares its final artifacts after transient stream interruptions. The existing nightly run reached the provider-fault path instead.

pr:1240.body:
Refs #1239 (evidence part — see scope below).

## Summary

Nightly run 44361037291, shard `research-11`: the managed Python base setup reached terminal `failed` and J5 was BLOCKED with no executed case. The failure transcript existed in the API response (`setup.error` / `components.conda.error`) but J5 and J3 built their BLOCKED reason from `setup.state` + `setup.message` only, so the transcript never reached the journey report and the next occurrence could not be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.

This PR carries that transcript into the BLOCKED reason. It does **not** investigate the Nightly setup failure itself — that failure is still unconfirmed as a repository defect (same commit, same run, J3 passed the readiness assertion in the L2 job), and it cannot be fixed until a transcript is captured.

## What changed

- `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`: widened `EnvironmentSetup` with optional `error` and `components` (matching `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:451-485`), and added one shared formatter `formatEnvironmentSetupBlockedReason(setup)`. It returns the existing `state: message` text, appends a length-bounded `setup.error`, and appends `conda: <components.conda.error>` only when it differs from `setup.error`. The bound is 1200 chars, the same as the `#1108` precedent (`MANAGED_SHELL_REASON_LIMIT`).
- `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` (J5) and `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` (J3): the BLOCKED reason now goes through the formatter.
- `test/helpers/journeys.ts`: `environmentSetup()` return type widened to the exported `EnvironmentSetup` (no runtime change).
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts`: 6 new cases (see below).

A failed setup remains BLOCKED; no pass/fail semantics change. Test helpers/specs only — no runner, API, or workflow change.

## Proof package

1. **Base SHA:** upstream `main` @ `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608` (merge commit of #1236). Reproduced and fixed on this commit.
2. **Reproduction before the fix:** an out-of-tree probe feeds a failed setup (with `error` and `components.conda.error`) through `waitForEnvironmentSetup` and builds J5's reason exactly as the spec did. The object carries both error fields, but the reason is only `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)` — the transcript is absent (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: false`, `ECONNRESET: false`).
3. **After the fix:** the same probe through the formatter prints the transcript in the reason (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: true`, `ECONNRESET: true`), and an identical conda error is printed once. New unit tests fail on base (the formatter does not exist there) and pass after: `node --test test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` → **17/17 pass** (11 pre-existing + 6 new).
4. **Control case:** a setup without `error` renders byte-identically to before — covered for `error` absent, `null`, `""`, whitespace-only, `components: {}`, and `components: { conda: {} }`. The skip condition (`setup.state !== "ready"`) and J3's `.toBe("ready")` assertion are untouched.
5. **Regression scope:**
   - `node --test test/helpers/*.unit.ts`: 53 tests, 50 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are file-level load errors (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: test/e2e-auth.js`, generated by the E2E global setup and absent from this checkout). Verified pre-existing via `git stash`: same 3 files fail on the clean base (47 tests, 44 pass). No new failure from this diff.
   - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
   - Not run: the full `pnpm ci:ut` layer (same `e2e-auth.js` limitation), the real E2E J5 (needs a paid Nightly / live stack), and the mocked J3 E2E (needs bubblewrap, not installed on this VM). The new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
6. **Diff scope:** 5 files, +137/−7. No derived files, snapshots, or docs to regenerate; no docs pin the old reason text.
7. **Risks checked and excluded:**
   - Secrets: `setup.error` is already credential-redacted at the source (`redactNetworkError` in `environment-store.ts:1458`, and `failSetup` is the sole writer of both `setup.error` and component errors), and the journey report redacts the BLOCKED reason (`journey-report.ts:377-380`). Appending the transcript adds no new secret channel.
   - Bound: both transcripts pass through the 1200-char bound; worst case ≈ 2.5k chars total in the reason.
   - Micromamba: a micromamba failure reaches the reason via `setup.error` (its failure is terminal for that attempt, so `lastSetupError` is the micromamba error); no information is lost by not appending `components.micromamba.error` separately.
   - The differing-conda branch is defensive: `failSetup` writes the same string to both fields, so today they are identical or the component one is null. It is kept (bounded, tested) so a future store change reporting a distinct per-component transcript still surfaces it.
   - Known limitation (follow-up, not this PR): a multi-line reason renders imperfectly in the journey report — `journey-report.ts:458` blockquotes only the first line in `report.md`, and the HTML `<blockquote>` collapses line breaks. No content is lost in either format; fixing the renderer touches shared report code and is left as a follow-up.

Refs #1239.

## E2E user journeys

- J5 (real E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs a paid Nightly run / live stack with real model credentials; the new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
- J3 (mocked E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs bubblewrap and a running stack, neither available on this VM.
- Unit: `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` 17/17 pass (see Validation above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test helpers/specs only; the next Nightly run's BLOCKED reason will carry the setup failure transcript.
Compatibility and migration: none

---

Note for the maintainer: I cannot apply the `release:internal` label myself (403), and I did not use auto-merge. Could you please add the `release:internal` label and add this PR to the merge queue when it is ready?

pr:1243.body:
The hub currently publishes and downloads, but a merged PR is the only way to add anything: there is no account, no upload, no review, no version history, and no way to keep an asset invisible until someone approves it. This adds the backend those four requirements need, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the two pieces that make the switch a deployment step rather than a rewrite: an importer for the existing catalogue and one build-time switch in the site.

**Stacked on #1225.** The static hub is that pull request. This branch is based on its head, so until #1225 merges the diff below includes it; the backend itself is the four commits on top.

## The service (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does:

- Five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models.
- No plugin-specific schema validation; a version is a zip or `.sdresearch` plus an inventory. The server validates what a server must: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, and an uncompressed-size ceiling. Every entry's size and sha256 become the manifest the Files tab renders.
- Stateless HMAC session tokens instead of a Redis-backed store, and scrypt password hashing, so the database is the only stateful dependency.
- The response envelope (`{code, message, data}`) and the public paths (`/api/v1/assets`, `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}`) match the reference, so a client can be repointed.

Endpoints: register/login/me (`{id, username, display_name, role}` payloads), asset list/detail/create/update, version upload/list/detail, the files listing with `with_content`, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}?version=` returning a presigned URL, and an admin review queue with approve/reject. Registration closes after the first account; that account is the administrator, and later accounts come from `POST /api/v1/auth/users`.

## Storage and access

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable: a download resolves through the API, which checks visibility and returns a URL that expires (`HUB_PRESIGN_SECONDS`, default 10 minutes). External skill ids are paths (`chemistry_and_materials/real_world_workstations/…`), so storage keys validate the id segment by segment and the API routes it with a path converter.

## The importer

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket. It preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps the single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks each imported version approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

## The site

One build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a short-lived URL before navigating, which is what a private bucket requires. If that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment behaves exactly as before. Listing, README and the Files tab still come from `catalog.json`.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: **13 passed**. Covers registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding the site sends, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end (including idempotence and a checksum mismatch).
- `python -m scripts.import_catalog --dry-run` against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files are not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub build`, with and without the API switch.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS on a local stack** — this host's MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real OBS bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium. Not yet on a deployment host; that is the next step when one is available.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: `assets: 387 created`, `versions: 385 imported`, the two sessions above skipped. Keys land under `assets/<kind>/…` in the bucket.
- Chromium, `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Chromium, the path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- HTTP, not the test client: login as the administrator, create an asset, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve (`200`), download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed afterwards.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.

Building the real service against OBS surfaced two fixes that are in this branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer that OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`), so checksum calculation is `when_required`; and asset ids longer than 64 characters (88 is the maximum, 84 exceed 64) needed wider columns and path-aware routes.

The host clock is 28 minutes ahead, which SigV4 rejects. The smoke tooling compensates for a drifting development host; the service deliberately does not, and its README says the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: accounts, uploads, version history and review can exist behind the hub; downloads can come from a private bucket through short-lived URLs.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. The static exporter and the public-read publishing workflow are unchanged; the site only changes shape when built with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE`. The database is new and its schema is created at startup; the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`.

pr:1248.body:
Fix the merge-queue UT flake reported in #1245. The case "an immediate bubblewrap failure is reported instead of leaving the execution pending" in `services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts` used a 500 ms fake seccomp close plus a 250 ms wall-clock assertion. On a loaded 4-worker/4-vCPU UT slice that assertion failed with `exit was reported only after 296ms; the seccomp close must not be awaited`, because the measured span also includes load-sensitive startup work.

The case now observes event order instead of time. `closeSeccompFilter` sets `closeStarted` and waits on a gate that the test releases only after `executePython` settles. The test asserts `closeStarted === true` and `closeFinished === false`, releases the gate, and waits for the close. `execTimeoutMs` remains 1 500 ms, so an implementation that awaits the close rejects with the execution timeout instead of passing. A `context.after` hook releases the gate when an assertion fails. The comment above the gate states that timeout-rejection path; its previous wording named the stderr assertion, which is not evaluated on that path.

The change is test-only: `services/runner/src/executor.ts:1310` still calls `void closeFilter(...)` and is unchanged.

Verified on candidate tree 277fbfc0885c2f933213663c58daeaf9e276a4cd (head 15d761e4cf0942d4798ded5bd3246aae183fab67 on top of PR head 11a1c1e1):
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="immediate bubblewrap" services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts` → 1/1 passed, exit 0 (27.7 ms).
- `node --import tsx --test services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts` → 66 tests, 63 passed, 3 failed; all three failures are sibling cases failing only with `spawn bwrap ENOENT` because the review container has no bubblewrap, and they fail identically on the unmodified baseline (diff of TAP result lines empty).
- Mutating `services/runner/src/executor.ts:1310` to `await closeFilter(filter)` in a scratch copy makes the case fail deterministically 3/3 times with `Python execution timed out after 1500 ms` (~1524 ms), so the regression is still caught.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0.
- `git diff 11a1c1e1 HEAD` touches only `services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts` (2 insertions/2 deletions, both comment lines); `executor.ts` diff is empty.
- For reference, CI at the previous head 11a1c1e1 (UT job 135478876612) passed 7813/7813, including this file's 66 cases.

Closes #1245

Tests: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="immediate bubblewrap" services/runner/src/npu-devices.test.ts
Reported by the agent; not rerun by the control plane.

pr:1255.body:
Closes #1253

The desktop MCP settings page could only edit a server that already existed: the form's sole entry was `setDraft(draftOf(server))`, and `emptyDraft()` was unreachable fallback filler. "Add my own MCP server" was impossible in the desktop app — which is where the local stack runs, and therefore where a `stdio` server would be launched. This brings the page to the web client's parity on the already-present routes; nothing on the server, the schema or the packaging moves.

## What the page can do now

**添加服务器.** The existing form opens empty (`emptyDraft()`) and saves with `POST /api/mcp/servers` (no id). The draft starts switched off, as an imported server does, and is reached by agents only once the user has read the test result and turned it on — testing it works while it is off, because the probe builds its own client. The created server is tested straight away — `POST /api/mcp/servers/:id/test` — and the dialog stays open with what the test found: the tool names, or the failure. That is the difference between finding a wrong command in the dialog and finding it at the next run. A refused save keeps the form and its fields on screen with the reason from the route.

**导入.** A `{"mcpServers": {…}}` spec is parsed and previewed as `name · transport · target`, then written **one request per server**. That is deliberate: `POST /api/mcp/servers/import` writes the whole spec or nothing and stops at the first name clash, so a spec of two servers would report one opaque error. Per-server requests give each entry its own outcome (`已添加` / `失败：…`) and let the valid half land.

**工具.** Each custom row expands to a read-only list of the tools the server reports (`name` and description). This is what tells the user whether adding it was worth it; the row already carried the count.

**未授权 / 授权 / 取消授权 / 清除授权.** A server whose `authorization.state` is not `authorized` says so — `未授权`, or `授权已过期` for `expired` — instead of looking broken next to a `已连接` status. 授权 opens a popup and posts `POST …/oauth/start` with this origin's callback URL (`/api/mcp/oauth/callback`), then navigates the popup to the URL the route minted; 取消授权 and 清除授权 call `…/oauth/cancel` and `…/oauth/clear` and re-read the list.

**Secrets stay unreadable.** The existing rule is untouched: a stored env/header value renders as an empty password field whose placeholder says it is stored, a rename without a value is refused before the write, and the new OAuth secret keeps the same `null`-means-keep semantics.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`: clean.
- New suite `apps/desktop/tests/mcp-servers-create.test.tsx`: **11/11** — 添加服务器 opens an empty form, posts without an id, and starts the new server disabled, then names the tools its first test found; a refused create keeps the form open with the reason; saving with no name says the name is required; 导入 writes one request per server and reports each outcome (including the refused half's own sentence); the import preview reads the transport the way the route stores it; 编辑 after a create opens the row's own fields; a row awaiting consent is re-read until the grant lands and is then tested; 授权 detaches the popup and keeps the minted URL reachable when the popup is blocked; a stored env secret is never rendered back.
- Related existing suites (`mcp-discovery-refresh`, `settings-screens`): on this Windows host 5 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. The two skipped are `os:linux`-tagged and do not register on Windows, so they are reported as skipped rather than as passing — an earlier version of this section said "skipped by their platform tag" without saying which platform, which the review correctly found does not reproduce on Linux. Across the three files on this host: 13 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped; CI `UT` (Linux) is green on `6edd132e` for the same files.
- Each fix above was mutation-checked: reverting it turns its own test red, and the file was restored afterwards.
- `vite build` (apps/desktop): succeeds, only the pre-existing chunk-size warning.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: not runnable on this host (the l1 profile targets `linux/amd64` and reports `executed: 0`), so CI is the word on it.
