recent.body:
Actions failure classification: **unknown**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663249 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11))

## Current behavior

`research-11` planned exactly one case, J5, and executed none. The shard reported `{"status":"FAIL","planned":1,"executed":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"skipped":1}`, `1 skipped`, and the problem line `- e2e-real: 1 skipped — a skip is not a pass`. The journey report captured in the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (id `14460243200`) records the precondition:

```
BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)
```

The environment-setup state was therefore `failed`, not `installing`. The message is the generic non-micromamba failure from `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:1460` (`Conda environment setup failed`); the store keeps the actual provisioner transcript in `setup.error` / `components.conda.error`, but J5 prints only `setup.message`, and `real-e2e.yml` uploads `.ci-results` only. The runner's operational log at `<CI_RUNTIME_DIR>/real-standard/data/logs/runner.log` is not in the artifact, so the precise conda/provisioning error is missing.

`Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reports `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`; `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) fails with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) fails with `RESULT: failure`.

## Expected behavior

The managed Python base reaches `ready` within J5's 180 s wait (the wait added by #286 / #287), J5 executes, and the shard reports planned=executed=passed=1. A setup failure must remain BLOCKED; the journey's reaction is the intended fail-closed behaviour. #286 was about the normal `installing` phase racing the first read; this run observed `failed`, so it is a different failure.

## What was checked

- The failed-step output of job 135002663249 and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (`14460243200`): the journey report and its blocked-step screenshot, `run.log`, `stack.log`, and `api-diagnostics`. The stack log shows three `GET /api/environment-setup 200 OK` requests and no conda/micromamba transcript. I read the artifact with `gh run download`; its origin is this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at `d57fc269`: `failSetup` (`environment-store.ts:1460`), `runManagedEnvironmentSetup` / `bootstrapStarter` / `validateStarter` (the `conda` component is entered only after micromamba is ready, so this is the Python-base create/validate phase), and `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts:73` (the BLOCKED skip).
- Previous runs: `research-11` succeeded in Nightly 44199315530 (job 134449454466) and 43984975918 (job 133711095274), both with J5 executed. In 43514552368 the job failed *after* J5 executed (a different, post-setup failure). The immediately preceding nightly, 44199315530 on `b2075e49`, ran the same provisioning path and J5 passed.
- Diff: 25 commits separate `b2075e49` from `d57fc269`; none touch `services/runner`, `packages/network`, `services/launcher`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, or `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` / `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`. That makes a regression from this commit in the provisioning path unlikely, but it does not identify the failing precondition.
- Not checked: the runner's operational log and the `setup.error` payload, because neither is uploaded. I did not rerun the paid Nightly to try to reproduce the state.

## Uncertainty

The inner failure is unresolved. Candidates that the missing transcript would separate: conda channel/CDN/network failure while creating the Python base, a runner disk/permission problem, or a latent race in the provisioning code. The job duration (~2 min) and the `failed` state observed before J5's 180 s deadline are consistent with a setup failure during the conda step, not with a wait timeout, but they do not choose among the candidates.

## Why report this / next verification

1. Re-run `research-11` (or the Nightly) on this commit and observe `GET /api/environment-setup`; a transition to `ready` and a J5 pass would support a transient provisioning failure, while a repeat failure would justify a code investigation.
2. Preserve the evidence next time: upload the runner's operational log for the real shard, or include `setup.state`, `setup.error` and the `components.conda` transcript in the journey report on a BLOCKED precondition. That is the one missing fact that would let the next occurrence be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.
3. If the transcript shows an external channel failure, this report can be closed as an environment precondition; if it shows a code error, it becomes a concrete repair issue.

recent.body:
Actions failure classification: **external**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663117 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-2))

## Current behavior

The only planned case in the `research-2` shard, `DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration`, was classified `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The shard reported `planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 0 / failed 0 / provider faults 1` and failed with `- e2e-real: 1 provider fault(s) — an unverified case is not a pass`. The full job log gives the case's own error:

```
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts; delivery_status=partial; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=1; run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The job's `stack.log` identifies the failing request as `model-8f784f89-e866-486a-88b8-9d48d6063774`: HTTP 200, 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes over 105.9 s, then `"error":{"classification":"network"}`, with `"attempts":1,"retries":0` and `"hasText":true,"hasToolCalls":true`. The next line is:

```
[jiuwenswarm-agent] run of 670fa97d-b9d0-4410-ad9f-ac0d80e75072 failed: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

## Expected behavior

DRB-59 completes its declared final artifacts and the shard reports `passed 1 of 1`. A live provider keeping the response open is a precondition of that journey, not a product assertion.

## Causal chain

The gateway accepted the request (`200`), streamed the answer and tool-call deltas for about 106 s, and the upstream connection was reset while answer text had already been exposed. The model gateway's bounded mid-stream retry is deliberately disabled once answer text is visible: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:517` throws when `state.text` is true, so the turn was not replayed and the run failed with the original transport error. The accounting then correctly recorded `PROVIDER_FAULT` (the status-less transport classification from #1071 / #1076). Under the repository's documented policy a provider fault is not a pass, so the downstream jobs failed:

- **Account for real cases** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reported `Planned 21; executed 20; passed 19; provider faults 1.` and `- PROVIDER_FAULT: ...DRB-59...`.
- **Gate / merge-gate** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) failed with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:52` throws because the daily profile requires the `real-scheduled` job to succeed.
- **Report the outcome** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) failed with `RESULT: failure`; it only asserts that the gate result is `success`.

The other 19 real cases in this run passed, so the endpoint was not globally down; the fault is confined to one model turn.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- The failed-step output of job 135002663117, its `error-context.md`, and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-2` artifact (id `14455408997`). The artifact's `stack.log` is the wire-level evidence quoted above. I read it with `gh run download`; the artifact belongs to this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at the failed SHA: `const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 4;` (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:188`) and the `state.text` guard at `:517`. The zero retries are the documented behaviour, not a missing retry loop.
- Existing Issues: #1071 / #1076 added the status-less transport classification; #898 documented that a reset after answer text starts is not replayed; #1222 recorded the same class for DRB-58 in run 44199315530. This run is a new occurrence of that class, not a new repository defect. It is not the cause reported in #1157-#1160, which describe run 43760882196 and a different failure.

## Uncertainty

The gateway diagnostics preserve only `classification: network`; the provider's own reason for closing the connection (load, edge reset, upstream timeout) is not visible. One reset in one request does not establish how widespread the provider problem was.

## Next verification

Re-run `research-2` (or the Nightly) once when the gateway is healthy and check that DRB-59 completes; a pass would separate the outage from the commit. A rerun was not requested here because the independent J5 provisioning failure in the same run (job 135002663249) is not yet established as external; see the separate report for that job. If maintainers want a turn-level retry that discards partial text, that is the enhancement space of #898, not a fix for this incident.

## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1024

The import dialog's review card showed `source · objects · record bytes` and nothing else, although `inspection.manifest.omissions` was already in the response and already typed on the client. This renders it — filtered down to what a reader can act on, collapsed behind its count.

## Owner decision this head implements

Recorded here because the thread now holds two different instructions. The owner, in a direct conversation with this bot on **2026-11-21 11:50 UTC+8**, after reading the full list of entry shapes, asked:

> 只显示A，然后默认折叠，用户点击之后才显示。并在鼠标划过去的时候对鼠标所在的条目做一些简单解释说明。

("Show only group A, collapsed by default, shown after the user clicks; on hover, give a short explanation of the entry under the pointer.")

So this head: lists the readable sentences only, starts collapsed, and explains each row on hover. That supersedes the earlier 03:43 comment on this PR (tokens verbatim, prose localized), which is what #1284 implements. The three findings in review `6002735848` are open against this head and are being handled with the owner, not silently dropped.

## What changes

- **the data is `inspection.manifest.omissions`** — the array the inspected package carries. Neither the count nor the rows is hard-coded.
- **only readable entries are listed.** That array mixes sentences a reader can act on with object references shaped `<token>:<id>:<reason>` (`cas:`, `version:`, `artifact:`, `workspace:`, `trajectory:`, `evolve:`); `readableOmissions` drops the second kind, and **the count is the number of shown rows**.
- **the rows start collapsed** behind the count; an empty array still states `0` and draws no disclosure.
- **each row explains itself on hover** via `title`, chosen by family (memory / evolve / scope / inherited / necessary / branch). Row text is verbatim; only the hint is ours.
- **no scroll area of its own**; the dialog body already scrolls.
- **a new dictionary key** `importOmissions` plus `omissionHints` in `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`; `omissionsSummary` was not reused because it counts unticked workspace files in the *export* dialog.

Untouched: the API, `packages/*`, the export path, and the rest of the import card.

## Screenshots

**Component-level render, not a full application journey.** The real `ResearchPackage` import dialog mounted with a stub client whose `/inspect` answer is one fixed inspection object, serialized from its host tree, loaded into headless Edge with the app's own stylesheets (the `.modal-backdrop` / `.modal-panel` markup is the component's own). Nothing in the frame is drawn by hand. No Electron window was involved: this environment has no display and no Playwright install, so a running-app capture was not available to me.

Provenance, precisely — the earlier version of this section claimed the images came from the head and did not say how, which the review rightly rejected:

- **after — commit `5b7754f`** (this PR's head): `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` blob `62f0c565`, `text/en.ts` blob `109bc1f3`, `text/zh.ts` blob `8a40421`, plus the rest of that commit's tree.
- **before — commit `fa6b8b8`** (the merge base with `main`): those same three files taken from it (`408ec73a`, `0851c81`, `51192f6`); every other file in the frame is byte-identical between the two states, so the pair differs only by this change.
- The `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../<sha>/shots/...` link is pinned to the commit that wrote the PNG on the `shots/1024-import-omissions` branch. That commit's tree holds the images, not the component — which is why it is not a code commit. The code commits are the two above.

All frames: 1280×900 CSS px at 2×, same viewport, same inspection object. The "with omissions" frames carry a seven-entry manifest — three readable sentences and four `<token>:<id>:` rows — and the "no omissions" frames an empty array.

**Before** (`fa6b8b8`) — the card ends at the meta line; the seven entries are not on screen:

![before zh-CN: the import card shows only source · objects · record bytes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/5d017be2943be630e18996f05183fef5fd443271/shots/1024/head-before-zh.png)

![before en: same card, no omissions line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/ff1c43ca412ef8b21746d35dfe1f1dcae253008e/shots/1024/head-before-en.png)

**After, collapsed** (`5b7754f`) — the count is visible, the rows are one click away; four of the seven entries are id-shaped and are neither listed nor counted:

![after zh-CN collapsed: 未包含 3 项 with a closed disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/9eebd58264a30213f8d6fb4fa65f05422ea547bc/shots/1024/head-after-collapsed-zh.png)

![after en collapsed: Not included: 3 items with a closed disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/71c08fdaea901d9fe468c8a7ff4cfab253b712de/shots/1024/head-after-collapsed-en.png)

**After, expanded** — the same render with the disclosure opened, i.e. what a click shows:

![after zh-CN expanded: three readable rows, each underlined for its hover hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/04612e68a897fdb4c8ab514b652b20d534bdd6f8/shots/1024/head-after-expanded-zh.png)

![after en expanded: the same three rows in English](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/00b3e885d488df5aca50abd6a3722441d9f7e33f/shots/1024/head-after-expanded-en.png)

**After, no readable omissions** — an empty array: the line states `0` and no disclosure is drawn:

![after zh-CN empty: 未包含 0 项 and no disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/6edf09c3ad25c90e34caa5564ee215349b4eb701/shots/1024/head-after-empty-zh.png)

![after en empty: Not included: 0 items and no disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/063e9aa845bf63af4ea51aecd0f404fee6a01e3a/shots/1024/head-after-empty-en.png)

**Not capturable:** the hover explanation is a native `title` tooltip, drawn by the OS and absent from a headless capture. The test pins each row's `title` instead.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop` → `tests/research-package-trim.test.tsx`: **12/12 pass**. The import case requires a `details` with a `summary` and no `open`; the mixed fixture requires the id-shaped rows to be absent from both list and count and every row to carry its family hint; the zero case requires the `0` line with no `details`.
- **Red-before-green:** with `ResearchPackage.tsx` reverted to the parent and the new tests kept, 2 fail (10 pass / 2 fail); with the change, 12 pass.
- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.
- The desktop cases are tagged `os:linux`, so a plain run on this Windows host skips them; the results above come from the same runner with the host reported as linux/amd64.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
The Idea Tree settings page had a **各阶段思考强度** block: five selects, one per stage (`发散` / `设计` / `评估` / `汇总` / `传播`), every one of them defaulting to `跟随模型`. Following the model is what a stage does when nobody picks a level, so the block only let a user move away from the behaviour they almost all keep. It is removed, and every stage now follows the research model's own thinking level.

Requested by the repository owner on 2026-11-21 (the block is redundant with the default). This does reverse part of #47, which introduced the per-stage effort, so a release note may want `release:breaking`.

Rebased onto `e4a7f8f4` on 2026-11-21T04:33Z, after #1280 (the save-row alignment) merged into the same file. The two conflicts were resolved by keeping both intents: the thinking group stays deleted, and the save row keeps #1280's `settings-actions is-end`. History was rewritten (`44a3b6e` → `6b0b2ae5`), so old review comments point at commits that no longer exist.

## What changes

The setting is removed end to end rather than hidden in one pane, because a stored map would otherwise keep overriding the model with no control left to clear it:

- **desktop pane** (`views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`): the `各阶段思考强度` group, its per-stage selects, the `跟随模型` option list and the PUT field are gone; the pane still sends exactly the fields the API accepts. `各阶段思考强度`, `跟随模型` and the per-stage names leave both dictionaries, and the page description no longer promises per-stage effort (research scope and stage prompts remain).
- **schema** (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`): `IdeaTreeThinkingRole`, `IdeaTreeRoleThinkingEfforts` and the three `roleThinkingEfforts` fields leave `IdeaTreeSettings`, `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` and `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest`.
- **api store** (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`): the map is no longer normalized, written or restored. A catalog row written by an older build drops it when it loads, and a client that still sends it does not fail its save — the field is simply not carried.
- **evolve engine** (`vendor/idea_tree`): `Settings` no longer takes the field, `role_effort` is gone, and `transport()` no longer sends `reasoning_effort`, so a stage request is exactly the model profile's own.
- **docs** (`docs/{en,zh}/reference/runtime-behavior.md` and `docs/{en,zh}/reference/cli.md`): both now describe the Reviewer as the only role with its own effort, so no reference still advertises the retired setting.

Nothing else on the pane moves: template, exploration intensity, score direction, depth, nodes, the two token fields and the three stage prompts are untouched, and the pane writes the same request shape.

## Screenshots

**Component-level render, not a full application journey.** The real `IdeaTreeSettings` component mounted with a stub client that returns one fixed settings object, serialized from its host tree, dropped into the settings dialog's own `.settings-main` / `.settings-group-detail` / `.settings-detail-header` wrapper, with the app's own stylesheets in `src/styles/index.css` order, screenshotted in headless Edge. Nothing in the frame is drawn by hand. No Electron window was involved: this environment has no display and no Playwright install, so a running-app capture was not available to me.

Two real commits: **before = `e4a7f8f4`** (main, this branch's parent) and **after = `6b0b2ae5`** (this PR's head). Both frames are 1280×1700 CSS px at 2×, **no crop** — the whole page including the `保存` row is in every frame — same language and same initial settings object.

zh-CN:

![before zh-CN: the page ends with a 各阶段思考强度 block of five selects, each on 跟随模型, then 保存](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/ab5a42da6258db492d92b94cb9206e246ff7dc58/shots/1279-rebased/before-zh.png)

![after zh-CN: the page ends with 阶段提示词覆盖 and 保存, no 各阶段思考强度 block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d562bf470bc31b414dfb7575548dd1224fa41e86/shots/1279-rebased/after-zh.png)

en:

![before en: the page ends with a Thinking effort per stage block of five selects, each on Follow the model, then Save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/acca66df1fcabacdb52777d842736df340a4fb00/shots/1279-rebased/before-en.png)

![after en: the page ends with Stage prompt overrides and Save, no Thinking effort per stage block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b8dfdf5f7c43c8e2393cd9c2fc245583daff05e9/shots/1279-rebased/after-en.png)

Both frames show `保存` at the right edge: main already carries #1280, so the pair differs only by this commit — the removed block and the page description that stops advertising it.

## Tests

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `services/api`, `apps/desktop` and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`, on the rebased head.
- `apps/desktop` → `tests/idea-tree-settings.test.tsx`: 3 passed. The pane test now asserts `各阶段思考强度` and `跟随模型` are absent, that a save does not PUT `roleThinkingEfforts`, **and** that the single action row still carries `settings-actions is-end` (the assertion #1280 added; both survive the rebase conflict).
- `services/evolve` → `tests/test_idea_research.py -k thinking_level`: 1 passed. A research asks for no `reasoning_effort`, and a legacy settings payload carrying `roleThinkingEfforts` is not carried into the research.
- `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts` is tagged `os:linux`, so it skips on this Windows host (`platform-inapplicable`); the rewritten case there asserts the retired field is ignored on write and dropped on load, and CI runs it.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1250

The desktop client had no trace of session archive: the list is fetched with `state=active`, the row menu offers only 重命名 / 导出 / 删除, and an archived Session is read-only on the server. So a Session archived in the web client **disappeared** from the desktop app — no filter to find it, no action to bring it back. This is the missing half of a feature the server and the web client already have.

## What changed (desktop only)

- **`api/sessions.ts`** — `archiveSession` / `restoreSession`, posting to the existing `/archive` and `/restore` routes and returning the Session the service stored.
- **`app/session-filter.ts`** (new) — the 活动 / 已归档 / 全部 choice, persisted under `sciencediscovery-desktop:session-filter` so a reload does not silently drop the reader back to 活动. Storage that refuses a write (quota, private mode) cannot break the filter.
- **`app/use-workspace.ts`** — the listing asks for the chosen set instead of the hardcoded `active`; `setSessionFilter` remembers the choice and re-reads; `archiveSession` goes through the existing confirm dialog, `restoreSession` does not (nothing is destroyed); and **the open Session is cleared when the new listing no longer carries it**, so switching to 已归档 cannot leave a 活动 Session's conversation on screen next to a list without it.
- **`views/Sidebar.tsx`** — a row offers 归档 for an active Session and 恢复 for an archived one, next to 导出, before 删除. While that Session is running the entry is `disabled` and the menu carries `会话正在运行，等它结束后再归档或恢复。` rather than letting the server answer 409. The three-way filter sits above the list.
- **`views/RowMenu.tsx`** — menu entries can be `disabled` (with `aria-disabled`), which is what the above needs.
- **`App.tsx` / `views/Composer.tsx`** — an archived Session opens read-only: a banner above the composer (`archivedBanner`), and the composer gated by `readOnlyReason` so the placeholder says why instead of failing a send. **The export entry stays available** — it only reads.
- **`text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts`** — both locales: menu labels, the archive confirmation (read-only **and** the scientific-environment kernel torn down with its persistent memory), the read-only banner and composer reason, the run-active refusal, and the filter labels.
- **`styles/design.css`** — the filter pill and the banner.

Deleting keeps its own dialog: archiving is reversible, deletion is not, and the two are separate commands.

## Where the consequences come from

Not invented here — the confirmation repeats what the service already does:

- `services/api/src/store.ts:6385` — an archived Session is read-only; writes throw `Session is archived and read-only`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3315-3317` — archiving tears down the Session's scientific-environment kernels with `Session was archived; persistent memory was lost`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3311-3312` — archiving is refused with `409 Cannot change archive state during an active run`, which is why the action is disabled while running.

A 409 that still arrives is shown **verbatim** (the toast carries the server's text); the client does not rewrite it.

## Not in this PR — a separate issue

`store.ts:6400-6410`: `archiveSession` stops the Session's notifications and the comment states *"Restore does not reopen it."* `restoreSession` then only clears `archivedAt`. Whether a restored Session should wake for notifications again is a product decision, not a client fix — reported separately, untouched here.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`: clean.
- `vite build` (apps/desktop): succeeds, only the pre-existing chunk-size warning.
- `apps/desktop/tests/session-archive.test.tsx` (new) plus the two existing sidebar suites: **28 tests / 28 pass** on this Windows host with the files' `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only — the tag is in the committed files and CI is the authority.
  - the three sets render with exactly one `aria-pressed`, and it is the one the workspace asked for;
  - the stored choice survives a reload, and an unknown stored value falls back to 活动 rather than hiding archived Sessions;
  - a menu entry can be inert and carries its reason;
  - the archive confirmation names read-only, the kernel teardown and the reversible/irreversible split.
- The screenshots for the archive dialog, the archived read-only Session and the three filters are being captured from this head; this description will carry them, with the harness named, before review is requested.
items.head: feat-1250-session-archive
items.title: feat(desktop): archive and restore Sessions from the sidebar

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1281

Idea Tree's per-call ceiling (`maxTokensPerCall`, default 32768, range 256–32768) is gone: the settings page no longer shows it, the API neither returns nor accepts it, and the engine sends no `max_tokens`, so a call is bounded by whatever the model and its service default to.

## What removed what

- **Schema** — `IdeaTreeSettings`, `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` and `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest` lose the field, as does `IdeaResearchSettings` (the settings echoed back with a research record).
- **Desktop** — the row and its two strings leave `IdeaTreeSettings.tsx`, `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`. The write payload stops carrying the field.
- **Configuration** — `settings-catalog.ts` drops it from `idea_tree`'s field list; `agent-metadata.ts` drops the capability field and its "bounded token" wording; `system-adapters.ts` stops offering the number field; `discovery.ts` stops summarising it.
- **Normalizer** — `normalizeIdeaTreeSettings` no longer validates it, and `resolveIdeaTreeSettings` no longer fills a default for it.
- **Engine** — `transport()` loses its `ceiling` parameter and no longer writes `max_tokens` into the request body. `_ask` keeps a 32768 reservation for the total-budget check; that is a reservation, not a cap, and the comment says so.
- **Dead labels** — the shared `configuration-ui` message maps and `apps/web`'s i18n lose their `maxTokensPerCall` entries, which nothing could reach once the field left the catalog.

## Screenshots

**These are component-level renders, not a full application journey.** The real `IdeaTreeSettings` component was mounted through the repo's own Vite dev server against a stub `ApiClient` returning the settings payload the API served before this change, and captured in headless Edge. No hand-written markup, no design mock: what you see is the shipped component and the shipped stylesheets. The Electron window itself cannot be automated in this environment.

Both frames come from two real commits: **before `2a5b51a4`** (current main, the branch's base) and **after `ea063ede`** (this PR's first head, which carries every UI/source change). Same viewport (1240×2 CSS px wide at 2× device scale), same stub payload, same language per pair. The later commit `58c5b5fb` only fixes four call sites in `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts` — no UI and no desktop source — so these captures still show this PR's UI.

Chinese — before: 研究范围 shows **单次调用 token 32768** under token 上限; after: the row is gone, token 上限 (the per-research budget) stays.

![before, zh: 单次调用 token row present](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/before-zh.png)

![after, zh: the row is gone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/after-zh.png)

English — before: **Tokens per call 32768**; after: gone, Token limit stays.

![before, en: Tokens per call row present](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/before-en.png)

![after, en: the row is gone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/4b3870d5c5b1a3e752d03e14325bbbbd1d1ddd5f/shots/1281/after-en.png)

## Every remaining `maxTokensPerCall` in the tree, and why it stays

Left over on purpose:

| Where | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts:307`, `services/api/src/evolution/{proposal,sidecar,orchestrator,preflight}.ts` and their tests, `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts:364`, `test/api/evolve-thinking-journey.mjs:147` | Evolve's **own** `budget.maxTokensPerCall` — a different per-call ceiling for the evolution sidecar, unrelated to the Idea Tree setting. Out of scope by the issue's boundary. |
| `test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json:8640` | The recorded legacy-API snapshot. `test/contract/README.md` calls the baselines **read-only for agents** and says changing one needs human review; it records what the old API answered, so the field belongs there. Not touched. |
| `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts:123` | A fixture that simulates a research record written by an older engine (`settings=dict(maxTokensPerCall=8,...)`). Kept deliberately: it is the case that shows an old record still parses. |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:551`, `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts:135–145` | The new legacy-tolerance test and the comment explaining it (below). |

Gone: the desktop page, both desktop dictionaries, the schema, the configuration catalog, capability metadata, the edit form, the discovery summary, the research record type, both message maps, the normalizer and the engine. `git grep maxTokensPerCall` now matches only the rows above.

## Upgrading from an older build

A stored settings row, or a stale client, may still carry the field. It is dropped silently rather than rejected, so an upgraded deployment reads its own catalog without a migration. `services/api/src/store/settings.test.ts` now pins exactly that: a stored object with `maxTokensPerCall: 8192` resolves to an object **without** the key and keeps the rest, and update payloads carrying 255 / 8192 / 32769 are ignored without throwing.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/schema build` clean; `services/api` `tsc --noEmit` clean; `apps/desktop` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean.
- `services/api`: `src/configuration/*.test.ts` + `src/store/*.test.ts` — **441 / 441 pass**; the three suites the normalizer touches also pass as a group (29 / 29).
- `apps/desktop`: **1352 / 1352 pass**.
- **The engine change has its own evidence**: the suite cannot run here (no pytest, no network to install one), so the test that pins it was inverted rather than deleted — `test_idea_research.py` now asserts `'max_tokens' not in sent[0]`, and locally I ran the same call against the real `transport()` with `urlopen` stubbed and read the body: `body keys: ['messages']`. That printed assertion is what stands in for the suite until CI runs it.
- **The full `services/api` suite did not complete locally**: run as one glob it stalls inside `src/server.test.ts` (observed >18 min with no progress); run alone, `src/server.test.ts` completes. CI is the authority for the whole suite, and this PR does not claim otherwise.

## Notes

- **One consequence of the reservation, stated plainly:** because the reservation is a fixed 32768, a deployment that used to set a small per-call cap and a total budget somewhere between the prompt estimate and 32768 will now hit the budget refusal where the old, smaller reservation let it through. The request itself is unchanged by this (it carries no cap); the difference is only how much the total-budget check sets aside before the call.
- Two optional review notes are left for a later cleanup rather than fixed here, because pushing to a PR already in the merge queue would eject it and discard both approvals: `test_idea_research.py:303` hard-codes `32768` where importing `OUTPUT_RESERVATION_TOKENS` would keep the test from drifting, and `research.py` carries one stray blank line before `class IdeaTreeEngine`.
- `maxTokens` (the per-research budget) is untouched, and so is every Evolve budget field.
- `maxTokensPerCall` is removed from the public `GET/PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` payload. A client that still sends it is ignored rather than rejected — the same tolerance the stored-settings path has.

## Screenshots
Captured from the real desktop page on this head: zh UI, `/api` answered by the E2E fixtures. The captured element is the Skills pane — 1074×888, from a 1440×900 viewport — so the pixels are the pane, not the whole window. 1. **Disable all in flight** — every switch and every 已停用 tag already flipped, both bulk buttons and every row switch disabled while the batch PUT is still open:

The `/api` surface is a fixture, not a real JiuwenSwarm, so this is rendered-page evidence; the real adapter under six concurrent management calls still needs a sandbox-capable CI run or a provisioned machine.

## Concurrency baseline
The adapter still toggles one skill per management call, bounded at `SKILL_SWITCH_CONCURRENCY = 6`, answering one outcome per target in request order. A page is therefore at most six rounds of management calls rather than one, so a handful of rows can settle a moment after the switches have already moved.

items.body:
Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

## Per-turn artifacts

- Groups saved Session outputs by Run using version provenance and subagent lineage, with five rows initially and an option to expand the list.

items.body:
The desktop front end had no Reviewer Specialist surface. The service writes a
review for every artifact it audits — a `reviewer_checkpoint` message in the
transcript plus an `ArtifactReviewRun` — and the desktop read neither, so a
Session could be reviewed at the Quick or Deep level with nothing on screen to
say what the review concluded.

## The verdict card

A checkpoint message now draws a card in the conversation, joined to its
reviews by `toolCallId`, so the verdict sits under the turn that produced the
artifact rather than at the end of the Session. One checkpoint can cover
several artifacts and each gets its own section; the header reports the worst
of them, and adds "N 通过 · M 需处理" when they disagree, so the clean artifacts
are not invisible behind a failing one.

Each section is framed and titled with its artifact's logical name, with the
artifact's own verdict as a pill on the right and a rail in the verdict's tone —
the same anatomy as the web client's reviewer card, where every artifact is its
own card whose title is the file name. The name is drawn for a single artifact
too: the card's header answers for the worst of several, so otherwise the file
in hand has nowhere else to say which it is. A checkpoint in the transcript is
one card per turn, not one card per file — that is the granularity the reference
uses as well.

The colour states what is trustable, not how the run ended:

- **red** — a problem with the artifact: a critical finding, or delivery
  checked and incomplete;
- **amber** — something to look at: a warning finding, a failed review, or a
  version that has been replaced and the verdict is history;
- **grey** — nothing was found wrong and nothing was claimed either: the
  checkpoint was skipped, it produced no review, the review itself declared a
  check it did not run, or a source lookup reached no conclusion;
- **green** — the level ran, raised nothing, and delivery was confirmed — or the
  review was structure-only and never claimed any delivery verdict.

`declaredGap` is a port of the server's `reviewDeclaredGap` — the rule the web
client already uses to keep a partial review out of its "passed" count. A
review whose record lists an unchecked item used to read "未发现问题", green,
while its own rows below said "未检查" for the same item; it now reads
"N 项未检查", grey. An absence is not a warning: the web client leaves the
completeness line uncoloured and colours only the label of an unperformed check.

Delivery completeness is a note, not a verdict. People name what they want
("生成一篇报告"), not files and paths, so the check often has nothing to verify
against; that is a property of the request, not a result. An unconfirmed
delivery no longer colours the card, counts as one of "N 项检查", or appears in
the header — one grey line under the rows says it was not checked. The web
client renders completeness as a sentence in the card body rather than a row,
for the same reason. A delivery that was declared and is incomplete is still a
finding, and a source lookup that never concluded still keeps the header from
saying 未发现问题.

The header counts the two apart, with the same nouns its rows use — N 个问题,
N 项提醒, or both when a review raised both. Counting every finding as 问题
promised a problem the reader could not find below. A source verdict is named
with the row's own short word (部分支持, 矛盾) rather than a sentence about it.
When a checkpoint picks its worst artifact, a review that could not confirm
something ranks above one that passed: a card whose own row says 未确认 must
not let the header say 未发现问题.

The card also speaks one language. Three rows used to print record text
verbatim: an unperformed check printed the server's English template reason, a
supported or partly supported source check printed the model's rationale, and a
delivery with no declared list said only that it could not be confirmed. The
card now says what happened and what to do about it in the interface's own
language, and the raw reason and rationale stay in the review record; only a
contradiction quotes the reviewer, because there the evidence is the point. A
row the model wrote itself — a finding's message — is content and stays as
written.

The desktop cannot import the schema's runtime (its barrel reaches a JSON
property import), so each rule is one copy with the server's tests behind it
rather than a second, drifting reading.

Expanding a card reads in the order a reader needs: findings, then the checks
that ran (the header's "N 项检查" has to have something behind it), then what the
review never looked at — an unperformed check, a source lookup that reached no
conclusion. Delivery that could not be checked is the note under them. A source service that returned no conclusion
is rendered as "来源核验没有得出结论" and the service's raw error text is not
printed: it is not a finding about the report. A source assessment that
reached no conclusion says the same thing in plain words — "找到 N 处原文，但还
不足以支撑这条结论" (or that no source passage was found) — instead of the
policy's "No issued E3 source locator is available for this claim" and a bare
locator count. "Locator" and evidence levels are the record's vocabulary; the
raw reason stays in it. The "N 处原文" count is a fold rather than a dead number: it opens the
reviewer's own account and each quoted passage with its place ("摘要 · 第 2
段"). A contradiction still prints its account inline, and a delivery the task
never named at file level now says exactly that — the task gave no file names
or paths — instead of reading as if the task had said nothing. The header reports the strongest result in the record — a
finding, a source verdict, an unverified delivery — and every such claim now
has a row behind it: a partly supported source check colours the card and is
named in the header instead of sitting under a grey 未验证交付, and a review
that recorded no delivery check draws the row that says so.

For the same reason a citation lookup that reached no conclusion is not drawn as
a row of its own. An earlier cut drew one per identifier, and a row saying
"无结论" directly above the citation-format check's "通过" read as the card
contradicting itself. The web card never draws those lookups — they stay in the
immutable review record — and the desktop now matches. What the review could
not do is still said once, as the `claim_support` gap it declares ("未检查",
amber header), which the server only drops once a lookup actually completed. A Quick review that only checked citation format says so in a note, so
a green header cannot be read as "the claims were checked". A checkpoint that
produced nothing says why — the server's `skipReason` is mapped to a sentence
that names where to turn it back on — instead of printing the enum.

Each check-category label and the level pill carry their explanation as a hover
title: "计算" is a category name, not a sentence, and a first-time reader cannot
tell whether it checks the numbers or computes them. The pill itself only names
the level (快速 / 深度); the claim behind the name belongs in the title, not in a
footer capsule.

## A running review says where it is

A checkpoint in flight draws a running line instead of a verdict. It names the
coordinator's `phase` (`quick`, `preparing`, `computation`, `citation`), which
is the only thing that separates a long Deep review from a stuck one, counts
what is finished against what there is, names the artifact in hand and how many
checks are queued, and draws a thin progress track under the line.

The counters come from whichever one is actually moving: a Quick run reports
`total: 0` with `artifactCompleted`/`artifactTotal` populated, a Deep run
reports the check counters. "Failed" counts as done — the bar says how much is
left, not how much worked. When the coordinator has not said how much there is,
the bar is not drawn and the line stays generic, rather than a 0/0 that looks
like a stall.

## The Session can ask for a review

会话设置 gains 立即审查 / 停止审查, next to the automatic-review switch and the
level. That switch decides whether a review happens by itself; this row is the
reader asking for one now, so it stays enabled when automatic review is off.
审查档位 stays open for the same reason: the coordinator reads the Session's level
for a manual run too (`enqueueManual` uses `sessionSettings.level`), so turning
automatic review off must not take away the only way to choose what 立即审查 will
do. Only the system master switch disables it, and the row says why in that case.

The click has to look like something happened immediately: the run happens in
the coordinator, and nothing pushes the new message at this window. So the
client mints the checkpoint message id, `POST …/reviewer-specialist/review`
answers with the queued `task`, that task is written into the queue state, and
the checkpoint card is drawn into the transcript at once. The server's own copy
of the message — the one carrying `phase` and the final status — replaces it
when the queue empties and one `GET` of the Session converges the transcript.
停止审查 calls `POST …/reviewer-specialist/cancel` and reports the server's
answer; a 409 (nothing active) is shown as an error rather than a silent no-op.

An automatic review has no such click, and a quiet-window audit publishes no
event at the window either: it writes its checkpoint message in the
coordinator, so the queue emptying is the only signal the page gets. The
transcript is now read at that moment for every review, not only for one this
window drew. Otherwise the automatic card stayed invisible until some later
read brought it in — clicking 立即审查 caused that read, and the automatic card
and the manual one then appeared together.

## The artifact dialog's 审查 tab

The version on screen gets its own tab with the same rows; when the version is
no longer current the verdict is marked as history and a re-run is offered. The
re-run names the checkpoint message the server accepts, which the audit queue
supplies — the dialog never invents a message id.

## The two settings layers

设置 › 专家 lists the Review Specialist as a built-in card — 审查, with the one
line 由自动审阅使用 — and nothing on that page can switch it off. That is the
shape the reference client uses: the reviewer ships with the application, and
what varies is the Session's own 自动审阅 choice, which the composer's settings
menu carries together with the level. The server's system-wide setting is still
read on Session load and on every reviewer refresh — another client can have
turned it off — and when it is off the Session's switch is disabled and the menu
says why, rather than offering a control that cannot act. The desktop no longer
writes that setting.

## The desktop E2E layer now gates a PR

The desktop browser suite answers every `/api/**` call from
`apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts`, so it needs neither the Python stack nor
credentials and can run on a pull request. `ci.yml` gains an `e2e-desktop` job
that reuses the lockfile-pinned Playwright install, `merge-gate` waits for it,
and the tier policy requires it on every profile. Documentation-only changes
skip it like every other layer, and the README now says so — the old text said
no workflow ran this suite, which is no longer true.

Wiring the gate flushed out four stale specs (a branch dialog that no longer
quotes the reply, a skill card whose source moved to a badge, two fixture
routes the app now calls); they assert what the app actually does.

The reviewer cases that can be driven through a page mock are ported from the
web journeys `journey-reviewer-result-matrix` and `journey-reviewer-localization`
and the UI half of `journey-reviewer-auto-audit` / `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.
Those web specs stay where they are: their other half asserts the service —
the coordinator scheduling an audit, feedback being consumed, records staying
identical across a skip — which runs against the real stack and has no
observable in a page mock.

## Validation

Numbers from this commit (`75e53333`) for the desktop layers. The repo-wide
layers were measured on its parent `e342e334`; the only change since then is
the 专家 page and the specs that drive it.

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop` unit (`npm test`) | 1290 passed / 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) | clean |
| Desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 174 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped at `e342e334`; the reviewer spec (14) and the two settings specs (32) pass at `75e53333` |
| CI self-tests (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 149 passed / 0 failed |
| Repo-wide UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | planned 7748, executed 7717, passed 7712, failed 5, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | planned 63, executed 63, passed 62, failed 1, skipped 0 |
| Repo-wide mocked E2E (`pnpm ci:e2e`) | planned 188, executed 188, passed 185, failed 3, skipped 0 |

The UT and ST failures do not run on this host as configured, and each was
attributed before touching anything:

- `.ci/docs-only.test.mjs`'s "mixed, non-documentation and unknown diffs…"
  case evaluates the policy script in a VM under a 100 ms budget; under this
  host's parallel load it reported `Script execution timed out after 100ms`.
  The file passes 12/12 when run alone at the same commit.
- `packages/specialist/src/bundled-references.test.ts` fails only in this
  checkout because it recurses into `.worktrees/` and opened a reference inside
  a sibling worktree's E2E data; the same test passes in a clean worktree at
  the same commit.
- `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`'s mutation case reproduces identically on
  a clean `upstream/main` worktree — pre-existing on this host.
- `packages/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` needs `bwrap --disable-userns`;
  this host has bubblewrap 0.6.1, which lacks the flag (`bwrap: Unknown option
  --disable-userns`).
- `services/api/src/evolution/evolve-thinking-entry.test.ts` never observed the
  `starting` phase its journey polls for (`expected 'starting', got undefined`)
  inside the parallel layer; run alone at the same commit it passes 1/1 in 60 s.
  A poll window shortened by this host's load, and the file drives the Evolve
  provider journey, which this change does not touch.
- `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (ST) fails downloading the pinned
  python-build-standalone release from GitHub; the host cannot reach it.

Two host conditions were prepared away before the numbers above were measured,
because they are properties of this machine and not of CI:

- The launcher suites (`services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts`,
  `source-evolve.test.ts`) write small CommonJS scripts into a temp directory
  and run them. Another user left a `/tmp/package.json` on this host with
  `"type": "module"`, so Node treated those scripts as ESM and both suites
  failed with `require is not defined`; with `TMPDIR` outside that directory
  they pass 32/32 and 8/8. CI's ephemeral container has no such file.
- `ci:e2e` refuses a port another stack already owns; 4410/4411 were held by a
  stack on this host, so the run used `SCIENCE_AGENT_PORT=4710`. CI starts
  with those ports free.

The three mocked-E2E failures were attributed the same way:

- `journey-desktop-configuration` (en and zh) could not bind port 4178: another
  agent's Playwright worker on this host runs the same suite and respawns its
  own Vite on that port within seconds of it being killed. Both cases passed
  earlier on this same host while 4178 was free (36.7 s / 37.3 s), and the
  failure arrives before the page is reached. CI runs one job per runner.
- `journey-prepare-environment`'s J3 stopped at
  `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`
  before reaching any UI — a precondition of this host's provisioning, not of
  the page.
- The earlier runs' `journey-compact-process` and `issue-143-proxy-settings`
  failures were the E2E data directory retaining a writable Skill library from
  a previous run; after resetting the layer's `data` (keeping `envs`) they pass.
  The run reported above is from that clean data.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Two surfaces, both exercised on this commit.

The desktop browser entry (mocked per-page API; no backend), 174 cases: a
confirmed delivery is green; a checkpoint over two artifacts names both in
separate framed sections, each carrying its own verdict while the header reports
the worse one; a review that never verified delivery is amber; a
review that declared an unchecked item is amber and named; structure-only is
green because it never claimed delivery; an incomplete delivery is red; a stale
verdict says it is history and offers a re-run; the eight-checkpoint Quick/Deep
outcome matrix including the two skip reasons and a reload; a running review
reporting its phase and progress; an automatic review's card arriving on its
own when the coordinator finishes; 立即审查 with automatic review off, at a level
chosen while that switch is off, queueing a deep manual review whose card
appears in the transcript and settles; 停止审查 stopping one already under way;
the built-in Review expert listed on 专家 with no switch; a reviewer switched
off on the server disabling the Session switch with its explanation; the
Session's own settings surviving a reload; the artifact dialog's 审查 tab
queueing a re-run with the right message id.

The shared `test/journey-reviewer-*.spec.ts` journeys, against the real control
plane (the mocked E2E layer's own stack), all pass in the same layer:
`journey-reviewer-auto-audit`, `journey-reviewer-localization`,
`journey-reviewer-result-matrix`, `journey-reviewer-upload-lifecycle`.

Closes #1203 — the desktop Reviewer Specialist feature request this implements.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account has no write access to apply it)
User impact: the desktop app shows Reviewer Specialist verdicts, can run or stop
a review from the Session settings, and configures both Reviewer settings
layers. The desktop E2E suite becomes a required PR check.
Compatibility and migration: none. No API or configuration change.
