recent_merged.body:
Closes #1261

Confirming a distilled Session draft wrote the Skill into a Library and stopped there: the Skills page lists the Skill **catalog**, and no Library is enabled by default, so the Skill the user had just confirmed appeared nowhere and a Session could not select it. The content was never lost — it sat in a Library version — but from the user's side "summarize this session into a Skill" produced nothing.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `baa66d05`, not taken from the report:

- `packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:1673` — `publishReviewDraft()` hands the reviewed bytes to an external publisher and deletes the draft. It never called `commitManaged()`, so nothing entered the Skill catalog.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2485` — the confirm handler's `publish` callback commits a **Library version** only (`skillLibraryCatalog.commitVersion`).
- `/api/skills` is `skillCatalog.list()` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:2456`); a Library is a separate catalog, and `enabledSkillLibraries` defaults to `[]` (`services/api/src/store.ts:348`), so a run imports nothing from it (`:1007`).
- The peer method `confirmReviewDraft()` (`packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:1638`) already did the full job — `commitManaged`, index entry, `saveIndex`, in-memory package. The Library path was the only one missing those three steps.

## What changed

`packages/specialist/src/skills.ts`

- The three installation steps move into one private `installReviewedDraft(loaded, provenance, baseRevision)`, called by **both** confirmation paths. The existing `SKILL_CONFLICT` guard for an already-installed Skill without a base revision comes with it, so a Library publication cannot silently overwrite revision 1 either.
- `publishReviewDraft()` installs the reviewed package into the catalog **after** the publisher succeeds, so a failed Library commit still leaves the draft intact (that ordering was already pinned by a test and is untouched).

Effect: a confirmed draft is now listed by `/api/skills` and selectable in a Session, with no client change — the Skills pages already render whatever the catalog returns. No UI file, no route shape and no Library behaviour was modified.

## Tests

`services/api/src/skills.test.ts`

- **New**: `a draft confirmed through a Library publication is also installed in the Skill catalog` — publishes through a stub publisher, then asserts the Skill is in the catalog at revision 1, appears in `list()`, the draft is consumed, and it survives a reload.
- **New**: `a Library publication refuses a colliding draft before it publishes anything` — installs the same id through an import while the draft is open, then asserts the publisher callback is never invoked and the draft survives.
- **Extended**: `keeps a reviewed Agent draft when its external Library publication fails` now also asserts the catalog stays empty when the publisher fails.

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` — the `swarm:required` case is renamed to `Agent-created Skill stays in draft until review publishes it to a Library and installs it in the catalog`; after the confirm it asserts `200`, the returned id, `currentRevision: 1`, presence in `/api/skills`, and that a Project created afterwards carries the id in `effective.enabledSkillIds`. The `404` **before** the confirm is untouched, so the two halves still bracket the confirm.

Both fixes are mutation-checked: dropping `installReviewedDraft` from `publishReviewDraft` turns the first case red; moving the guard back behind the publisher turns the collision case red.

## Verification

- `tsc -p packages/specialist`, `tsc -p services/api`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` (root): all clean.
- `skills.test.ts` **27 tests / 26 pass / 1 fail** and `skill-library-api.test.ts` **4/4**, run on this Windows host with the files' `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only (the tag is restored in the committed file). The single failure is `an imported script that declares an interpreter stays executable`, which asserts `stat().mode & 0o100` — NTFS has no POSIX mode bits. CI's Linux `UT` is the authority for it.
- `server.test.ts` cannot complete on this host: it reaches teardown and fails with `EBUSY … executions.sqlite-shm` while deleting its temp root, with no assertion error. I am not claiming a green run for it.

## Not in this PR

- **Auto-enabling the Library** and **listing Library-only Skills** were the alternative designs. Neither is needed once the confirmed package is in the catalog: the catalog is what both Skills pages already read, and a Skill installed there is selectable without touching `enabledSkillLibraries`. The Library keeps its role as the versioned archive.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1252

## What this adds

An assistant turn that wrote files used to say nothing about them. The artifacts lived only in the right panel, grouped by Session, so a reader following the conversation had to work out which of them came from the answer in front of them — the panel answers "what does this research hold", not "what did this answer hand me".

The data already carried the link: a `ScientificArtifactVersion` records the turn that wrote it in `turnId`, which is the `SessionRun` the transcript draws, and `AssistantTurn` already had that run id. This PR reads that link and draws the result under the turn.

![A turn that wrote a report, a figure and a dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-zh.png)

Two cards to a line, each carrying the glyph and tint of the kind that wrote it — report, figure, dataset, structure, notebook, page, LaTeX, JSON, document, other. A row per file was a table of contents under every answer; a card is one file, and two of them fit beside each other without the next answer being pushed down the page. The width is fixed by `min(100%, 320px)` in the grid: the transcript column is about 716px, so two cards and the gap fit and a third does not. On a narrow window it collapses to one column rather than squeezing names to two characters:

![The same strip in a narrow window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-narrow.png)

Pressing a card opens **the right panel's own artifact view, at the version the card printed** — not the dialog, and not the newest version. Here the report is at v2 with `已更新`, and the panel opens on v2:

![Pressing a card opens it in the panel at that version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-preview.png)

Past five files the strip stops and offers the rest, which opens the panel's artifact group:

![Seven files: five cards and the door to the rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-overflow.png)

English strings on the same three files:

![The same cards with English strings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d4b3e32e6bc6a36c7f3b69a07a032d0e525f7c97/docs/screenshots/1252/1252-cards-en.png)

## The rules, and why

**A version is attached by `version.turnId`, never by `executionRunIds`.** The schema states the rule: `SessionArtifactOutput` is assigned "to the visible top-level Run from `version.turnId`" (`packages/schema/src/artifact-provenance.ts`), and `apps/web/src/session/run-artifacts.ts` groups outputs the same way. `executionRunIds` names something else — the `ExecutionRun`, i.e. the code or shell execution that wrote the bytes — and never shares a value with the run id. The real shape is `{turnId: "run-source", executionRunIds: ["exec-source"]}` (`test/support/research-package.fixture.ts`).

**A child agent's version climbs to its run.** A subagent-produced version records the subagent as its `turnId`; the subagent records the turn that delegated it as `parentTurnId`. The walk follows that chain (children of children included) until it reaches a run the transcript holds. The lineage comes from the subagents already in the run states the conversation renders — no new request.

**A version the transcript cannot place is left out, not guessed at.** No `turnId` (an upload, a hand-registered file), a `turnId` that resolves to no run here, or a `parentTurnId` cycle: none of these is attached. Attributing by timestamp would turn project history into invented chat history; the version stays reachable from the panel's artifact list either way.

**One card per artifact, at the highest `version` ordinal — not the latest `createdAt`.** These two disagree exactly where it matters: an imported Session keeps the package's ordinals while `createdAt` can be the import time, so the newest timestamp may be an old version. The ordinal is the file's own lineage. A test pins this (`the ordinal wins over a later timestamp, which import reorders`).

**The card opens the version it names, not the newest one.** The card hands the panel the whole `SessionArtifactOutput` record, and the panel is matched on `version.id` — the identity, not the ordinal — so "the card says v3" and "the document shows v3" cannot drift apart even when the file has a v4 written by a later run. Pressing `v3` gives `v3`. The third screenshot shows it: the card is at v2 and the panel opens at v2.

**`已更新` comes from `baseVersionId` on the version the row points at.** Boundary worth stating: if a run created v1 and then wrote v2 in the same turn, v2 carries a `baseVersionId` and a file this turn created is marked 已更新. That is rare and accepted — the marker answers "did the last write derive from an earlier one", not "did this run create the artifact". Noted in the module.

**日志 has no kind of its own.** #1252 asks for logs to be folded; `ScientificArtifactKind` has ten values (`dataset | figure | html | json | latex | markdown | notebook | other | report | structure`) and no `log`. The run's intermediate output is `json`/`other`, so those two are the folded set. They sit behind the overflow card when the turn also produced something better, and are shown when they are all it produced — an empty strip reading "3 more" with nothing behind it reads as a bug.

**A later turn's version of the same file stays under that later turn.** Each turn shows the highest ordinal *it* wrote; a file amended by turn 2 still shows turn 1's version under turn 1. `limit` counts per run, not per Session.

**Nothing is drawn while the run is streaming.** The guard is the existing `run.terminal`, the same signal the rest of the transcript uses to settle a turn, rather than a second local heuristic. A list that grows and reshuffles under the reader while the run is still writing is worse than no list.

## Where the code is

- `apps/desktop/src/app/turn-artifacts.ts` — the selection: `ownerRunId` (the `turnId` → `parentTurnId` walk), kind order, the folded set, the five-row cap, and `turnArtifactsByRun`, which does the work once per `outputs`/lineage pair instead of once per turn.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/TurnArtifactStrip.tsx` — the cards, the per-kind glyphs, and the overflow tile.
- `App.tsx` → `Conversation.tsx` → `AssistantTurn.tsx` — `outputs={state.outputs}` down to each turn, `openArtifactPanel` for the overflow tile, and `previewTurnArtifact` — a stable callback (outputs and the panel's opener are read through refs) so the memoised transcript is not re-rendered by a tab switch — for the cards. `Conversation` builds the lineage from the runs and subagents it already renders and memoises the map on it and on `outputs`; `WorkspacePanel` already rebuilds its grouping on every render, and a per-turn scan would make typing in the composer cost O(turns × outputs).

## Two defects this PR fixes on itself

**The join was on the wrong field.** The first cut matched the turn's run id against `version.executionRunIds`. Those are different identifiers (see the first rule above), so on a real Session the strip would have been empty for every turn. Review caught it on `86d254ef`; the tests had not, because their fixtures set `executionRunIds` to the run id — a shape the backend never writes. The join is now on `turnId` with the subagent walk, and the fixtures use the real shape: `turnId` = the run, `executionRunIds` = a distinct execution id. A case pins the boundary directly (`a version whose executionRunIds happen to name a run is not attached by them`): with a join on `executionRunIds` added back, it fails (`16 tests, 15 pass, 1 fail`); without it, 16/16.

**The row order fell back to the version id.** That tiebreak is there so that picking one file's newest version is deterministic when two of its versions share an ordinal — but between two *different* files the ids always differ, so it always fired and the name comparison after it could never run. Seven reports written in one turn came out `7, 6, 5, 4, 3`. The order now falls back to the name, and a test pins it: with the id-ordered sort restored, `files of one kind and one version are listed by name, not by id` fails; with the fix, it passes.

## Verification

- `apps/desktop` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root): clean.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: **1270/1270**, no failures.
- New cases: `turn-artifacts.test.ts` (the `turnId` join and its `executionRunIds` boundary, no turn id, an unknown turn id, the subagent walk including nesting and a cycle, one row per artifact, a later turn's version staying under that turn, ordinal-over-timestamp, kind order, folding, the cap, name order, the by-run map) and `turn-artifact-strip.test.tsx` (no artifacts draws nothing; a streaming run draws nothing and a terminal one does; a card previews the exact `version.id` it prints rather than the newest; every card carries its kind's glyph and kind-tinted tile; five cards plus the 还有 2 个 tile opening the panel).
- Mutation checks: with `run.terminal` replaced by `true`, the streaming case fails; with the join on `executionRunIds` restored, the boundary case fails; with the id-ordered sort restored, the name-order case fails. Each passes once restored.

**What this does not prove.** Screenshots were captured against a Vite dev server serving this branch, with the desktop L2 mock answering `/api/**` — the same mock the desktop e2e specs use. Their fixtures now follow the real version shape (`turnId` = run, `executionRunIds` = a separate execution id, taken from `test/support/research-package.fixture.ts`), but they are synthetic: no real model and no real catalog wrote them. That is exactly how the first cut's wrong join slipped past both the tests and the screenshots, so a reviewer should treat the real-stack check as still owed. I could not run one here.
recent_merged.head: feat-1252-turn-artifacts
recent_merged.title: feat(desktop): show what each assistant turn produced

Closes #1253

The desktop MCP settings page could only edit a server that already existed: the form's sole entry was `setDraft(draftOf(server))`, and `emptyDraft()` was unreachable fallback filler. "Add my own MCP server" was impossible in the desktop app — which is where the local stack runs, and therefore where a `stdio` server would be launched. This brings the page to the web client's parity on the already-present routes; nothing on the server, the schema or the packaging moves.

## What the page can do now

**添加服务器.** The existing form opens empty (`emptyDraft()`) and saves with `POST /api/mcp/servers` (no id). The draft starts switched off, as an imported server does, and is reached by agents only once the user has read the test result and turned it on — testing it works while it is off, because the probe builds its own client. The created server is tested straight away — `POST /api/mcp/servers/:id/test` — and the dialog stays open with what the test found: the tool names, or the failure. That is the difference between finding a wrong command in the dialog and finding it at the next run. A refused save keeps the form and its fields on screen with the reason from the route.

**导入.** A `{"mcpServers": {…}}` spec is parsed and previewed as `name · transport · target`, then written **one request per server**. That is deliberate: `POST /api/mcp/servers/import` writes the whole spec or nothing and stops at the first name clash, so a spec of two servers would report one opaque error. Per-server requests give each entry its own outcome (`已添加` / `失败：…`) and let the valid half land.

**工具.** Each custom row expands to a read-only list of the tools the server reports (`name` and description). This is what tells the user whether adding it was worth it; the row already carried the count.

**未授权 / 授权 / 取消授权 / 清除授权.** A server whose `authorization.state` is not `authorized` says so — `未授权`, or `授权已过期` for `expired` — instead of looking broken next to a `已连接` status. 授权 opens a popup and posts `POST …/oauth/start` with this origin's callback URL (`/api/mcp/oauth/callback`), then navigates the popup to the URL the route minted; 取消授权 and 清除授权 call `…/oauth/cancel` and `…/oauth/clear` and re-read the list.

**Secrets stay unreadable.** The existing rule is untouched: a stored env/header value renders as an empty password field whose placeholder says it is stored, a rename without a value is refused before the write, and the new OAuth secret keeps the same `null`-means-keep semantics.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`: clean.
- New suite `apps/desktop/tests/mcp-servers-create.test.tsx`: **11/11** — 添加服务器 opens an empty form, posts without an id, and starts the new server disabled, then names the tools its first test found; a refused create keeps the form open with the reason; saving with no name says the name is required; 导入 writes one request per server and reports each outcome (including the refused half's own sentence); the import preview reads the transport the way the route stores it; 编辑 after a create opens the row's own fields; a row awaiting consent is re-read until the grant lands and is then tested; 授权 detaches the popup and keeps the minted URL reachable when the popup is blocked; a stored env secret is never rendered back.
- Related existing suites (`mcp-discovery-refresh`, `settings-screens`): on this Windows host 5 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. The two skipped are `os:linux`-tagged and do not register on Windows, so they are reported as skipped rather than as passing — an earlier version of this section said "skipped by their platform tag" without saying which platform, which the review correctly found does not reproduce on Linux. Across the three files on this host: 13 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped; CI `UT` (Linux) is green on `6edd132e` for the same files.
- Each fix above was mutation-checked: reverting it turns its own test red, and the file was restored afterwards.
- `vite build` (apps/desktop): succeeds, only the pre-existing chunk-size warning.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: not runnable on this host (the l1 profile targets `linux/amd64` and reports `executed: 0`), so CI is the word on it.

## Screenshots

Desktop renderer at this head, mock control plane, 1440×940, one browser per locale; the MCP routes are mocked, and every capture is taken after the assertion quoted beside it. The images live on `screenshots-1253`, not on this branch — the PR diff carries no binary.

**UI hold:** the approval for this PR needs the **code owner to look at these captures in person**. It is a UI change; a code-only approval is not enough.

**1. The page, with both entry points.** The toolbar reads `添加服务器 / 导入` (`Add server / Import`).

**3. The same dialog after saving — the first test's result.** `测试结果` names `list_notebooks` and `read_cell`, the tools the mocked test returned.

**5. 导入 — per-server outcomes.** `notebook` reads `已添加`; `taken` reads `失败：A server named taken already exists` — its own sentence, not one error for the whole spec.

DOM sample, zh-CN (row visible, every control enabled):

```

```

**7. The same row after 授权 was pressed.** `授权` is now disabled, `取消授权` appears, and the popup was pointed at the provider URL the route minted. A grant that lands is picked up by the page's poll and tested; the captures predate that poll, which changes only what happens after the consent page completes, not this frame.

## What is deliberately not here

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1265

## The defect

A provider that answers `400 … temperature is deprecated for this model` failed **every** run of that model, as `semantic-error` / `181001`, while another model on the same provider worked.

The streamed sender already had a strip-and-retry rule — strip exactly the field a 400 names, remember it for the endpoint once a stripped request succeeds — but it was **gated on the thinking-control names**, so this 400 never matched, the error was rethrown, and the run ended. `temperature` and `top_p` were in the request (the gateway copies whatever sampling the swarm sends into the model policy) and nothing could take them out.

## The fix

`temperature` and `top_p` join the thinking controls in one list of fields this sender knows how to do without, and the existing rule applies to them unchanged:

- **strip only what this 400 names** — a field the provider accepts is not dropped;
- **a value or state complaint is not a rejection** — `temperature must be between 0 and 2` and `temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled` still fail the request rather than silently changing the sampling the run asked for;
- **remember the field for the endpoint only after a stripped request succeeds**, so a fallback that itself fails (429, 5xx, timeout) proves nothing.

Two additions to the rejection wording: `deprecated`, and the `no longer supported/available/accepted` / `has been removed` phrasings, because *"is deprecated for this model"* is a rejection of the parameter, not of its value.

`rejectedThinkingControlFields` / `carriedThinkingControls` become `rejectedRequestFields` / `carriedRequestFields`, and the Settings connectivity probe (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`) uses them, so the probe strips the same fields the sender does. Otherwise an endpoint whose streaming chat now works would still be reported broken by the probe.

## Verification

New `packages/model/src/sampling-fallback.test.ts`, three cases against a stub server:

| Case | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `400 "temperature is deprecated for this model"` | retried without `temperature`, `top_p` kept, run continues, and the next turn sends no `temperature` |
| `400 "temperature must be between 0 and 2"` (with `param: "temperature"`) | **not** retried, still surfaces, and the field is not suppressed later |
| `400 "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled"` | **not** retried — a state complaint is not a rejection |

**Mutation check:** with only the thinking controls in the list, case 1 fails (`2 pass, 1 fail`); restored, `3/3`.

Wider checks on this head: `packages/model` suite **162/162**; `model-connectivity.test.ts` **37/37**; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p packages/model --noEmit` clean.

## What this does not do

The optional half of the issue — having the gateway stop forwarding sampling fields to endpoints whose models never asked for them — is not included. The client-side fallback is what makes such a model usable; suppressing the fields up front would be a second, independent decision about the swarm's defaults.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1262

## The defect

On a Session with no prior conversation, `/distill-session` still told the model to *"infer the reusable workflow from the complete prior Session conversation and execution history supplied above"*. There was nothing to infer from, and nothing told it to stop, so it went looking for the conversation: **28 `run_shell` calls walking the application's own data directory**, `turn: 32`, `totalTokens 88,824`, **0 drafts**, cancelled by hand after nine minutes.

The sibling `/skill-creator` branch in the same function already guards its missing input — *"No workflow description was supplied. Ask one concise question … do not create a generic Skill yet."* The distill branch had no equivalent.

## The fix

`skillAuthoringCommandPrompt` now takes `{ hasHistory }`. With no prior conversation the distill instruction becomes:

- **it says the Session has nothing to distil** — one short paragraph, in the reader's terms;
- **it asks one concise question** for what the Skill should capture (goal, inputs, outputs, checks) instead of inventing a generic one;
- **it forbids looking for the conversation**, naming the places the run actually wandered: the workspace, the application data directory, project and session folders, and shell commands;
- **it does not say `create_skill` yet**, so nothing half-formed lands in review.

`hasHistory` is "any user or assistant message", so a Session holding only runtime notices counts as empty. It defaults to **true**: a caller that does not know keeps the previous behaviour rather than silently refusing every distill.

The call site passes it from the messages already read for the prompt (`previousMessages`), so no extra read.

## Verification

`services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts`, **23/23**, and `tsc -p services/api --noEmit` clean.

The new case pins four things the prompt must say and the one instruction that must *not* be there — the inference sentence that caused the search. It also pins that the sibling `/skill-creator` path and the unknown-caller default are unchanged.

**Mutation check:** with the guard block removed, the case fails (`22 pass, 1 fail`); restored, `23/23`.

What that evidence does *not* claim: a unit test on a prompt cannot prove the model then makes no shell call — that needs a live run. What it does prove is that the instruction which sent the agent searching is gone and that the replacement forbids exactly the behaviour in the report.

## Deliberately not in this change

Two of the issue's suggestions are hardening around a cause this removes, and both need a decision rather than a default:

1. **A turn budget for authoring runs.** The main agent's budget is composed once per runtime (`profile.budget.maxModelTurns`), not per run, so a per-command cap means threading an override through that composition. It also needs a number, and picking one wrongly fails legitimate long distills of contentful Sessions — a product decision, not a default I should pick here.
2. **Disabling the action in the UI when the Session is empty.** `SkillManager`'s "Distill current Session" row (`apps/web/src/SkillManager.tsx:537`) already disables for "no session"; disabling for "no messages" needs the active Session's message count in that panel, which it does not receive today. That is a web-app plumbing change and a user-visible one, so it wants its own review.

Say the word and I will open a follow-up for either; I did not want to hold the fix behind them.

Add a dedicated Package workflow for on-demand distribution builds and make macOS ARM64 packaging a required part of the Nightly and Release gates. This consolidates both packaging changes into one commit based on upstream `main` and supersedes #1259.

## Package workflow

- Expose the `linux-windows`, `macos`, and `all` choices in the Package workflow. The regular CI dispatch form contains only its test profile inputs.
- Keep the Windows x64 installer downstream of the two Linux Runner SEA artifacts. The macOS DMG and ZIP build independently on Apple Silicon.
- Require each selected build to pass before `package-gate` succeeds and store the packages as Actions artifacts for build verification. The Package workflow runs L1 and the selected builders. The UT, ST, E2E, and coverage layers are skipped.

## Nightly and Release

Include the macOS ARM64 DMG and ZIP build in both gates. The job uses ad-hoc signing. Its unnotarized DMG and ZIP are retained as Actions artifacts for seven days. The Nightly summary identifies the macOS artifact. A failed macOS build blocks the draft Release even though the publish job continues to attach only Linux binaries.

## Validation

- `actionlint` passed for all four workflows, and `git diff --check` passed. Local test suites were left to Actions per the contributor's request.
- The upstream `main` ruleset requires the GitHub Actions check `merge-gate`. GitHub reported that exact name and a successful result on the [previous PR head](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44670581048/job/136074485628). The job-name expression is unchanged in this review update.

## E2E user journeys

The [Package run with `package-platform=all`](https://github.com/zhaochen39/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44686337577) is in progress on `a946f877309cb91bc4834f5adc769a8d7567f3ea`. Policy, L1, and both Linux builds passed. The [hosted macOS ARM64 job](https://github.com/zhaochen39/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44686337577/job/136121781765) passed, verified the ad-hoc signed app, and uploaded the DMG and ZIP. The Windows x64 build is still in progress.

## Review follow-up

- F1: The Windows verification step uses the same installer glob as the package upload and requires exactly one non-empty file. The contract check covers the discovery and rejection conditions. This accepts both the normal version-based name and the literal dotted prerelease name proposed in #1258.
- F2: macOS remains required for Nightly and Release. The hosted ARM64 build and upload passed on the PR head in the Package run above.
- F3: `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the CI skill now describe the Package workflow, the two gate check names, the merge queue's skipped distribution jobs, and the macOS builds required by Nightly and Release.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

Maintainers can request packages from Actions → Package → Run workflow. Scripts that dispatched `ci.yml` with `profile=package` should now dispatch `package.yml` with the desired `package-platform`.

recent_merged.body: Closes #1199. ## What changes The desktop 设置 › 技能 page gains the surfaces the web app has and the desktop did not: importing a Skill, editing one in place, reading one on its own page, and taking a package back out. Import, edit, and detail are pages inside the settings pane rather than dialogs, so the list stays one step away. - **添加技能** is a menu in the list header with three entries: **上传技能** (a `SKILL.md`, a ZIP package, or a `.skill` archive, dropped or picked), **从 GitHub 导入** (inspect the repository, then pick the packages to install), and **从零开始写** (the existing authored form). - **搜索** narrows the list on a Skill's name or description as the user types. The global switches stay above the filtered rows and still act on the whole list; a term that matches nothing says so instead of leaving the page blank. - A repository is inspected first (`POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect`) and each chosen package is imported at the commit that inspection saw, so what the user reviewed is what gets installed. Replacing an installed Skill requires `overwrite` plus the revision the user saw (`expectedRevision`); a different revision is a 409 rather than a silent replacement of an edit made in another window. Re-importing identical bytes is a no-op instead of an empty revision, and a built-in Skill stays read-only. - An inspection of a real, large repository says what it is doing and offers **取消**, which stops waiting without reporting a failure. The metadata clone has a 60 s ceiling and the checkout that fetches files 180 s; a timeout is reported as one. The scan no longer downloads the repository: it clones commit metadata only (`--filter=blob:none`) and checks out just the `SKILL.md` files (non-cone sparse), which is what discovery and the candidate list read. A package's resources are fetched only when an installed Skill has to be compared (unchanged vs update) or when the package is imported. A server without partial-clone support falls back to a plain shallow clone — and only an explicit refusal of the filter falls back: previously any transport error did, which turned a one-second hiccup into a 471 MB download (`github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills`) and made a normally 4 s inspection time out at 180 s. A transfer that broke (early EOF, `RPC failed`, reset connection, TLS) is now retried as the same clone once, and a transfer that stops moving is abandoned after 30 s below 1 KiB/s. - The checkout an inspection made is kept for 15 minutes, so the packages that follow are imported from it instead of cloning the repository once per package. Measured against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` (~471 MB, 177 `SKILL.md` files): inspection went from 29 s to **3.6 s** through the API (0.07 s to import a package whose content is its `SKILL.md` alone, 1.1 s for one with 15 resource files). Before the checkout was reused, an import spent ~41 s cloning on its own. A request for another commit, ref or repository still clones. - A selection is imported by one **background job** (`POST /api/skills/import-git/jobs`). The page returns to the list as soon as the job is accepted; the list reports `正在后台导入 n / total`, and the job keeps going when the reader leaves 设置. The job expands the retained checkout once for the whole selection instead of once per package, reports per-package failures without stopping the rest, and switches on the packages it created when JiuwenSwarm is the backend. A job the server no longer knows (a restart or its 30-minute cleanup) is treated as terminal instead of being polled forever. Same-name uploads are renamed only when the desktop asks; the route's default remains 409. - Discovery used to stop at 100 packages, which silently hid 77 of that repository's 177; discovery now lists every package the checkout holds, so no repository can be silently truncated. One inspection response carries at most **500** candidates, reports the repository's `total`, and returns a `nextCursor` while more remain. **加载更多** reads the next page at the same commit, from the checkout the first page made (no second clone); the rows already read stay on screen with their ticks, and new importable rows join the selection only when the user had kept everything selected. Candidate cards use `content-visibility: auto`, so a response holding hundreds of them costs what is on screen. Against the same repository one page is enough: 177 candidates, `total` 177, no cursor. - **Clicking a Skill opens the Skill's own page**, as OpenScience does, instead of expanding its instructions inside the card. A breadcrumb names the list, and the page carries the Skill's mark, name and source badge above its description, **文件** with `SKILL.md` rendered in a measured column, and **详情** printing the frontmatter keys the package declares (`许可证`, `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, …) as label-over-value facts, omitted entirely when there are none. At the product owner's request the page does not repeat the list's switch, a version line, or a 可用范围 block: availability is a list decision, and repeating it here only pushed the document down the page. Sections are separated by a hairline rather than boxed in cards; the instruction column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so a wide table scrolls inside the prose instead of stretching the page. - A row ends in a chevron. Hovering it opens the actions that package allows, drawn in the row's own popover and flipped upwards when the row sits near the bottom of the pane: **导出** on every package (a built-in is read-only, not uncopyable), and **编辑** / **删除** on a managed package: - **导出** downloads the installed package as the ZIP the importer accepts back (`GET /api/skills/:id/package`, built by `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` from the same files the importer reads, under the single root directory an uploaded package has), so an export can be imported again here or on another machine without rearranging it. Built-in packages export too: read-only says who may change them, not who may copy them. - **编辑** opens the editor below. - **删除** reads the deletion impact first (`GET /api/skills/:id/deletion-impact`); if a Project or Session selection still names the package it says how many and stops, rather than turning the route's refusal into a failed request. Otherwise the deletion goes through the settings shell's one confirmation dialog, which names the Skill and what removing it means. - **编辑** is a page of its own: name (read-only), description, one content editor with 撰写 / 上传, and a collapsed 高级设置 holding license, compatibility and the package's files. Reference files can be added under a chosen subdirectory (`references`, `assets`, `scripts`, …); choosing one opens an editor under its row with its own 保存文件, while the main editor stays `SKILL.md`. A non-UTF-8 pick is refused before any write. Saving sends back `metadata` and `allowed-tools` as declared (string or YAML sequence), so optional frontmatter is not dropped; a stale revision from another window surfaces as a conflict message. A partial multi-file upload still surfaces the revision it already stored. - **Uploading a package whose name is taken** is the desktop's choice, not a change to the route's contract: the desktop sends `onDuplicate=rename`, and the server installs it as `name-2`, `name-3`, … with `SKILL.md`'s name rewritten. `POST /api/skills/import` keeps its historical 409 for web and CLI callers, which omit the flag. Every page below the list replaces it and is left through the header's back control; the editor also offers 取消 in its footer, which is the same exit. The header names the page that is actually open, and the list keeps the installed count. The pages share one content measure so moving between them does not move the fields under the pointer, and they reuse the pane's existing tokens and controls rather than introducing a second visual language. A newly installed Skill is enabled when the switches are available; the background job owns that step, so closing 设置 before it finishes does not skip it. Updating an already-installed Skill leaves its switch alone, because a user may have switched it off on purpose. Closing 设置 after visiting 技能 re-reads the catalog, so the composer's `/` palette reflects the change without a reload. Backend support: `ImportSkillFromGitRequest` gains optional `commit`, `overwrite` and `expectedRevision`; `InspectGitSkillRepositoryRequest` gains optional `commit` and `cursor`, and `GitSkillRepositoryInspection` gains `total` and `nextCursor`; background imports add `StartGitSkillImportJobRequest` and `GitSkillImportJob` with `POST/GET /api/skills/import-git/jobs`; `CreateSkillRequest.allowedTools` accepts `string | string[]`; `SkillCatalog` accepts an injectable checkout so the Git import branches can be tested without a network; `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` builds an installed package as a ZIP and `GET /api/skills/:id/package` serves it as `application/zip` with a `content-disposition` name; and `SKILL_VALIDATION` now maps to HTTP 400 instead of falling through to an unclassified 500 when its message wording does not match the client-input patterns. ## Screenshots Captured at `308c08e1`, 1440×900, in zh-CN and en; the list images (`01`, `02`) and the search images were refreshed at `867b4ebb`, where the search field sits above the list. The save dialog is a native OS window, so a page screenshot cannot capture it; the export image shows the row after the write, and the E2E stubs the picker to assert the ZIP name and bytes. The detail page intentionally has no 可用范围 block, version line or switch: those were removed at the product owner's request, and availability stays in the list. | State | 中文 | English | |---|---|---| | 技能 list + 添加技能 menu | | | | Row chevron menu (导出 / 编辑 / 删除) | | | | 上传技能 | | | | Skill detail | | | | 编辑 | | | | Edit-save conflict | | | | 删除 confirmation | | | | Delete refused while a selection names it | | | | 导出 result (native dialog not page-capturable) | | | | 从 GitHub 导入 — inspection running | | | | Git candidates with ticks | | | | Git candidates after 加载更多 | | | | 技能 search filtering the list | | | | A term that matches nothing | | | | Search at 1100 px (no horizontal overflow) | | | ## What was run ### Search and rebase (`867b4ebb`) - Rebased onto `main` (`0c3d4d52`); the merge queue had rejected the previous head as conflicting after #1258. No merge commit: the 25 branch commits were replayed on the new base. - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1277 pass, 0 fail (adds the search field: typing a term narrows both lists, and a term with no match renders the no-match line instead of the empty state) - Desktop Vite against the live stack at 1440×900 and 1100 px, zh-CN and en: the field renders above the list, filtering matches name and description, the no-match line appears, and the pane has no horizontal overflow. ### After the review round (`308c08e1`) - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` skill suites — 70 pass; background-job store tests — 2 pass - `services/api` skills + import-job tests — 27 pass - full desktop Skill E2E journey — 1 passed (13.0 s) - `pnpm --recursive typecheck` — pass (all workspace packages) - `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1193 pass, 0 fail (includes a two-page repository: the header shows the repository total, 加载更多 reads at the same commit from the returned cursor, the rows already read stay, and loading more does not re-tick a selection the user cleared; the card opens the detail page and lists what the page must show; the chevron menu offers 导出 / 编辑 / 删除 only on a managed row, closes on Escape and on a press outside, exports the returned bytes, deletes through the confirmation dialog, and reports a package still named by a selection instead of deleting it) - `packages/specialist` unit tests — 10 pass, 0 fail. Four drive the real checkout against a `git` on `PATH` that answers like the transport: a broken transfer retries the same clone and never asks for a full repository, a clone that never answers is attempted again before giving up, a checkout that loses its connection is fetched again, a refused filter is the only path to a full clone, and a repository that does not exist is cloned exactly once. - `services/api` Skill suites (`skills.test.ts`, `skills-git-import.test.ts`) — 30 pass, 0 fail (includes the checkout-reuse case, a partial-checkout case that builds a real sparse clone from a local repository and asserts that the resources are fetched on import and that the second scan reports `unchanged`, a 120-package listing, a 520-package repository read as 500 + 20 from one checkout with no gap or overlap, a cursor without its commit rejected, `exportPackage` opening its own archive with the importer's unzip — the files under the Skill's root directory, the same bytes importing back through the upload path, a read-only built-in exporting, and an unknown id refused — and the lifecycle test downloading `/api/skills/:id/package` and checking `application/zip`, the `content-disposition` name, the archive's entries, and a 404 for a Skill that does not exist) - `services/api` targeted suites (`server.test.ts`, `skills.test.ts`) — 138 run, 135 pass. The 3 failures are pre-existing and environmental: `services/paper/.venv` is absent in this checkout (PDF upload test), and two subagent event-order assertions expecting a `model.usage` event that this host does not emit; both fail without this change. - `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` — 96 spec files, 0 errors - `pnpm docs:lint` — 0 issues - Live stack: `POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect` against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` returned 177 candidates with `total` 177 and no cursor; importing one package took 0.07 s. The desktop (Vite on 4178, 1440×900) drew all 177 rows and showed no 加载更多, because that repository fits in one page. Repeated on an earlier head while this host's GitHub connection was unreliable: sequential clones of the same repository alternated between 1.8 s and hanging past 120 s, and four concurrent clones all failed with GnuTLS or connect errors. The inspection ran in 4.2 s when the network answered, and 64 s instead of a 180 s failure when the first clone was cut at the new ceiling and the retry answered. ## E2E `test/journey-desktop-skill-import-edit.spec.ts` (mocked, zh-CN, desktop Vite entry on 4178 against an isolated stack on 4510): 8 steps pass. Five repeated runs passed on `d0e3e48f`, `0287aa41` passed again, and the final head `308c08e1` passed after the page layout, 详情, editor and background-import changes (1 passed, 13.0 s). 1. Open 设置 › 技能 on the desktop; the Skill about to be imported is not listed. 2. 添加技能 › 上传技能 hands the page one file; it reports the installed package by name, and the list is back through the header's back control. 3. Open the card: the Skill's own page names it, its breadcrumb names the list, it carries the description, renders `SKILL.md` under 文件, shows 详情 with the `license` the card never displayed, and the pane does not scroll horizontally. 4. From the row's chevron menu, open 编辑; the editor page is named after the Skill. 5. Rewrite 指令 and 保存; the editor reports the save. 6. 导出 from the same menu hands the save picker `.zip`; the bytes it writes are a ZIP (the E2E stubs the picker and checks the name and magic). 7. Read the package back through the API: the new instructions are installed and the `license` key the form does not display survived the save. 8. 删除 from the menu, confirmed in the dialog that names the Skill, removes the card and the package from the catalog. The menu steps press an entry with Playwright's `force`, after asserting it is visible, and the reason is recorded in the spec: Playwright's own scroll-into-view measures the entry while the popover is still opening and then moves the settings pane by that distance, which carries the row out from under the pointer; the pointer's absence closes the popover before the press lands. A person scrolls to the row, points at it, and presses; the step does the same. Every entry's effect is asserted after the press, so the skipped stability check does not weaken the journey. The Git import page is not part of the mocked journey: it clones a remote repository, which the mocked project's network guard forbids. Its paging contract is covered by the desktop and API unit tests above and was exercised by hand against the real repository (177 candidates, one page, no cursor; `加载更多` only appears beyond 500). The specialist reference test now skips the gitignored `.e2e-data/` run directory, where a partial checkout leaves `SKILL.md` without the resources those links name. The isolated stack ran locally with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_STUB_ONLY=1`; this journey never touches Evolve, so the stub-only environment does not weaken it. The journey report (per-step screenshots and logs) was produced under a local run directory outside the tree.

recent_merged.body:
Closes #1254

## What was wrong

`main` carried **`0.4.1`**, a version no release has. The only 0.4.x release is **`v0.4.0-rc1`**, and the planned next one is `v0.4.0` (#1198). The number got there from a one-line edit inside an unrelated MCP fix (`#1197` / `65299d1e`):

```diff
-  "version": "0.4.0",
+  "version": "0.4.1",
```

That field is not a label. It names the Windows installer through `artifactName`, and it becomes the exe's `FileVersion` / `ProductVersion` — the "Apps & features" line a support conversation quotes. So an installer built from `main` advertised a release that does not exist, and nothing in CI noticed, because no workflow reads the field.

The same drift left two other things behind: both README badges said `Release-0.4.0` and linked `releases/tag/v0.4.0`, **which 404s**, and the NSIS syntax-check stub still said `0.4.0`.

## What this changes

**1. `main` goes back to the release line, with one spelling per place it is legal.**

| Place | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `application/package.json` `version` | `0.4.0-rc1` | SemVer — what electron-builder and electron-updater need |
| `application/electron-builder.yml` `artifactName` | `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-win-x64-setup.${ext}` | the dot form is a *file name*; `0.4.0.rc1` is not a valid version (`semver.valid()` is `null`) |
| `README.md`, `README_zh.md` | badge `0.4.0.rc1` → `releases/tag/v0.4.0-rc1` | the tag that actually exists |
| `application/build/nsh-syntax-check-stub.nsi` | `!define VERSION "0.4.0.rc1"` | same as the release branch |

This is the repo's own documented policy, written in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh:59-61`: the dot spelling is not legal SemVer, so `package.json` takes the hyphen form and `artifactName` is pinned to the literal; at GA the version returns to `X.Y.Z` and `artifactName` goes back to `${version}`.

**2. Every payload now records the version it claims.**

`resources/version.json` carried `repoCommit` and `builtAt` but not the version, and `repoCommit` degrades to `"unknown"` when the tree has no git metadata — which is how one build came to report nothing at all. The version is one read of the shell's own `package.json`, the same file electron-builder takes its number from, so the two cannot disagree:

```json
{ "repoCommit": "…", "appVersion": "0.4.0-rc1", "builtAt": "…" }
```

**3. A version bump is now a release change, and CI enforces it.**

New `scripts/check-release-version.mjs`, run inside the **L1 job** (already required, so no new check to wire into `merge-gate`). When `application/package.json`'s `version` moves in a pull request, both must hold:

- the title starts with **`chore(release):`**, and
- **every** place the release is spelled carries the **new** number — the NSIS stub and both READMEs (badge dot form **and** `v<version>` tag link), and the artifact name as the dot-spelled literal for a pre-release or `${version}` for a final release, matching the policy in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`.

Either alone would be a door: a title is a password anyone can type, and a file set alone lets a functional PR launder a bump by nudging a README line. Together they describe `#1147`, the shape every release is supposed to take. "Carries the new number", not "was touched", is the half that matters in practice: touching `electron-builder.yml` while leaving `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-…` in place is the original defect wearing a release title. The version is also rejected outright if it is not SemVer-shaped, which catches the dot spelling with the form to use instead.

It lives in `.ci/release-version.mjs` and is computed by the **policy job** through `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, because that job is already the diff-aware one — `fetch-depth: 0` and `changed-paths.mjs` are pre-existing — and it is the only place that can read the version the PR moved *from*. Its cases carry the same `category:ut` tags as every other `.ci/*.test.mjs`, so the shared plan collects, selects and counts them. **No workflow file changes at all**: not a step in `ci.yml`, not a job in the graph, not an L1 checkout depth. Only pull requests are checked — a push to `main` and the merge queue re-verify a commit whose PR already answered. `.ci/README.md` describes the rule next to the job that enforces it, including that a violation stops the run before L1.

## Verification

Driven through the policy job's own entry point, with a real `pull_request` payload and a real base commit:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| this PR, release title | **pass** (`rc=0`), policy outputs written |
| the same tree, `fix(mcp):` title | **fail** — the title |
| a bump to `0.5.0` with the metadata left at `0.4.0.rc1` | **fail** — names each file and each missing spelling |
| a `push` event | **pass** — not checked; the pull request already answered |

Unit cases: `.ci/release-version.test.mjs`, **18/18** — the unchanged tree, the release change, the **GA shape** (macro accepted, so #1198 can ship while following the policy), a pre-release that leaves the macro in place (still rejected: the macro cannot spell the dot form), the title-only door, the stale-metadata drift, one file behind being named alone, the dead prefix, the dot spelling, an unreadable file, `dotForm`, SemVer shapes, a guard that every declared requirement is one the checker implements, the policy verdict for a pull request versus a push/merge group, the wiring call, and the checkout read covering every metadata file — which caught a real defect on the way in: the mapping still destructured the old entry objects and crashed on `undefined`.

Other checks on this tree:

- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest, including this PR's cases and the contract test that reads the job graph: **173/173**. `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 6 cases, 20 tags, 4 layers`.
- `scripts/*.test.mjs`: 121 pass, 3 fail — `check-doc-links`, `component-boundaries` and a race-contract case. All three fail **identically at the base commit `a117ae9`** in a worktree without `node_modules`, with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `markdown-it` and `@babel/parser`. They are missing dependencies in this checkout, not regressions; CI installs them.
- Not run here: `pnpm --dir application dist` (needs the full Windows provisioning chain) and `pnpm docs:lint` (needs `markdownlint-cli2`). The README change is one badge URL; the lint config enables only MD001/012/031/040/045, none of which a link edit touches.

## What this does not do

The issue's fourth suggestion — surfacing the build identity in an About window — is **not** included; it is a new UI surface and was left out deliberately. `version.json` is the identity for now, which is what makes "which build is this?" answerable without the version. Suggested as a separate change if it is wanted.

`repoCommit` still falls back to `"unknown"` instead of failing the build: failing would break packaging from a source tarball, and the issue lists that as a decision rather than a defect.
recent_merged.head: feat-1254-release-version
recent_merged.title: chore(release): reset main to the 0.4.0-rc1 line and gate version bumps

The sidebar draws `新建会话` and `导入会话` as two unrelated rows: the split holds the first, and the second sits below it with the same 18px column gap as everything else. This groups the pair — one container, `flex-direction: column`, `gap: 2px` — so they read as the two session actions they are, at the compact spacing the session rows use.

## Before / after

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-before-sidebar.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-after-sidebar.png) |

Full page, before and after:

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| ![before page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-before-page.png) | ![after page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-after-page.png) |

Measured in the renderer at both trees (`getBoundingClientRect` on the two buttons):

- **before** — `.side-new-split` is `display:flex; flex-direction: row`, the import button is a sibling of the split and starts 20px below the new-session button's bottom edge (124 → 144).
- **after** — `.side-new-split` is `display:flex; flex-direction: column; row-gap: 2px`, both buttons are children of it, and the gap is 2px (122 → 124).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — **1249 tests, 1249 pass, 0 fail** at this head.
- Diff is two files, `Sidebar.tsx` (the button moves inside the group) and `research-package.css` (the group's direction and gap; the rule that only zeroed the old margin is removed).

The shots come from the desktop renderer under the mock control plane at 1440×940; the sidebar crop is the region a reader compares, and the full pages are there to show nothing else moved. The images live on the `screenshots-1249` branch so they stay out of this diff.

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
> Sub-task of #84.

### Scope

Split the two idea-tree routers out of evolve, with their own state directory, and expose them to the agent as MCP tools.

### Dependencies

**Prerequisites:**

- #87 Adapter core: auth, connection pool, run and event log, storage and proxy framework: reverse proxy framework
- #93 Skills and skill library: `skills/:id/deletion-impact` must check idea-tree references
- #97 Science toolset as MCP: agent-side tool convention
- #98 artifact / provenance / CAS service (including papers): research references artifacts

**Depended on by:**

- #102 evolve service

### Interface list

6 in total: standalone backend 6. **0 need wrapper adaptation (approximate mapping + adapter-implemented).**

| Method | Path | Handling | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | standalone backend | idea-tree service /research/command |  |
| POST | `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | standalone backend | idea-tree service | create/get/pause/continue/end/defaults; create also writes a chat message |
| GET | `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | standalone backend | idea-tree service /research/events | SSE |
| GET | `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | standalone backend | idea-tree service /command |  |
| GET | `/api/settings/idea-tree` | standalone backend | idea-tree service |  |
| PUT | `/api/settings/idea-tree` | standalone backend | idea-tree service |  |

### Non-interface tasks

- [ ] Split `idea_tree_service` and `research_service` out of the evolve service into a standalone service
- [ ] Research stream SSE pass-through; `create` also appends a chat message
- [ ] Wrap as MCP tools for the JiuwenSwarm agent
- [ ] Migrate the TS package (tool contract and runtime), removing the `python-client.ts` layer

### Acceptance

- [ ] Every interface row in the table above has an L1 contract diff case, or is explicitly marked “no migration needed”
- [ ] Involved events have an L2 golden trace
- [ ] Corresponding E2E cases, to be added once the list of 10 cases is settled

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
## 1. Problem description `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview?defaults=1` computes **five** export profiles (`necessary`, `complete`, `completeWithTrajectory`, `completeWithMemoryGraph`, `completeWithTrajectoryAndMemoryGraph`) in one request. Two of those five walk the session's content-addressed trajectory closure, and that walk reads and `JSON.parse`s every record object in the closure. On a real session in our test instance the closure is **7 740 objects / 3 202 534 318 bytes** (5 442 of them record objects, 3 186 108 662 bytes). The frozen integrity path over exactly that closure takes **56.0–57.2 s** per profile. The five profiles are submitted through `Promise.all` but serialized on a **single global promise queue**, so one dialog open costs at least `2 × 56 s ≈ 112 s` of serial work (derived, see §5.3). The web client does not wait that long: - `apps/web/src/research-package/export-preview-cache.ts:47-49` sets `setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000)` — **without an abort reason**; - `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx:152-159` catches the rejection and calls `errorText(reason)` (`:49`, `reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : …`), so Chromium's internal string — `signal is aborted without reason` — is rendered verbatim in the export dialog; - because `preview` stays `undefined`, `files` stays `[]`, and `:235` renders `researchPackage.noWorkspaceFiles` ("当前会话没有工作区文件。") for a session that actually has **176 workspace files**, while `:243` disables both export buttons (`disabled={… || !preview}`). So a user opening 导出证据包 on a long-running session sees: two rows stuck at 正在计算大小…, then a browser-internal exception string, then a claim that the session has no workspace files, and an unusable 立即导出 button. Nothing in the server log looks like a failure — the work finishes after the browser left (2 970 × HTTP 200 out of 2 999 `defaults=1` requests in our log dump), which is why this is invisible server-side. The existing `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` contract does not help here. It is raised when `canWarm` returns false, i.e. **when a run is active** (`services/api/src/research-export-previews.ts:103`, `:119`, `:173`, `:200`), and `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1450-1452` only turns it into `202` if the client sent `Prefer: respond-async` — which the web client does (`apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts:138`) and maps to a **localized** message (`:139-151`). On an *idle but expensive* session there is no pending answer at all: the server just holds the request open for ~1–2 minutes. The gap is "slow", not "busy". ## 2. Minimal reproduction Two halves — (a) shows the server-side cost without any client, (b) shows the user-visible failure. **(a) Server-side cost, read-only, ~1 minute, no model calls** On a Docker instance with a session that has a long `agents/main:/head` history: ```bash # size the closure (read-only; uses the frozen CAS code, no writes) docker exec -i node --input-type=module <<'MJS' const { VersionStore } = await import("/app/packages/cas/dist/index.js"); const { DatabaseSync } = await import("node:sqlite"); const db = new DatabaseSync("/app/data/versioning/refs.sqlite", { readOnly: true }); const row = db.prepare("SELECT target FROM live_refs WHERE name=?") .get("agents/main%3A%2Fhead".replace("%2F", "/")); // adjust to the real ref name db.close(); const store = new VersionStore("/app/data"); const t = performance.now(); const n = await store.validateClosure(JSON.parse(String(row.target))); console.log({ objects: n, seconds: ((performance.now() - t) / 1000).toFixed(1) }); MJS ``` Observed on our instance: `{ objects: 7740, seconds: "57.2" }`, repeat `"56.0"`. To confirm where the time goes (bounded, 25 record objects / 33 MB): | call on the same objects | ms | MB/s | | --- | --- | --- | | `store.read(ref)` — read + sha256 verify | 34 | 968.7 | | `store.readRecord(ref)` — read + verify + JSON parse + dependency extraction | 517 (493 warm) | 64.6 (67.7) | **(b) User-visible failure** 1. Open a session with a long history (ours: 176 workspace files, 226 catalog file rows, 7 740-object closure). 2. 更多会话操作 → 导出证据包. 3. Within 10 s the dialog shows the raw `signal is aborted without reason`, `已选择 0/0 个工作区文件`, `当前会话没有工作区文件。`, and both export buttons stay disabled. ## 3. Expected vs actual | # | Actual today | Expected | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `AbortError` from the client's own 10 s timer is rendered verbatim (`signal is aborted without reason`) | The dialog recognises its own cancellation (`isAbortError`, which already exists at `apps/web/src/api/client.ts:86-88` and is used by chat paths) and shows localised "still preparing" copy instead of a browser-internal string | | 2 | A failed/absent preview renders as `当前会话没有工作区文件。` while the session has 176 files, and both export buttons are disabled | "unknown yet" and "empty" are different states; an empty list is only claimed when the server actually reported zero files | | 3 | A slow preview holds the HTTP request open for ~56–112 s | The pending contract is not only for a busy runtime: a preview the client cannot get inside its budget should answer `202`/`EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` (or a job handle) and let the client poll | | 4 | One `defaults=1` request computes five profiles, serialized on one global queue, and re-walks the whole trajectory closure once per trajectory profile | The two trajectory profiles should share one closure walk, and sizing should not require deserialising every record | | 5 | Server logs show 2 970 × 200 for this route | A `200` that arrives after the caller aborted is not evidence the user got a preview | ## 4. Source location Line numbers are on SD live main `8a37206be19e4f4d92f52dfa0f08873383a1d50f`, and were re-verified byte-identical on `2d9aa5d344b63b4dca55f92fc3077d0e55d2643d` at submission time (§8). Per-file git blob SHA and size at that revision, so the quoting can be checked without guessing: | File | git blob SHA | bytes | | --- | --- | --- | | `services/api/src/research-export-previews.ts` | `3a2aa07990617f337c4c0d5ee7bdbeec700aaee7` | 13 806 | | `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` | `2a0961912d52debfacd03c6ac39dec4ad5b52d5b` | 80 423 | | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | `e67d07b1d156f185f47216ed2a2959628e595120` | 259 340 | | `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts` | `776b2154c3ded335b2ca9049d44eb930960ff31f` | 20 155 | | `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` | `902c6ca9d14052e6f53ce976f87cbf4464b01353` | 141 829 | | `apps/web/src/research-package/export-preview-cache.ts` | `18dbe2e337b1cbc11f1faca864c8893af4ead40e` | 5 355 | | `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` | `c21473542c66a9f205335ece37e516dd28762d39` | 29 207 | | `apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts` | `8341fa5dccbda3c847f71e1f6a5d409b465b2f52` | 11 299 | | `apps/web/src/api/client.ts` | `b25fef29a473fb06696c922147696f7619e1fb74` | 4 403 | The lines that carry the defect: | File | Line | Code | | --- | --- | --- | | `apps/web/src/research-package/export-preview-cache.ts` | 47-49 | `const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000);` (no reason) | | `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` | 49 | `errorText = (reason) => reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : …` | | same | 152-162 | `refresh()` → `previewCache.refreshDefaults(...)`, `catch` → `setError(errorText(reason))`, re-armed every `3_000` ms | | same | 112 / 114 / 168 | `files` and `preview` seeded from `previewCache.peekDefaults(...)?.necessary`, `setPreview(undefined)` when no defaults | | same | 235 | `{!files.length ?

{t("researchPackage.noWorkspaceFiles")}

: null}` | | same | 243 | `disabled={busy \|\| scopeGone \|\| !preview}` on both export buttons | | `apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts` | 125-152 | `defaults=1` request, `Prefer: respond-async`, pending → localized `ApiRequestError` | | `services/api/src/research-export-previews.ts` | 139 / 180 | `const work = this.queue.then(async () => { … })` — one global serial queue shared by all projects, sessions and profiles | | same | 188-198 | `defaults()` fans five profiles out through `Promise.all` onto that one queue | | same | 103 / 119 / 173 / 200 | `409 EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, raised only from `assertCanCalculate` (busy-runtime gate) | | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | 1432-1436 | preview route: `exportPreviews.watch(...)`, `await exportPreviews.defaults(...)` | | same | 1450-1452 | `202` only when the caller sent `Prefer: respond-async` | | same | 4699 | 3 s `exportPreviews.tick()` | | `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` | 481-482 | `includeFullTrajectory === false` empties `entries/untimedEntries/historicalEntries` ⇒ only 2 of 5 profiles pay the closure walk | | same | 597-598 | `const bytes = await versions.read(ref); … addPreviewObject(ref.digest.slice(7), bytes.byteLength, "log")` — per-object byte read (and, for records, full deserialisation via `readRecord`) just to obtain a size | | same | 639 | `await listWorkspaceFiles(store, sessionId, true)` per profile | | `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts` | 87-89, 108-109 | `if (complete) return readWorkspaceFiles(store, sessionId, true)` bypasses the shared listing cache; scan + `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` per call | | `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` | 803, 823 | `MAX_WORKSPACE_SCAN_FILES = 500`; `scanWorkspaceWithStatus` (readdir + stat, no content read) | ## 5. Runtime evidence Instance: Docker test container (`jd-fresh-test-sciencediscovery-1`, `restart: on-failure`, **no CPU or memory limit set** — `NanoCpus=0`, `CpuQuota=0`, `Memory=0`; Docker Desktop VM with 31.35 GiB and 24 visible CPUs), API on 4310 (host 4320), no model calls involved in these measurements. Data read read-only (`file:…?mode=ro`, `docker exec … node --input-type=module < script`, nothing written into the audited data volume by these probes). **5.1 Single-profile cost — RECORDED (direct measurement, frozen code path)** | measurement | value | | --- | --- | | `VersionStore.validateClosure(agents/main:/head)` | **57.223 s**, repeat **56.042 s** (56 MB/s) | | same closure, BFS replica via `readRecord` | 55.539 s | | closure size | 7 740 objects / 3 202 534 318 bytes / 5 442 records (3 186 108 662 record bytes) | | a 191-object / 4.67 MB closure (workspace tree head) | 55 ms | | a 1 006-object / 430.7 MB closure (subagent head) | 6.44 s | | a 1-object closure | 12 ms | **5.2 Where the time goes — RECORDED on a bounded sample, cross-checked against 5.1** | arm | rate | extrapolated over the closure | | --- | --- | --- | | `store.read` (read + sha256) — 60-object size-stratified fit `a=0.208 ms/object, b=0.844 ms/MB` | 968.7 MB/s | ≈ 4.3 s | | `store.readRecord` (+ JSON parse + dependency extraction) — 25 records / 33.4 MB | 64.6 / 67.7 MB/s ⇒ 15.48 ms/MB | ≈ 49.3 s | | **sum 53.6 s vs directly measured 56.0–57.2 s** | — | agrees within **6 %** | The cost is dominated by deserialising ~3.19 GB of record JSON, not by disk IO. This is the same mechanism that exhausted the heap in #1085. **5.3 Five profiles in one request — DERIVED** `defaults()` submits five profiles; two carry the trajectory closure; all five go through one serial queue ⇒ `≥ 2 × 56.0 s ≈ 112 s` of serial server work per dialog open. The client budget is 10 s ⇒ a factor of ~11; raising it to 60 s would still leave the request at ~0.5× of the required time, which is why "just increase the timeout" is not a fix. Note also that an aborted HTTP request does not cancel the server-side computation, so each retry adds queued work. **5.4 What is NOT the driver — RECORDED (negative results)** | candidate | result | | --- | --- | | workspace file count | 176 files scan = 8.77 / 10.04 / 15.81 ms (`Infinity` limit), 8.56–9.45 ms at the default limit; a raw readdir+stat replica = 7.19–8.40 ms; a 14 932-file tree = 640–684 ms. Five profiles × scan = 45–110 ms, i.e. **<0.1 %** of 112 s. Real defect, immaterial latency. | | `/app/node_modules` in the scan | correctly ignored (25 512 files on disk, 8 returned) | | memory-graph export | `duration_ms=0`, 1.9 MB store | | concurrency contention | interval-overlap count vs elapsedMs over 32 samples: Pearson **r = −0.465** → rejected | | session/closure scale vs the logged `workspace_snapshot` samples | ρ = 0.275, r ≈ −0.14…−0.03 → rejected, because those samples are censored: `recordingStage` logs `completed` only when `tracing \|\| slow \|\| aborted` with `slowAfterMs = 30_000`, so every logged sample is structurally ≥ 30 s and cannot measure a fast snapshot | | server errors on this path | none. The route answers 200/202. `/app/data/logs/api.log` (span 2026-11-11T23:44:17Z → 2026-11-12T13:21:56Z, 2 540 lines) holds 2 028 `http_request_failed` lines = 2 023 × `statusCode=401` and 6 × `statusCode=404`; **0** of them mention `research-package` or `preview`. | **5.5 Not measured (and why)** - **Queue wait with an active run**: creating a run writes into the audited instance, which was out of scope for this read-only audit. The mechanism is stated from code (§1, `assertCanCalculate` → `canWarm` → `409`), not from a measurement. - **End-to-end wall time of one `defaults=1` request**: the server log carries no duration field for this route, and measuring it live would enqueue real preview work on the audited instance. - **A full closure-size growth series**: single point plus two smaller real closures (§5.1). ## 6. Impact - 导出证据包 is unusable on long-trajectory sessions from the web client: the size estimate never arrives, and the buttons stay disabled. - The user is shown a browser-internal exception string and a false statement that the session has no workspace files — the two most misleading things this dialog can say. - Every dialog open (and the 3 s re-arm) enqueues five profiles on one global queue, which also delays other sessions' previews and background `tick()` warms. - Server-side observability is misleading: the route reports 200 for work that finished after the caller gave up. - This is the same cost mechanism behind #1085's heap exhaustion; #1085 removed the *trigger* (warming on a plain session read, commit `5fc09fc8`) but not the per-request cost, so it can still be reached from the dialog itself. ## 7. Suggested fix direction Ordered to match what the user actually sees; none of these is a timeout bump. 1. **P0 — treat the client's own cancellation as cancellation.** Use the existing `isAbortError(reason)` helper in `ResearchPackageActions.tsx`, and give the abort a reason (`controller.abort(new Error("preview-budget-expired"))`) so nothing can leak a browser string. 2. **P0 — never render "no workspace files" from an unknown.** Keep the empty-state only when the server returned `files: []` for a successful preview; render a distinct "scope not determined yet" state otherwise, and keep export reachable through the existing background/async path. 3. **P1 — make "slow" answer like "busy" does.** Reuse the `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` / `respond-async` contract (already implemented end-to-end) for a preview that will not finish inside a budget, instead of holding the request open; or make `defaults=1` return the requested profile only and let the other four be computed lazily when the user changes the switches. 4. **P1 — one closure walk per request, shared by the profiles that need it.** The two trajectory profiles currently walk the same 3.20 GB closure independently. 5. **P1 — drop the single global serial queue** (or make it per-session/per-project) so one session's five profiles do not serialise, and do not serialise behind other sessions. 6. **P1 — size without deserialising.** `addPreviewObject(..., bytes.byteLength, "log")` needs a length, not a parsed object: `stat`/`ref.size` gives it, and the dependency walk could read the record's dependency list only. At 968.7 MB/s vs 64.6 MB/s this turns ~56 s into a few seconds. 7. **P2 — scale-aware budget/cache policy** (e.g. derive the client budget from a cheap closure-size probe, or keep the previous revision's estimate visible while recomputing). 8. Related but separate: `complete` previews bypass the shared listing cache and re-run `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` five times per dialog open — five directory *writes* to produce one read-only estimate. The write-side consequence is filed separately as #1125; here it only matters as redundant work. ## 8. Version note - Anchors and all quoted code are on **SD live main `8a37206be19e4f4d92f52dfa0f08873383a1d50f`** (per-file git blob SHA and size recorded in §4). - Re-verified at submission time (2026-11-12T13:42Z) against **`2d9aa5d344b63b4dca55f92fc3077d0e55d2643d`**, which is one commit ahead of that baseline. The newer commit is the #1125 fix (`fix(api): record the delivered file's own mtime so a listing cannot demote it`) and touches `agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts`, `artifacts/materialize.ts`, `artifacts/materialize.test.ts`, `remote-runner.ts`, `subagents/index.ts`. All nine anchor files above are **byte-identical** between the two revisions (git blob SHA and size compared per file), so the defect is live on current main and every line number quoted here still applies. - **Merged PR #1035** (2026-11-10, `fix(research): prevent export preview OOM and finalize excluded-cache executions`) already rewrote parts of `research-export-previews.ts` (+65 −9) and `research-snapshots.ts` (+61 −26) to bound preview memory — streaming CAS validation, incremental trajectory measurement, memoized JSON byte counts, cancellation on scope deletion/shutdown. Its merge commit `1aeb6598ad05c2692b3ab58d04c16b44ad1f57a0` is an **ancestor** of the baseline used here (`compare` status `ahead`, 172 commits), so every number in §5 was measured **with #1035 already applied**. #1035 addressed the heap ceiling; the ~56 s per-profile duration, the per-object sizing reads at `research-snapshots.ts:597-598`, the one global serial queue and the 10 s reason-less client abort are all outside what it changed. - Open-duplicate check at submission time: 85 open issues (title-filtered on export / package / preview / trajectory / research / timeout / abort / performance / slow) plus the changed-file list of all 35 open PRs filtered against the nine anchor paths. The only open PR touching this area is #1136 (`Preserve Evolve candidate sources in research packages`, `research-snapshots.ts` +82 −5), which extends what an export contains — it does not change how expensive computing a preview is. - Measurements were taken on a Docker test instance built from our fork tip `30178fda7`, which is behind main by `5fc09fc8` (the #1085 fix). Everything cited above exists on main independently of that commit; the session-read warming is explicitly *not* claimed as a live main defect. - Relation to existing issues: - **#1085 / PR #1086 (closed)** — same cost mechanism, different trigger; that fix removed the plain-session-read warm and reduced the background warm to one profile. The per-request five-profile cost and the client-side error handling are untouched. - **#1079, #1083 (closed)** — `complete` + full trajectory failures reported as bare `404`s, with no root cause claimed in either report. This issue is about the *cost* path and the web client's 10 s budget, a different symptom (a held-open request, not a 404). - **#1099 / PR #1103 (closed)** — mapped a preview `ENOENT` race onto the pending contract; the remaining gap is that "slow" has no pending answer at all (§1). - **#1013 (closed)** — bounded the export/copy *task* polls; the *preview* abort path is separate. - **#1024 (open, feature)** — desktop-first export UI redesign (honest size, pending explanation, durable export center). It asks for the presentation half; this issue is the server-side cost and the web client's error handling, and is reproducible without any UI redesign. - What is *not* established here: no end-to-end `defaults=1` wall-clock measurement, no active-run queue-wait measurement (both would have written to the audited instance), and therefore no claim about the exact total a user waits — only that one profile's closure walk is 56 s and two of five profiles perform it behind one serial queue.
