Desktop users need Web to manage execution resources and inspect model usage. This brings those capabilities into Desktop's existing settings layout, makes environments clearly belong to a Runner, and adds compact token statistics both in settings and below conversation replies.

Closes #1220.

The release-version CI correction is tracked separately in #1269; this PR's diff contains no release-gate changes.

## Changes

- Combine remote machines and scientific environments into Runtime environments. The overview contains registered Runners and global Conda/Pip sources; Runner details contain connection, resources and environment management. Package sources save quietly, and environment creation uses creation-specific feedback.
- Add execution quotas, JiuwenSwarm paid-search credentials and webpage-fetch selection, and network proxy configuration. DeepSeek search/fetch share a key. Proxy selection, connection testing and bypass editing use compact grouped controls; custom proxy URLs can be viewed and edited.
- Add deployment-wide model usage with date filters, total/input/output tokens and a flat model table. Below each finished conversation turn, add a token badge with an expandable model/token breakdown. Omit unreported fields and avoid counting cache or reasoning tokens twice.
- Record JiuwenSwarm task usage at the model gateway before SDK defaults can turn missing reasoning into zero. Keep platform main/child accounting separate and ignore duplicate SDK reports. Existing usage records are not rewritten.
- Remove project Runner selection from system settings. Unspecified selection follows the registered Runner catalog dynamically; explicit selections and admission restrictions remain enforced. No session Runner picker is introduced.

Analytics reporting fields are additive; exchange rates remain enabled by default for existing clients. Existing Web settings remain available. Dormant DeepSeek credentials require an explicit re-save to enable search rather than being silently activated.

## Validation

Focused checks performed during implementation:

- Runtime-settings browser journeys: **14 mocked-backend Playwright cases passed**, including registration, detail navigation, connection/resources, credentials, deletion, NPU selection, and no project-availability writes. Both real-backend Runner cases were updated and successfully collected (not executed); targeted TypeScript checking of both specifications and their imported helpers passed.

- Resource/settings regressions: **156 passed, 0 failed** (Desktop 116, schema/API 38, focused store 2).
- Conversation and per-turn usage regressions: **150 passed, 0 failed**, including existing transcript/configuration behavior; follow-up usage-label checks: **6 passed**.
- JiuwenSwarm gateway, agent, orchestration and usage-accounting regressions: **240 passed, 0 failed**.
- Latest bypass-layout change: **1 focused save regression passed**. Affected-package type checks, targeted test type checks, and Desktop/API builds passed during implementation; `git diff --check` passed.
- CI regression checks: **8 app-model-setup render scenarios, 6 turn-usage tests, and 16 analytics tests passed**; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passed. App fixtures include the session usage endpoint, and analytics fixtures supply the required context maps.
- Runner-selection review regressions: **35 Web, 14 schema/API, and 28 Desktop tests passed**. Catalog loading cannot seed a partial override; unspecified availability does not imply an existing remote workspace. Web/API/Desktop and shared test type checks passed.
- Verified in a disposable worktree that all 16 feature commits can be rebased onto upstream main `f10ac0fe` without conflicts. The published branch history is preserved.

The browser capture below verifies rendering and navigation in both interface languages against an existing JiuwenSwarm backend. It does not exercise settings writes or paid model calls. Full local UT/ST/E2E gates and native Electron platform checks were not run; the current Actions run reports CI results.

## Screenshots

Captured from Desktop frontend `6bdfda513` on 2026-11-19, in Simplified Chinese and English. Host identifiers and local paths are redacted only in the browser presentation; settings were not changed. The conversation images isolate an existing short test exchange and retain its original reply text and recorded token figures in both interface languages.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1262

## The defect

On a Session with no prior conversation, `/distill-session` still told the model to *"infer the reusable workflow from the complete prior Session conversation and execution history supplied above"*. There was nothing to infer from, and nothing told it to stop, so it went looking for the conversation: **28 `run_shell` calls walking the application's own data directory**, `turn: 32`, `totalTokens 88,824`, **0 drafts**, cancelled by hand after nine minutes.

The sibling `/skill-creator` branch in the same function already guards its missing input — *"No workflow description was supplied. Ask one concise question … do not create a generic Skill yet."* The distill branch had no equivalent.

## The fix

`skillAuthoringCommandPrompt` now takes `{ hasHistory }`. With no prior conversation the distill instruction becomes:

- **it says the Session has nothing to distil** — one short paragraph, in the reader's terms;
- **it asks one concise question** for what the Skill should capture (goal, inputs, outputs, checks) instead of inventing a generic one;
- **it forbids looking for the conversation**, naming the places the run actually wandered: the workspace, the application data directory, project and session folders, and shell commands;
- **it does not say `create_skill` yet**, so nothing half-formed lands in review.

`hasHistory` is "any user or assistant message", so a Session holding only runtime notices counts as empty. It defaults to **true**: a caller that does not know keeps the previous behaviour rather than silently refusing every distill.

The call site passes it from the messages already read for the prompt (`previousMessages`), so no extra read.

## Verification

`services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts`, **23/23**, and `tsc -p services/api --noEmit` clean.

The new case pins four things the prompt must say and the one instruction that must *not* be there — the inference sentence that caused the search. It also pins that the sibling `/skill-creator` path and the unknown-caller default are unchanged.

**Mutation check:** with the guard block removed, the case fails (`22 pass, 1 fail`); restored, `23/23`.

What that evidence does *not* claim: a unit test on a prompt cannot prove the model then makes no shell call — that needs a live run. What it does prove is that the instruction which sent the agent searching is gone and that the replacement forbids exactly the behaviour in the report.

## Deliberately not in this change

Two of the issue's suggestions are hardening around a cause this removes, and both need a decision rather than a default:

1. **A turn budget for authoring runs.** The main agent's budget is composed once per runtime (`profile.budget.maxModelTurns`), not per run, so a per-command cap means threading an override through that composition. It also needs a number, and picking one wrongly fails legitimate long distills of contentful Sessions — a product decision, not a default I should pick here.
2. **Disabling the action in the UI when the Session is empty.** `SkillManager`'s "Distill current Session" row (`apps/web/src/SkillManager.tsx:537`) already disables for "no session"; disabling for "no messages" needs the active Session's message count in that panel, which it does not receive today. That is a web-app plumbing change and a user-visible one, so it wants its own review.

Say the word and I will open a follow-up for either; I did not want to hold the fix behind them.

A functional PR based on an older main can fail `Select CI policy` after main changes the release version. The policy compares the event's recorded base version with the checked-out synthetic merge, so main's `0.4.1 -> 0.4.0-rc1` reset is attributed to a feature that never edited the version. This blocked #1221 after #1258 landed.

Compare the checked-out version with the first parent of the tested PR merge, which is the target revision actually used. Verify that the checkout has exactly two parents and its second parent equals `pull_request.head.sha`; a raw branch or unrelated merge fails explicitly. Existing release-title and metadata requirements still apply when the candidate actually changes the version.

This is the CI-only follow-up to #1258, extracted from #1221 as requested in its review. The diff contains only `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` and `.ci/release-version.test.mjs`.

## Validation

- `node --test .ci/release-version.test.mjs .ci/test-layers.test.mjs`: **36 passed, 0 failed** on this branch (27 version-policy tests and 9 existing layer tests).
- Real temporary Git histories cover an old PR inheriting main's version change and a functional PR that really changes the version. Invalid checkout topology and mismatched PR heads are rejected.
- The inherited-version regression reproduced the original rejection before the fix. The fixed policy also accepts the exact failed #1221 merge `6f9f56fbb294988c79f639b9b7c763fb1aa42797`.
- `git diff --check` passed; the branch is based directly on current main `0c3d4d52`.

Release category: `release:fix`.

Add a dedicated Package workflow for on-demand distribution builds and make macOS ARM64 packaging a required part of the Nightly and Release gates. This consolidates both packaging changes into one commit based on upstream `main` and supersedes #1259.

## Package workflow

- Expose the `linux-windows`, `macos`, and `all` choices in the Package workflow. The regular CI dispatch form contains only its test profile inputs.
- Keep the Windows x64 installer downstream of the two Linux Runner SEA artifacts. The macOS DMG and ZIP build independently on Apple Silicon.
- Require each selected build to pass before `package-gate` succeeds and store the packages as Actions artifacts for build verification. The Package workflow runs L1 and the selected builders. The UT, ST, E2E, and coverage layers are skipped.

## Nightly and Release

Include the macOS ARM64 DMG and ZIP build in both gates. The job uses ad-hoc signing. Its unnotarized DMG and ZIP are retained as Actions artifacts for seven days. The Nightly summary identifies the macOS artifact. A failed macOS build blocks the draft Release even though the publish job continues to attach only Linux binaries.

## Validation

- `actionlint` passed for all four workflows, and `git diff --check` passed. Local test suites were left to Actions per the contributor's request.
- The upstream `main` ruleset requires the GitHub Actions check `merge-gate`. GitHub reported that exact name and a successful result on the [previous PR head](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44670581048/job/136074485628). The job-name expression is unchanged in this review update.

## E2E user journeys

The [Package run with `package-platform=all`](https://github.com/zhaochen39/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44686337577) is in progress on `a946f877309cb91bc4834f5adc769a8d7567f3ea`. Policy, L1, and both Linux builds passed. The [hosted macOS ARM64 job](https://github.com/zhaochen39/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44686337577/job/136121781765) passed, verified the ad-hoc signed app, and uploaded the DMG and ZIP. The Windows x64 build is still in progress.

## Review follow-up

- F1: The Windows verification step uses the same installer glob as the package upload and requires exactly one non-empty file. The contract check covers the discovery and rejection conditions. This accepts both the normal version-based name and the literal dotted prerelease name proposed in #1258.
- F2: macOS remains required for Nightly and Release. The hosted ARM64 build and upload passed on the PR head in the Package run above.
- F3: `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the CI skill now describe the Package workflow, the two gate check names, the merge queue's skipped distribution jobs, and the macOS builds required by Nightly and Release.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

Maintainers can request packages from Actions → Package → Run workflow. Scripts that dispatched `ci.yml` with `profile=package` should now dispatch `package.yml` with the desired `package-platform`.

recent_merged.body: Closes #1199. ## What changes The desktop 设置 › 技能 page gains the surfaces the web app has and the desktop did not: importing a Skill, editing one in place, reading one on its own page, and taking a package back out. Import, edit, and detail are pages inside the settings pane rather than dialogs, so the list stays one step away. - **添加技能** is a menu in the list header with three entries: **上传技能** (a `SKILL.md`, a ZIP package, or a `.skill` archive, dropped or picked), **从 GitHub 导入** (inspect the repository, then pick the packages to install), and **从零开始写** (the existing authored form). - **搜索** narrows the list on a Skill's name or description as the user types. The global switches stay above the filtered rows and still act on the whole list; a term that matches nothing says so instead of leaving the page blank. - A repository is inspected first (`POST /api/skills/import-git/inspect`) and each chosen package is imported at the commit that inspection saw, so what the user reviewed is what gets installed. Replacing an installed Skill requires `overwrite` plus the revision the user saw (`expectedRevision`); a different revision is a 409 rather than a silent replacement of an edit made in another window. Re-importing identical bytes is a no-op instead of an empty revision, and a built-in Skill stays read-only. - An inspection of a real, large repository says what it is doing and offers **取消**, which stops waiting without reporting a failure. The metadata clone has a 60 s ceiling and the checkout that fetches files 180 s; a timeout is reported as one. The scan no longer downloads the repository: it clones commit metadata only (`--filter=blob:none`) and checks out just the `SKILL.md` files (non-cone sparse), which is what discovery and the candidate list read. A package's resources are fetched only when an installed Skill has to be compared (unchanged vs update) or when the package is imported. A server without partial-clone support falls back to a plain shallow clone — and only an explicit refusal of the filter falls back: previously any transport error did, which turned a one-second hiccup into a 471 MB download (`github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills`) and made a normally 4 s inspection time out at 180 s. A transfer that broke (early EOF, `RPC failed`, reset connection, TLS) is now retried as the same clone once, and a transfer that stops moving is abandoned after 30 s below 1 KiB/s. - The checkout an inspection made is kept for 15 minutes, so the packages that follow are imported from it instead of cloning the repository once per package. Measured against `github.com/k-dense-ai/scientific-agent-skills` (~471 MB, 177 `SKILL.md` files): inspection went from 29 s to **3.6 s** through the API (0.07 s to import a package whose content is its `SKILL.md` alone, 1.1 s for one with 15 resource files). Before the checkout was reused, an import spent ~41 s cloning on its own. A request for another commit, ref or repository still clones. - A selection is imported by one **background job** (`POST /api/skills/import-git/jobs`). The page returns to the list as soon as the job is accepted; the list reports `正在后台导入 n / total`, and the job keeps going when the reader leaves 设置. The job expands the retained checkout once for the whole selection instead of once per package, reports per-package failures without stopping the rest, and switches on the packages it created when JiuwenSwarm is the backend. A job the server no longer knows (a restart or its 30-minute cleanup) is treated as terminal instead of being polled forever. Same-name uploads are renamed only when the desktop asks; the route's default remains 409. - Discovery used to stop at 100 packages, which silently hid 77 of that repository's 177; discovery now lists every package the checkout holds, so no repository can be silently truncated. One inspection response carries at most **500** candidates, reports the repository's `total`, and returns a `nextCursor` while more remain. **加载更多** reads the next page at the same commit, from the checkout the first page made (no second clone); the rows already read stay on screen with their ticks, and new importable rows join the selection only when the user had kept everything selected. Candidate cards use `content-visibility: auto`, so a response holding hundreds of them costs what is on screen. Against the same repository one page is enough: 177 candidates, `total` 177, no cursor. - **Clicking a Skill opens the Skill's own page**, as OpenScience does, instead of expanding its instructions inside the card. A breadcrumb names the list, and the page carries the Skill's mark, name and source badge above its description, **文件** with `SKILL.md` rendered in a measured column, and **详情** printing the frontmatter keys the package declares (`许可证`, `allowed-tools`, `compatibility`, …) as label-over-value facts, omitted entirely when there are none. At the product owner's request the page does not repeat the list's switch, a version line, or a 可用范围 block: availability is a list decision, and repeating it here only pushed the document down the page. Sections are separated by a hairline rather than boxed in cards; the instruction column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so a wide table scrolls inside the prose instead of stretching the page. - A row ends in a chevron. Hovering it opens the actions that package allows, drawn in the row's own popover and flipped upwards when the row sits near the bottom of the pane: **导出** on every package (a built-in is read-only, not uncopyable), and **编辑** / **删除** on a managed package: - **导出** downloads the installed package as the ZIP the importer accepts back (`GET /api/skills/:id/package`, built by `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` from the same files the importer reads, under the single root directory an uploaded package has), so an export can be imported again here or on another machine without rearranging it. Built-in packages export too: read-only says who may change them, not who may copy them. - **编辑** opens the editor below. - **删除** reads the deletion impact first (`GET /api/skills/:id/deletion-impact`); if a Project or Session selection still names the package it says how many and stops, rather than turning the route's refusal into a failed request. Otherwise the deletion goes through the settings shell's one confirmation dialog, which names the Skill and what removing it means. - **编辑** is a page of its own: name (read-only), description, one content editor with 撰写 / 上传, and a collapsed 高级设置 holding license, compatibility and the package's files. Reference files can be added under a chosen subdirectory (`references`, `assets`, `scripts`, …); choosing one opens an editor under its row with its own 保存文件, while the main editor stays `SKILL.md`. A non-UTF-8 pick is refused before any write. Saving sends back `metadata` and `allowed-tools` as declared (string or YAML sequence), so optional frontmatter is not dropped; a stale revision from another window surfaces as a conflict message. A partial multi-file upload still surfaces the revision it already stored. - **Uploading a package whose name is taken** is the desktop's choice, not a change to the route's contract: the desktop sends `onDuplicate=rename`, and the server installs it as `name-2`, `name-3`, … with `SKILL.md`'s name rewritten. `POST /api/skills/import` keeps its historical 409 for web and CLI callers, which omit the flag. Every page below the list replaces it and is left through the header's back control; the editor also offers 取消 in its footer, which is the same exit. The header names the page that is actually open, and the list keeps the installed count. The pages share one content measure so moving between them does not move the fields under the pointer, and they reuse the pane's existing tokens and controls rather than introducing a second visual language. A newly installed Skill is enabled when the switches are available; the background job owns that step, so closing 设置 before it finishes does not skip it. Updating an already-installed Skill leaves its switch alone, because a user may have switched it off on purpose. Closing 设置 after visiting 技能 re-reads the catalog, so the composer's `/` palette reflects the change without a reload. Backend support: `ImportSkillFromGitRequest` gains optional `commit`, `overwrite` and `expectedRevision`; `InspectGitSkillRepositoryRequest` gains optional `commit` and `cursor`, and `GitSkillRepositoryInspection` gains `total` and `nextCursor`; background imports add `StartGitSkillImportJobRequest` and `GitSkillImportJob` with `POST/GET /api/skills/import-git/jobs`; `CreateSkillRequest.allowedTools` accepts `string | string[]`; `SkillCatalog` accepts an injectable checkout so the Git import branches can be tested without a network; `SkillCatalog.exportPackage` builds an installed package as a ZIP and `GET /api/skills/:id/package` serves it as `application/zip` with a `content-disposition` name; and `SKILL_VALIDATION` now maps to HTTP 400 instead of falling through to an unclassified 500 when its message wording does not match the client-input patterns. ## Screenshots Captured at `308c08e1`, 1440×900, in zh-CN and en; the list images (`01`, `02`) and the search images were refreshed at `867b4ebb`, where the search field sits above the list. The save dialog is a native OS window, so a page screenshot cannot capture it; the export image shows the row after the write, and the E2E stubs the picker to assert the ZIP name and bytes. The detail page intentionally has no 可用范围 block, version line or switch: those were removed at the product owner's request, and availability stays in the list. | State | 中文 | English | |---|---|---| | 技能 list + 添加技能 menu | | | | Row chevron menu (导出 / 编辑 / 删除) | | | | 上传技能 | | | | Skill detail | | | | 编辑 | | | | Edit-save conflict | | | | 删除 confirmation | | | | Delete refused while a selection names it | | | | 导出 result (native dialog not page-capturable) | | | | 从 GitHub 导入 — inspection running | | | | Git candidates with ticks | | | | Git candidates after 加载更多 | | | | 技能 search filtering the list | | | | A term that matches nothing | | | | Search at 1100 px (no horizontal overflow) | | | ## What was run ### Search and rebase (`867b4ebb`) - Rebased onto `main` (`0c3d4d52`); the merge queue had rejected the previous head as conflicting after #1258. No merge commit: the 25 branch commits were replayed on the new base. - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1277 pass, 0 fail (adds the search field: typing a term narrows both lists, and a term with no match renders the no-match line instead of the empty state) - Desktop Vite against the live stack at 1440×900 and 1100 px, zh-CN and en: the field renders above the list, filtering matches name and description, the no-match line appears, and the pane has no horizontal overflow. ### After the review round (`308c08e1`) - `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — pass - `apps/desktop` skill suites — 70 pass; background-job store tests — 2 pass - `services/api` skills + import-job tests — 27 pass - full desktop Skill E2E journey — 1 passed (13.0 s) - `pnpm --recursive typecheck` — pass (all workspace packages) - `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — pass - `apps/desktop` unit tests — 1193 pass, 0 fail (includes a two-page repository: the header shows the repository total, 加载更多 reads at the same commit from the returned cursor, the rows already read stay, and loading more does not re-tick a selection the user cleared; the card opens the detail page and lists what the page must show; the chevron menu offers 导出 / 编辑 / 删除 only on a managed row, closes on Escape and on a press outside, exports the returned bytes, deletes through the confirmation dialog, and reports a package still named by a selection instead of deleting it) - `packages/specialist` unit tests — 10 pass, 0 fail. Four drive the real checkout against a `git` on `PATH` that answers like the transport: a broken transfer retries the same clone and never asks for a full repository, a clone that never answers is attempted again before giving up, a checkout that loses its connection is fetched again, a refused filter is the only path to a full clone, and a repository that does not exist is cloned exactly once. - `services/api` Skill suites (`skills.test.ts`, `skills-git-import.test.ts`) — 30 pass, 0 fail (includes the checkout-reuse case, a partial-checkout case that builds a real sparse clone from a local repository and asserts that the resources are fetched on import and that the second scan reports `unchanged`, a 120-package listing, a 520-package repository read as 500 + 20 from one checkout with no gap or overlap, a cursor without its commit rejected, `exportPackage` opening its own archive with the importer's unzip — the files under the Skill's root directory, the same bytes importing back through the upload path, a read-only built-in exporting, and an unknown id refused — and the lifecycle test downloading `/api/skills/:id/package` and checking `application/zip`, the `content-disposition` name, the archive's entries, and a 404 for a Skill that does not exist) - `services/api` targeted suites (`server.test.ts`, `skills.test.ts`) — 138 run, 135 pass. recent_merged.body:
Closes #1254

## What was wrong

`main` carried **`0.4.1`**, a version no release has. The only 0.4.x release is **`v0.4.0-rc1`**, and the planned next one is `v0.4.0` (#1198). The number got there from a one-line edit inside an unrelated MCP fix (`#1197` / `65299d1e`):

```diff
-  "version": "0.4.0",
+  "version": "0.4.1",
```

That field is not a label. It names the Windows installer through `artifactName`, and it becomes the exe's `FileVersion` / `ProductVersion` — the "Apps & features" line a support conversation quotes. So an installer built from `main` advertised a release that does not exist, and nothing in CI noticed, because no workflow reads the field.

The same drift left two other things behind: both README badges said `Release-0.4.0` and linked `releases/tag/v0.4.0`, **which 404s**, and the NSIS syntax-check stub still said `0.4.0`.

## What this changes

**1. `main` goes back to the release line, with one spelling per place it is legal.**

| Place | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `application/package.json` `version` | `0.4.0-rc1` | SemVer — what electron-builder and electron-updater need |
| `application/electron-builder.yml` `artifactName` | `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-win-x64-setup.${ext}` | the dot form is a *file name*; `0.4.0.rc1` is not a valid version (`semver.valid()` is `null`) |
| `README.md`, `README_zh.md` | badge `0.4.0.rc1` → `releases/tag/v0.4.0-rc1` | the tag that actually exists |
| `application/build/nsh-syntax-check-stub.nsi` | `!define VERSION "0.4.0.rc1"` | same as the release branch |

This is the repo's own documented policy, written in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh:59-61`: the dot spelling is not legal SemVer, so `package.json` takes the hyphen form and `artifactName` is pinned to the literal; at GA the version returns to `X.Y.Z` and `artifactName` goes back to `${version}`.

**2. Every payload now records the version it claims.**

`resources/version.json` carried `repoCommit` and `builtAt` but not the version, and `repoCommit` degrades to `"unknown"` when the tree has no git metadata — which is how one build came to report nothing at all. The version is one read of the shell's own `package.json`, the same file electron-builder takes its number from, so the two cannot disagree:

```json
{ "repoCommit": "…", "appVersion": "0.4.0-rc1", "builtAt": "…" }
```

**3. A version bump is now a release change, and CI enforces it.**

New `scripts/check-release-version.mjs`, run inside the **L1 job** (already required, so no new check to wire into `merge-gate`). When `application/package.json`'s `version` moves in a pull request, both must hold:

- the title starts with **`chore(release):`**, and
- **every** place the release is spelled carries the **new** number — the NSIS stub and both READMEs (badge dot form **and** `v<version>` tag link), and the artifact name as the dot-spelled literal for a pre-release or `${version}` for a final release, matching the policy in `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`.

Either alone would be a door: a title is a password anyone can type, and a file set alone lets a functional PR launder a bump by nudging a README line. Together they describe `#1147`, the shape every release is supposed to take. "Carries the new number", not "was touched", is the half that matters in practice: touching `electron-builder.yml` while leaving `ScienceDiscovery-0.4.0.rc1-…` in place is the original defect wearing a release title. The version is also rejected outright if it is not SemVer-shaped, which catches the dot spelling with the form to use instead.

It lives in `.ci/release-version.mjs` and is computed by the **policy job** through `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, because that job is already the diff-aware one — `fetch-depth: 0` and `changed-paths.mjs` are pre-existing — and it is the only place that can read the version the PR moved *from*. Its cases carry the same `category:ut` tags as every other `.ci/*.test.mjs`, so the shared plan collects, selects and counts them. **No workflow file changes at all**: not a step in `ci.yml`, not a job in the graph, not an L1 checkout depth. Only pull requests are checked — a push to `main` and the merge queue re-verify a commit whose PR already answered. `.ci/README.md` describes the rule next to the job that enforces it, including that a violation stops the run before L1.

## Verification

Driven through the policy job's own entry point, with a real `pull_request` payload and a real base commit:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| this PR, release title | **pass** (`rc=0`), policy outputs written |
| the same tree, `fix(mcp):` title | **fail** — the title |
| a bump to `0.5.0` with the metadata left at `0.4.0.rc1` | **fail** — names each file and each missing spelling |
| a `push` event | **pass** — not checked; the pull request already answered |

Unit cases: `.ci/release-version.test.mjs`, **18/18** — the unchanged tree, the release change, the **GA shape** (macro accepted, so #1198 can ship while following the policy), a pre-release that leaves the macro in place (still rejected: the macro cannot spell the dot form), the title-only door, the stale-metadata drift, one file behind being named alone, the dead prefix, the dot spelling, an unreadable file, `dotForm`, SemVer shapes, a guard that every declared requirement is one the checker implements, the policy verdict for a pull request versus a push/merge group, the wiring call, and the checkout read covering every metadata file — which caught a real defect on the way in: the mapping still destructured the old entry objects and crashed on `undefined`.

Other checks on this tree:

- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest, including this PR's cases and the contract test that reads the job graph: **173/173**. `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 6 cases, 20 tags, 4 layers`.
- `scripts/*.test.mjs`: 121 pass, 3 fail — `check-doc-links`, `component-boundaries` and a race-contract case. All three fail **identically at the base commit `a117ae9`** in a worktree without `node_modules`, with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `markdown-it` and `@babel/parser`. They are missing dependencies in this checkout, not regressions; CI installs them.
- Not run here: `pnpm --dir application dist` (needs the full Windows provisioning chain) and `pnpm docs:lint` (needs `markdownlint-cli2`). The README change is one badge URL; the lint config enables only MD001/012/031/040/045, none of which a link edit touches.

## What this does not do

The issue's fourth suggestion — surfacing the build identity in an About window — is **not** included; it is a new UI surface and was left out deliberately. `version.json` is the identity for now, which is what makes "which build is this?" answerable without the version. Suggested as a separate change if it is wanted.

`repoCommit` still falls back to `"unknown"` instead of failing the build: failing would break packaging from a source tarball, and the issue lists that as a decision rather than a defect.

The sidebar draws `新建会话` and `导入会话` as two unrelated rows: the split holds the first, and the second sits below it with the same 18px column gap as everything else. This groups the pair — one container, `flex-direction: column`, `gap: 2px` — so they read as the two session actions they are, at the compact spacing the session rows use.

## Before / after

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-before-sidebar.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-after-sidebar.png) |

Full page, before and after:

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| ![before page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-before-page.png) | ![after page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/130ebdae552a36502caceec2a668aaa4ba348cc7/docs/screenshots/1249/1249-after-page.png) |

Measured in the renderer at both trees (`getBoundingClientRect` on the two buttons):

- **before** — `.side-new-split` is `display:flex; flex-direction: row`, the import button is a sibling of the split and starts 20px below the new-session button's bottom edge (124 → 144).
- **after** — `.side-new-split` is `display:flex; flex-direction: column; row-gap: 2px`, both buttons are children of it, and the gap is 2px (122 → 124).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — **1249 tests, 1249 pass, 0 fail** at this head.
- Diff is two files, `Sidebar.tsx` (the button moves inside the group) and `research-package.css` (the group's direction and gap; the rule that only zeroed the old margin is removed).

The shots come from the desktop renderer under the mock control plane at 1440×940; the sidebar crop is the region a reader compares, and the full pages are there to show nothing else moved. The images live on the `screenshots-1249` branch so they stay out of this diff.
